children.text: vinītaḥ śāstrasampannaḥ kośaśauryasamanvitaḥ
children.translated_text: Disciplined, accomplished in <s>śāstra</s>, and endowed with treasury and valor,

children.text: brahmaṇyo dānaśīlaḥ syāt satyadharmaparo nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a king should be devoted to Brahmins, given to generosity, and intent on truth and <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: stambhopatāpapaiśunyacāpalakrodhavarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: He should be free from arrogance, oppressive conduct, slander, fickleness, and anger,

children.text: pragalbhaḥ saṃnatodagraḥ sambhāṣī priyadarśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: bold, humble yet elevated, ready in conversation, and pleasing to behold.

children.text: vaśyendriyaṃ jitātmānaṃ dhṛtadaṇḍaṃ vikāriṣu
children.translated_text: Royal fortune especially attends one whose senses are submissive, who has conquered himself, and who keeps punishment firm toward offenders,

children.text: parīkṣyakāriṇaṃ dhīram atyantaṃ śrīr niṣevate ||
children.translated_text: who acts after examination and is steady.

children.text: śauryavidyārthabāhulyāt prabhutvāc ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Because of an abundance of valor, learning, and wealth, and especially because of lordship,

children.text: sadā cittaṃ narendrāṇāṃ moham āyāti kāraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: the minds of kings constantly fall into delusion for such causes.

children.text: tasmāc cittaṃ praboddhavyaṃ rājadharme sadā dvijaiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore the king's mind must always be awakened by twice-born men to <s>rājadharma</s> (royal duty),

children.text: pavitraṃ paramaṃ puṇyaṃ smṛtivākyaṃ na laṅghayet ||
children.translated_text: and he should not transgress the supremely pure and meritorious statement of <s>smṛti</s>.

children.text: vedadhvaniprabhāveṇa devāḥ svarganivāsinaḥ
children.translated_text: Through the power of Vedic sound, the gods who dwell in heaven

children.text: te 'pi tatra pramodante tṛptās tu dvijapūjanāt ||
children.translated_text: rejoice there too, satisfied by the honoring of twice-born men.

children.text: tasmād yatnena kartavyā dvijapūjā sadā nṛpaiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore kings should always make every effort to honor twice-born men;

children.text: tena bhūyo 'pi śakratvaṃ narendratvaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by that they obtain <s>Śakra</s>-hood again, and kingship again and again.

children.text: surādhyakṣaś cyutaḥ svargān nṛparūpeṇa tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: The lord of the gods, fallen from heaven, remains in the form of a king;

children.text: kartavyaṃ tena tan nityaṃ yena tattvaṃ samāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: therefore he must always do that by which he may attain true reality.

children.text: ātmīye saṃsthitā dharme nṛpāḥ śakratvam āpnuyuḥ
children.translated_text: Established in their own <s>dharma</s>, kings attain <s>Śakra</s>-hood;

children.text: avīcivāsino ye tu vyapetācāriṇaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: but those who are always separated from proper conduct become dwellers in <s>Avīci</s>.

children.text: gacchet samyagavijñāya vaśaṃ krodhasya yo nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: A king who, without ascertaining properly, falls under the power of anger

children.text: vaset sa narake ghore kalpārdhaṃ tu na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: dwells in a terrible hell for half a kalpa, without doubt.

children.text: etair eva guṇair yuktam amātyaṃ kāryacintakam
children.translated_text: He should appoint as minister, a thinker on affairs, one endowed with these very qualities,

children.text: brāhmaṇaṃ tu prakurvīta nṛpabhaktaṃ kulodvaham ||
children.translated_text: a Brahmin loyal to the king and an ornament of his lineage.

children.text: mantriṇo yatra sabhyāś ca vaidyāś ca priyavādinaḥ
children.translated_text: Where ministers, assessors, and physicians are merely pleasant speakers,

children.text: rājyād dharmāt sukhāt tatra kṣipraṃ hīyeta pārthivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there the ruler quickly falls away from kingdom, <s>dharma</s>, and happiness.

children.text: na tasya vacane kopam eteṣāṃ tu pravartayet
children.translated_text: He should not direct anger against the speech of these men,

children.text: yasmād etaiḥ sadā vācyaṃ nyāyyaṃ supariniṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: because what is just and well settled must always be spoken by them.

children.text: yatra karmāṇi nṛpatiḥ svayaṃ paśyati dharmataḥ
children.translated_text: Where the king himself observes affairs according to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: tatra sādhusamācārā nivaseyuḥ sukhaṃ prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: there subjects of good conduct live happily.

children.text: prajānāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ nityaṃ kaṇṭakānāṃ ca śodhanam
children.translated_text: The constant protection of subjects, the removal of thorns,

children.text: dvijānāṃ pūjanaṃ caiva etadarthaṃ kṛto nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the honoring of twice-born men: for this purpose a king was made.

children.text: bhūsvāmī tu smṛto rājā nānyadravyasya sarvadā
children.translated_text: The king is remembered as owner of the land, not at all of another's property;

children.text: tatphalasya hi ṣaḍbhāgaṃ prāpnuyān nānyathaiva tu ||
children.translated_text: he should receive the sixth part of its produce, and not otherwise.

children.text: bhūtānāṃ tannivāsitvāt svāmitvaṃ tena kīrtitam
children.translated_text: Because beings dwell on it, his ownership is declared on that account;

children.text: tatkriyā baliṣaḍbhāgaṃ śubhāśubhanimittajam ||
children.translated_text: the tax, a sixth part, arises in connection with their acts, whether good or bad.

children.text: evaṃ pravartate yas tu lobhaṃ tyaktvā narādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: The ruler who proceeds in this way, having abandoned greed,

children.text: tasya putrāḥ prajāyante rāṣṭraṃ kośaś ca vardhate ||
children.translated_text: has sons born to him, and his kingdom and treasury increase.

children.text: anyāyena hi yo rāṣṭrāt karaṃ daṇḍaṃ ca pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: But the ruler who unjustly takes from the kingdom tax and fine,

children.text: sasyabhāgaṃ ca śulkaṃ cāpy ādadīta sa pāpabhāk ||
children.translated_text: as well as the share of crops and tolls, becomes a participant in sin.

children.text: arthaśāstroktam utsṛjya dharmaśāstroktam āvrajet ||
children.translated_text: He should set aside what is stated in the <s>Arthaśāstra</s> and resort to what is stated in the <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>.

children.text: duṣṭasyāpi narendrasya tadrāṣṭraṃ na vināśayet
children.translated_text: One should not destroy the realm even of a wicked king,

children.text: na prajānumato yasmād anyāyeṣu pravartate ||
children.translated_text: because, when he proceeds in injustices, the people have not consented to them.

children.text: akleśenārthine yas tu rājā samyaṅ nivedayet
children.translated_text: The king who properly grants to a petitioner without causing hardship

children.text: tat tārayaty anantaṃ syād dharmārthaṃ dānam īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: carries him across; such giving for the sake of <s>dharma</s> and wealth becomes endless in result.

children.text: nyāyenākramya yallabdhaṃ ripuṃ nirjitya pārthivaiḥ
children.translated_text: What is acquired by kings through lawful seizure, after defeating an enemy,

children.text: tac chuddhaṃ tatpradeyaṃ tan nānyathopahṛtaṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: that is pure and may be given; not anything brought by other means.

children.text: rājā purohitaṃ kuryād uditaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: The king should make as his <s>purohita</s> an eminent Brahmin who is beneficial,

children.text: kṛtādhyayanasampannam alubdhaṃ satyavādinam ||
children.translated_text: who has completed his study, is not greedy, and speaks the truth.

children.text: prayatnasādhye vicchinne dharmākhye nyāyavistare
children.translated_text: In the extensive field of justice called <s>dharma</s>, where accomplishment requires effort and has been obstructed,

children.text: sādhyamūlas tu yo vādo vyavahāraḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: a contention whose basis is the matter to be proved is called <s>vyavahāra</s> (legal procedure).

children.text: vi nānārthe 'va saṃdehe haraṇaṃ hāra ucyate
children.translated_text: In differing matters, or where there is doubt, the removal is called a taking away;

children.text: nānāsaṃdehaharaṇād vyavahāra iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: because it removes many doubts, it is remembered as <s>vyavahāra</s>.

children.text: na rājā tu viśitvena dhanalobhena vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: The king, however, should not, from superiority or again from greed for money,

children.text: svayaṃ kāryāṇi kurvīta narāṇām avivādinām ||
children.translated_text: himself create legal matters among people who have no dispute.

children.text: utpādayati yo hiṃsāṃ deyaṃ vā na prayacchati
children.translated_text: One who produces injury, or does not give what is due,

children.text: yācam ānaya dauḥśīlyād ākṛṣyo 'sau nṛpājñayā ||
children.translated_text: because of bad conduct toward a petitioner, is to be brought in by the king's command.

children.text: dvipade sādhyabhedāt tu padāṣṭādaśatāṃ gate
children.translated_text: When the twofold basis, through difference in what is to be proved, has gone into eighteen legal categories,

children.text: aṣṭādaśa kriyābhedād bhinnāny aṣṭasahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: those eighteen, through differences of procedure, are divided into many thousands.

children.text: sādhyavādasya mūlaṃ syād vādinā yan niveditam
children.translated_text: The basis of the provable claim is what has been stated by the plaintiff;

children.text: deyāpradānaṃ hiṃsā cety utthānadvayam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: nonpayment of what is due and injury are called the two grounds of arising.

children.text: pūrvapakṣaś cottaraṃ ca pratyākalitam eva ca
children.translated_text: The plaint, the answer, the rejoinder as calculated in return,

children.text: kriyāpādaś ca tenāyaṃ catuṣpāt samudāhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the procedural section: thus this is declared to have four feet.

children.text: dharmaśāstrārthaśāstre tu skandhadvayam udāhṛtam
children.translated_text: The two branches are declared to be <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> and <s>Arthaśāstra</s>;

children.text: jayaś caivāvasāyaś ca dve phale samudāhṛte ||
children.translated_text: victory and defeat are declared to be the two results.

children.text: śāstreṇa ninditaṃ tv arthamukhyo rājñā pracoditaḥ
children.translated_text: One who, urged by the king, first reports a matter censured by the <s>śāstra</s>,

children.text: āvedayati yaḥ pūrvaṃ stobhakaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: though chiefly concerned with gain, is called a <s>stobhaka</s>.

children.text: nṛpeṇaiva niyukto yaḥ padadoṣam avekṣitum
children.translated_text: One who is appointed by the king to examine faults in a statement,

children.text: nṛpasya sūcayej jñātvā sūcakaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, having learned them, reports them to the king, is called a <s>sūcaka</s>.

children.text: doṣakārī tu kartṛtvaṃ dhanasvāmī svakaṃ dhanam
children.translated_text: Where in a dispute the doer of the fault obtains responsibility,

children.text: vivāde prāpnuyād yatra dharmeṇaiva sa nirṇayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the owner of wealth his own property, that is a decision by <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: smṛtiśāstraṃ tu yat kiṃcit prathitaṃ dharmasādhakaiḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>smṛtiśāstra</s> has been made known by those who establish <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: kāryāṇāṃ nirṇayārthe tu vyavahāraḥ smṛto hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the purpose of deciding cases, that indeed is remembered as <s>vyavahāra</s>.

children.text: yad yad ācaryate yena dharmyaṃ vādharmyam eva vā
children.translated_text: Whatever is practiced by a person, whether righteous or unrighteous,

children.text: deśasyācaraṇān nityaṃ caritraṃ tatprakīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: because it is the regular practice of a region, that is called <s>caritra</s> (custom).

children.text: nyāyaśāstrāvirodhena deśadṛṣṭes tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: So too, in accordance with local observation, without contradiction of the science of justice...

children.text: yaṃ dharmaṃ sthāpayed rājā nyāyyaṃ tadrājaśāsanam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>dharma</s> the king establishes as just, that is the royal ordinance.

children.text: yuktiyuktaṃ tu kāryaṃ syād divyaṃ yatra vivarjitam
children.translated_text: But a case should be supported by reasoning where divine ordeal is excluded;

children.text: dharmas tu vyavahāreṇa bādhyate tatra nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: there <s>dharma</s> is set aside by <s>vyavahāra</s> (legal procedure), and not otherwise.

children.text: pratilomaprasūteṣu tathā durganivāsiṣu
children.translated_text: For those born from reverse unions, and likewise for those living in difficult places,

children.text: viruddhaṃ niyataṃ prāhus taṃ dharmaṃ na vicālayet ||
children.translated_text: they say the contrary rule is fixed; one should not disturb that <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: nirṇayaṃ tu yadā kuryāt tena dharmeṇa pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: But when the ruler makes a decision according to that <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: vyavahāraś caritreṇa tadā tenaiva bādhyate ||
children.translated_text: then <s>vyavahāra</s> is set aside by <s>caritra</s> (custom), by that very rule.

children.text: viruddhaṃ nyāyato yat tu caritraṃ kalpyate nṛpaiḥ
children.translated_text: But whatever custom is established by kings in a way contrary to justice,

children.text: evaṃ tatra nirasyeta caritraṃ tu nṛpājñayā ||
children.translated_text: in that case it should be rejected; custom is subject to the king's command.

children.text: anena vidhinā yuktaṃ bādhakaṃ yad yad uttaram
children.translated_text: According to this rule, each later authority that is overriding is valid;

children.text: anyathābādhanaṃ yatra tatra dharmo vihanyate ||
children.translated_text: where there is overriding in some other way, there <s>dharma</s> is destroyed.

children.text: asvargyā lokanāśāya parānīkabhayāvahā
children.translated_text: A self-made act of kings, when an authoritative statement exists, is not conducive to heaven, destroys the people, and brings fear of hostile armies;

children.text: āyurbījaharī rājñāṃ sati vākye svayaṃkṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: it steals away the life and seed of kings.

children.text: tasmāc chāstrānusāreṇa rājā kāryāṇi sādhayet
children.translated_text: Therefore the king should settle cases according to the <s>śāstra</s>;

children.text: vākyābhāve tu sarveṣāṃ deśadṛṣṭena saṃnayet ||
children.translated_text: but when statements are absent in all the authorities, he should reconcile the matter according to local usage.

children.text: yasya deśasya yo dharmaḥ pravṛttaḥ sārvakālikaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>dharma</s> of a region has been current at all times,

children.text: śrutismṛtyavirodhena deśadṛṣṭaḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: without contradiction of <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, is called local usage.

children.text: deśapattanagoṣṭheṣu puragrāmeṣu vāsinām
children.translated_text: For the inhabitants of regions, market towns, guilds, cities, and villages,

children.text: teṣāṃ svasamayair dharmaśāstrato 'nyeṣu taiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: their <s>dharma</s> rests on their own conventions, together with others, apart from what is fixed by <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>.

children.text: deśasyānumatenaiva vyavasthā yā nirūpitā
children.translated_text: A regulation that has been set forth with the approval of the region

children.text: likhitā tu sadā dhāryā mudritā rājamudrayā ||
children.translated_text: should always be kept in writing, sealed with the royal seal.

children.text: śāstravad yatnato rakṣyā tāṃ nirīkṣya vinirṇayet
children.translated_text: It should be carefully protected like a <s>śāstra</s>; after examining it, one should decide.

children.text: naigamasthais tu yat kāryaṃ likhitaṃ yad vyavasthitam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever matter has been written and established by members of a corporate town or guild,

children.text: tasmāt tat sampravarteta nānyathaiva pravartayet
children.translated_text: from that it should proceed; he should not cause it to proceed in any other way.

children.text: pramāṇadeśadṛṣṭaṃ tu yad evam iti niścitam ||
children.translated_text: What has thus been determined as authoritative and locally observed

children.text: apravṛttaṃ kṛtaṃ yatra śrutismṛtyanumoditam
children.translated_text: and where an unpracticed rule has been made with the approval of <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>,

children.text: nānyathā tat punaḥ kāryaṃ nyāyāpetaṃ vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: that should not afterward be done otherwise; one should avoid what is devoid of justice.

children.text: dharmaśāstravicāreṇa mūlasāravivecanam
children.translated_text: The place where, through consideration of the <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>,

children.text: yatrādhikriyate sthāne dharmādhikaraṇaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: the examination of the legal root and substance is undertaken is indeed the court of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: prātar utthāya nṛpatiḥ śaucaṃ kṛtvā samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: In the morning, after rising, the king should perform purification and become composed;

children.text: guruṃ jyotirvidaṃ vaidyān devān viprān purohitān ||
children.translated_text: then he should honor his teacher, the astrologer, physicians, gods, Brahmins, and priests.

children.text: yathārham etān sampūjya supuṣpābharaṇāmbaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Having honored these according to rank with fine flowers, ornaments, and garments,

children.text: abhivandya ca gurvādīn sumukhāṃ praviśet sabhām ||
children.translated_text: and having saluted the teacher and the others, he should enter the auspicious court.

children.text: vinītaveṣo nṛpatiḥ sabhāṃ gatvā samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: The king, in modest dress, having gone to the court and become composed,

children.text: āsīnaḥ prāṅmukhaḥ sthitvā paśyet kāryāṇi kāryiṇām
children.translated_text: seated and facing east, should examine the cases of litigants,

children.text: saha traividyavṛddhaiś ca mantrajñaiś caiva mantribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with elders versed in the three Vedas and with ministers skilled in counsel.

children.text: saprāḍvivākaḥ sāmātyaḥ sabrāhmaṇapurohitaḥ
children.translated_text: Together with the <s>prāḍvivāka</s>, ministers, Brahmins, and priest,

children.text: sasabhyaḥ prekṣako rājā svarge tiṣṭhati dharmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with assessors, the king as overseer abides in heaven through <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: saha sabhyaiḥ sthirair yuktaiḥ prājñair maulair dvijottamaiḥ
children.translated_text: He should be joined by assessors who are steady, competent, wise, native, and excellent twice-born men,

children.text: dharmaśāstrārthakuśalair arthaśāstraviśāradaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: skilled in the meaning of <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> and expert in <s>Arthaśāstra</s>.

children.text: kulaśīlavayovṛttavittavadbhir amatsaraiḥ
children.translated_text: They should possess good family, conduct, age, practice, and wealth, and be free from envy;

children.text: vaṇigbhiḥ syāt katipayaiḥ kulabhūtair adhiṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: the court should be attended by a few merchants who are established members of good families.

children.text: śrotāro vaṇijas tatra kartavyā nyāyadarśinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Merchants who see justice should be made listeners there.

children.text: sabhāsthāneṣu pūrvāhṇe kāryāṇāṃ nirṇayaṃ nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: In the court places, in the forenoon, the king

children.text: kuryāc chāstrapraṇītena mārgeṇāmitrakarṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the subduer of enemies, should make decisions in cases by the path laid down in the <s>śāstra</s>.

children.text: divasasyāṣṭamaṃ bhāgaṃ muktvā kālatrayaṃ tu yat
children.translated_text: After setting aside the eighth part of the day, the three periods that follow

children.text: sa kālo vyavahārāṇāṃ śāstradṛṣṭaḥ paraḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are remembered as the proper time for legal proceedings, as seen in the <s>śāstra</s>.

children.text: ādyād ahno 'ṣṭabhāgād yad ūrdhvaṃ bhāgatrayaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: After the first eighth part of the day, the three parts above that

children.text: sa kālo vyavahārasya śāstre dṛṣṭo manīṣibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: are the time for <s>vyavahāra</s>, as seen in the <s>śāstra</s> by the wise.

children.text: yadā kuryān na nṛpatiḥ svayaṃ kāryavinirṇayam
children.translated_text: When the king does not himself make the decision in a case,

children.text: tadā tatra niyuñjīta brāhmaṇaṃ śāstrapāragam ||
children.translated_text: then he should appoint there a Brahmin who has mastered the <s>śāstra</s>.

children.text: dakṣaṃ kulīnamadhyastham anudvegakaraṃ sthiram
children.translated_text: He should be capable, well-born, impartial, not causing agitation, and firm,

children.text: paratra bhīruṃ dharmiṣṭham udyuktaṃ krodhavarjitam ||
children.translated_text: fearful of the next world, very righteous, energetic, and free from anger.

children.text: akrūro madhuraḥ snigdhaḥ kṣamāyāto vicakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: He should be non-cruel, gentle, affectionate, endowed with patience, and discerning,

children.text: utsāhavān alubdhaś ca vāde yojyo nṛpeṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: energetic and not greedy; such a man should be appointed by the king in disputes.

children.text: ekaśāstram adhīyāno na vidyāt kāryaniścayam
children.translated_text: One who studies only a single <s>śāstra</s> would not know the determination of a case;

children.text: tasmād bahvāgamaḥ kāryo vivādeṣūttamo nṛpaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore kings should appoint, in disputes, one learned in many traditions as the best.

children.text: brāhmaṇo yatra na syāt tu kṣatriyaṃ tatra yojayet
children.translated_text: Where there is no Brahmin, he should appoint a Kshatriya there,

children.text: vaiśyaṃ vā dharmaśāstrajñaṃ śūdraṃ yatnena varjayet ||
children.translated_text: or a Vaishya who knows <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>; he should carefully avoid a Shudra.

children.text: ato 'nyair yat kṛtaṃ kāryam anyāyena kṛtaṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: Whatever case is conducted by others than these is done unjustly;

children.text: niyuktair api vijñeyaṃ daivād yady api śāstrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: even if they have been appointed, and even if somehow according to the <s>śāstra</s>, it should be understood as such.

children.text: vyavahārāśritaṃ praśnaṃ pṛcchati prāṅ iti sthitiḥ
children.translated_text: The established rule is that he first asks a question connected with legal procedure;

children.text: vivecayati yas tasmin prāḍvivākas tataḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: because he analyzes it in that matter, he is therefore remembered as a <s>prāḍvivāka</s>.

children.text: anirṇīte tu yady arthe sambhāṣeta raho 'rthinā
children.translated_text: But if, while a matter is undecided, he should converse privately with a litigant,

children.text: prāḍvivāko 'tha daṇḍyaḥ syāt sabhyāś caiva viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: then the <s>prāḍvivāka</s> should be fined, and the assessors especially as well.

children.text: alubdhā dhanavantaś ca dharmajñāḥ satyavādinaḥ
children.translated_text: The assessors should be excellent twice-born men who are not greedy, are wealthy, know <s>dharma</s>, and speak the truth,

children.text: sarvaśāstrapravīṇāś ca sabhyāḥ kāryā dvijottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and who are proficient in all <s>śāstras</s>.

children.text: nyāyaśāstram atikramya sabhyair yatra viniścitam
children.translated_text: Where a decision is made by assessors in violation of the science of justice,

children.text: tatra dharmo hy adharmeṇa hato hanti na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there <s>dharma</s>, struck down by <s>adharma</s>, strikes back; there is no doubt.

children.text: yatra dharmo hy adharmeṇa satyaṃ yatrānṛtena ca
children.translated_text: Where <s>dharma</s> is struck down by <s>adharma</s>, and truth by falsehood,

children.text: hanyate prekṣamāṇānāṃ hatās tatra sabhāsadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: while they look on, there the members of the court are themselves struck down.

children.text: adharmataḥ pravṛttaṃ tu nopekṣeran sabhāsadaḥ
children.translated_text: The members of the court should not ignore what has proceeded from <s>adharma</s>;

children.text: upekṣamāṇāḥ sanṛpā narakaṃ yānty adhomukhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: if they ignore it, they, together with the king, go head downward to hell.

children.text: anyāyenāpi taṃ yāntaṃ ye 'nuyānti sabhāsadaḥ
children.translated_text: Those members of the court who follow him even as he goes by an unjust course

children.text: te 'pi tadbhāginas tasmād bodhanīyaḥ sa tair nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: also share in that; therefore the king should be admonished by them.

children.text: nyāyamārgād apetaṃ tu jñātvā cittaṃ mahīpateḥ
children.translated_text: But when he has understood that the king's mind has departed from the path of justice,

children.text: vaktavyaṃ tatpriyaṃ tatra na sabhyaḥ kilbiṣī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: he should speak there what is beneficial to him; a court assessor does not thereby become guilty.

children.text: sabhyenāvaśyavaktavyaṃ dharmārthasahitaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>sabhya</s> (court assessor) must necessarily speak words joined with <s>dharma</s> and practical interest;

children.text: śṛṇoti yadi no rājā syāt tu sabhyas tato 'naghaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if the king does not listen, then the assessor is without fault.

children.text: adharmāya yadā rājā niyuñjīta vivādinām
children.translated_text: When the king would direct the litigants toward <s>adharma</s>,

children.text: vijñāpya nṛpatiṃ sabhyas tadā kāryaṃ nivartayet ||
children.translated_text: the assessor, after informing the ruler, should then stop the proceeding.

children.text: snehād ajñānato vāpi lobhād vā mohato 'pi vā
children.translated_text: From affection, from ignorance, from greed, or also from delusion,

children.text: tatra sabhyo 'nyathāvādī daṇḍyo 'sabhyaḥ smṛto hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: an assessor who speaks otherwise in that case is punishable; for he is remembered as no true assessor.

children.text: kāryasya nirṇayaṃ samyag jñātvā sabhyas tato vadet
children.translated_text: Having properly understood the decision of the case, the assessor should then speak;

children.text: anyathā naiva vaktavyaṃ vaktā dviguṇadaṇḍabhāk ||
children.translated_text: otherwise he should not speak at all, for the speaker incurs a double fine.

children.text: sabhyadoṣāt tu yan naṣṭaṃ deyaṃ sabhyena tat tadā
children.translated_text: What has been lost through the assessor's fault should then be paid by the assessor;

children.text: kāryaṃ tu kāryiṇām eva niścitaṃ na vicālayet ||
children.translated_text: but he should not disturb a case settled by the parties themselves.

children.text: kulāni śreṇayaś caiva gaṇas tv adhikṛto nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Families, guilds, corporate bodies, and the authorized king

children.text: pratiṣṭhā vyavahārāṇāṃ gurvebhyas tūttarottaram ||
children.translated_text: are the bases of legal procedures, each later one weightier than the one before.

children.text: tapasvināṃ tu kāryāṇi traividyair eva kārayet
children.translated_text: He should have the cases of ascetics handled only by men versed in the three Vedas,

children.text: māyāyogavidāṃ caiva na svayaṃ kopakāraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: and likewise those of men skilled in magical practices and yoga, not by himself, since they may cause anger.

children.text: samyagvijñānasampanno nopadeśaṃ prakalpayet
children.translated_text: Even one endowed with correct knowledge should not lay down instruction

children.text: utkṛṣṭajātiśīlānāṃ gurvācāryatapasvinām ||
children.translated_text: for those of excellent birth and conduct, for gurus, teachers, and ascetics.

children.text: gotrasthitis tu yā teṣāṃ kramād āyāti dharmataḥ
children.translated_text: The lineage custom of theirs that comes down in sequence according to <s>dharma</s>

children.text: kuladharmaṃ tu taṃ prāhuḥ pālayet taṃ tathaiva tu ||
children.translated_text: is called the family <s>dharma</s>; he should preserve it just as it is.

children.text: kāle kāryārthinaṃ pṛcchet praṇataṃ purataḥ sthitam
children.translated_text: At the proper time he should question the petitioner, who is bowed down and standing before him:

children.text: kiṃ kāryaṃ kā ca te pīḍā mā bhaiṣīr brūhi mānava ||
children.translated_text: "What is your case, and what is your injury? Do not be afraid; speak, man."

children.text: kena kasmin kadā kasmāt pṛcched evaṃ sabhāgataḥ
children.translated_text: Having entered the court, he should ask, "By whom, in what matter, when, and for what reason?"

children.text: evaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ sa yad brūyāt tat sabhyair brāhmaṇaḥ sahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever the man says when questioned thus, the Brahmin, together with the assessors,

children.text: vimṛśya kāryaṃ nyāyyaṃ ced āhvānārtham ataḥ param
children.translated_text: should examine the case; if it is just, then next, for the purpose of summons,

children.text: mudrāṃ vā nikṣipet tasmin puruṣaṃ vā samādiśet ||
children.translated_text: he should place a seal on it or appoint a man.

children.text: samarpito 'rthinā yo 'nyaḥ paro dharmādhikāriṇi
children.translated_text: Another person presented by the plaintiff before the authority over <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: prativādī sa vijñeyaḥ pratipannaś ca yaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: or one who has himself accepted the matter, is to be known as the <s>prativādī</s> (defendant).

children.text: adhikāro 'bhiyuktasya netarasyāsty asaṃgateḥ
children.translated_text: The competence belongs to the accused man, not to the other, because there is no connection;

children.text: itaro 'py abhiyuktena pratirodhikṛto mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: but the other too, when made an opponent by the accused, is considered a counter-party.

children.text: arthinā saṃniyukto vā pratyarthiprahito 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Whether appointed by the plaintiff or sent by the opposing party,

children.text: yo yasyārthe vivadate tayor jayaparājayau ||
children.translated_text: whoever litigates for another's interest, victory and defeat belong to those two parties.

children.text: dāsāḥ karmakarāḥ śiṣyā niyuktā bāndhavās tathā
children.translated_text: Slaves, laborers, pupils, appointed agents, and relatives likewise,

children.text: vādino na ca daṇḍyāḥ syuḥ yas tv ato 'nyaḥ sa daṇḍabhāk ||
children.translated_text: when acting as litigants, should not be punished; but one other than these incurs a fine.

children.text: brahmahatyāsurāpānasteyagurvaṅganāgame
children.translated_text: In cases of Brahmin-murder, liquor-drinking, theft, and intercourse with the guru's wife,

children.text: anyeṣu cātipāpeṣu prativādī na dīyate ||
children.translated_text: and in other very grave sins, a representative defendant is not to be supplied.

children.text: manuṣyamāraṇe steye paradārābhimarśane
children.translated_text: In killing a human being, theft, touching another's wife,

children.text: abhakṣyabhakṣaṇe caiva kanyāharaṇadūṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: eating forbidden food, and the abduction or defilement of a maiden,

children.text: pāruṣye kūṭakaraṇe nṛpadrohe tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: in verbal abuse, forgery, and treason against the king likewise,

children.text: prativādī na dātavyaḥ kartā tu vivadet svayam ||
children.translated_text: a representative defendant is not to be supplied; the doer himself must litigate.

children.text: dharmotsukān abhyudaye rogiṇo 'tha jaḍān api
children.translated_text: The king should not summon those intent on religious duty, those engaged in an auspicious undertaking, the sick, or the dull-witted,

children.text: asvasthamattonmattārtastriyo nāhvānayen nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor those who are unwell, intoxicated, insane, distressed, or women.

children.text: na hīnapakṣāṃ yuvatiṃ kule jātāṃ prasūtikām
children.translated_text: Nor should he summon an unsupported young woman, a woman born in a good family, a woman recently delivered,

children.text: sarvavarṇottamāṃ kanyāṃ tā jñātiprabhukāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: or a maiden of the highest standing among all classes; such women are remembered as under the authority of their kin.

children.text: tadadhīnakuṭumbinyaḥ svairiṇyo gaṇikāś ca yāḥ
children.translated_text: But women householders dependent on them, independent women, courtesans,

children.text: niṣkulā yāś ca patitās tāsām āhvānam iṣyate ||
children.translated_text: and those who are without family or fallen: their summons is approved.

children.text: saśastro 'nuttarīyo vā muktakeśaḥ sahāsanaḥ
children.translated_text: If a man, armed, without an upper garment, with loose hair, or seated together with another,

children.text: vāmahastena vā vādaṃ vadan daṇḍam avāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: or using his left hand, states a lawsuit, he incurs a fine.

children.text: āhūtas tv avamanyeta yaḥ śakto rājaśāsanam
children.translated_text: If one who has been summoned, though able, disregards the king's command,

children.text: tasya kuryān nṛpo daṇḍaṃ vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: the king should impose a fine on him according to the prescribed procedure.

children.text: hīne karmāṇi pañcāśanmadhyame dviśatāvaraḥ
children.translated_text: In a minor matter the fine is fifty; in a middling matter it has a lower limit of two hundred;

children.text: gurukāryeṣu daṇḍaḥ syān nityaṃ pañcaśatāvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: in serious cases the fine should always have a lower limit of five hundred.

children.text: kalpito yasya yo daṇḍas tv aparādhasya yatnataḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever fine has been carefully fixed for a particular offense,

children.text: paṇānāṃ grahaṇaṃ tu syāt tanmūlyaṃ vātha rājani ||
children.translated_text: there should be taking of <s>paṇa</s>s, or else their equivalent value, for the king.

children.text: utpādayati yo hiṃsāṃ deyaṃ vā na prayacchati
children.translated_text: One who causes injury or does not pay what is due

children.text: yācamānāya dauḥśīlyād ākṛṣyo 'sau nṛpājñayā ||
children.translated_text: to a petitioner, because of bad character, is to be dragged in by the king's command.

children.text: āvedya tu nṛpe kāryam asaṃdigdhe pratiśrute
children.translated_text: After reporting the case to the king, when the undertaking is clear and not doubtful,

children.text: tadāsedhaṃ prayuñjīta yāvad āhvānadarśanam ||
children.translated_text: he should apply that <s>āsedha</s> (legal restraint) until the summoned person appears.

children.text: āsedhayogya āsiddha utkrāman daṇḍam arhati ||
children.translated_text: One fit to be restrained who, once restrained, departs, deserves punishment.

children.text: yas tv indriyanirodhena vyāhārocchvasanādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: But one who, by obstructing the faculties, by speech, breath, and the like,

children.text: āsedhayed anāsedhyaṃ sa daṇḍyo na tv atikramī ||
children.translated_text: restrains a person not fit to be restrained is punishable, not the one who transgressed.

children.text: vṛkṣaparvatam ārūḍhā hastyaśvarathanausthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who have climbed a tree or mountain, or are mounted on an elephant, horse, chariot, or boat,

children.text: viṣamasthāś ca te sarve nāsedhyāḥ kāryasādhakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and all those who are in dangerous positions are not to be restrained by those pursuing a case.

children.text: vyādhyārtā vyasanasthāś ca yajamānās tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Those afflicted by illness, those in distress, and sacrificers likewise,

children.text: anuttīrṇāś ca nāsedhyā mattonmattajaḍās tathā ||
children.translated_text: those who have not crossed over, and those who are intoxicated, insane, or dull-witted, are not to be restrained.

children.text: na karṣako bījakāle senākāle tu sainikaḥ
children.translated_text: A farmer in seed-time is not to be summoned, nor a soldier in time of war;

children.text: pratijñāya prayātaś ca kṛtakālaś ca nāntarā ||
children.translated_text: nor one who has set out after making a promise, nor one whose time has been fixed, in the interval.

children.text: udyuktaḥ karṣakaḥ sasye toyasyāgamane tathā
children.translated_text: A farmer engaged in his crop, and likewise when water has arrived,

children.text: ārambhāt saṃgrahaṃ yāvat tatkālaṃ na vivādayet
children.translated_text: should not be made to litigate at that time, from the beginning until the gathering in of the crop.

children.text: āsedhayaṃs tv anāsedhyaṃ rajñā śāsya iti sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who restrains a person not fit to be restrained is to be punished by the king: such is the established rule.

children.text: abhiyuktaś ca ruddhaś ca tiṣṭheyuś ca nṛpājñayā
children.translated_text: The accused and the restrained should remain under the king's command;

children.text: na tasyānyena kartavyam abhiyuktaṃ vidur budhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise know that another proceeding is not to be undertaken against him as an accused person.

children.text: ekāhadvyāhādyapekṣaṃ deśakālādyapekṣayā
children.translated_text: depending on one day, two days, and so on, according to place, time, and the like...

children.text: dūtāya sādhite kārye tena bhaktaṃ pradāpayet ||
children.translated_text: When the matter has been carried through, he should cause him to give subsistence to the messenger.

children.text: deśakālavayaḥśaktyādyapekṣaṃ bhojanaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: Food is remembered as depending on place, time, age, strength, and the like

children.text: ākārakasya sarvatra iti tattvavido viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: in every case for the <s>ākāraka</s> (summoning officer); so those who know the truth understand.

children.text: na svāmī na ca vai śatruḥ svāminādhikṛtas tathā
children.translated_text: Neither a master, nor indeed an enemy, nor one appointed by a master,

children.text: niruddho daṇḍitaś caiva saṃśayasthāś ca na kvacit ||
children.translated_text: nor one detained, one punished, or persons under suspicion, anywhere,

children.text: naiva rikthī na riktaś ca na caivātyantavāsinaḥ
children.translated_text: nor an heir, nor one without means, nor those dwelling permanently elsewhere,

children.text: rājakāryaniyuktaś ca ye ca pravrajitā narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor one appointed to royal business, nor men who have renounced the world,

children.text: nāśakto dhanine dātuṃ daṇḍaṃ rājñe ca tatsamam
children.translated_text: nor one unable to pay the creditor and the king an equal fine,

children.text: jīvan vāpi pitā yasya tathaivecchāpravartakaḥ
children.translated_text: nor one whose father is still alive, nor likewise one who acts according to his own wish,

children.text: nāvijñāto grahītavyaḥ pratibhūtvakriyāṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: nor an unknown man should be accepted for the undertaking of suretyship.

children.text: atha cet pratibhūr nāsti vādayogyasya vādinaḥ
children.translated_text: But if there is no surety for a plaintiff who is fit to plead,

children.text: sa rakṣito dinasyānte dadyād dūtāya vetanam ||
children.translated_text: he, being kept under guard, should at the end of the day pay wages to the messenger.

children.text: dvijātiḥ pratibhūhīno rakṣyaḥ syād bāhyacāribhiḥ
children.translated_text: A twice-born man without a surety should be guarded by outside warders;

children.text: śūdrādīn pratibhūhīnān bandhayen nigaḍena tu ||
children.translated_text: but <s>śūdra</s>s and the like who have no sureties should be bound with a fetter.

children.text: atikrame 'payāte ca daṇḍayet taṃ paṇāṣṭakam
children.translated_text: If he transgresses or goes away, one should fine him eight <s>paṇa</s>s;

children.text: nityakarmāparodhas tu kāryaḥ sarvavarṇinām ||
children.translated_text: yet confinement should be arranged for members of all <s>varṇa</s>s without obstructing their daily duties.

children.text: grahītagrahaṇo nyāye na pravartyo mahībhṛtā
children.translated_text: In a legal proceeding, one already taken into custody should not be proceeded against by the king;

children.text: tasya vā tat samarpyaṃ syāt sthāpayed vā parasya tat ||
children.translated_text: that person or property should either be handed over to him, or one should place it in another's charge.

children.text: tatrābhiyoktā prāg brūyād abhiyuktas tv anantaram
children.translated_text: There the plaintiff should speak first, and the defendant immediately afterward;

children.text: tayor ante sadasyāstu prāḍvivākas tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: after both of them the assessors, and after that the <s>prāḍvivāka</s> (chief judge).

children.text: yasya syād adhikā pīḍā kāryaṃ vāpy adhikaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: The one whose injury is greater, or whose case is greater,

children.text: pūrvapakṣo bhavet tasya na yaḥ pūrvaṃ nivedayet ||
children.translated_text: his is the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (initial plaint), not that of whoever reports first.

children.text: yasya vārthagatā pīḍā śārīrī vādhikā bhavet
children.translated_text: The one whose injury concerning property, or bodily injury, is greater,

children.text: tasyārthivādo dātavyo na yaḥ pūrvaṃ nivedayet ||
children.translated_text: his plaintiff's statement should be allowed, not that of whoever reports first.

children.text: niveśya kālaṃ varṣaṃ ca māsaṃ pakṣaṃ tithiṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Having entered the time: the year, month, fortnight, and lunar day,

children.text: velāṃ pradeśaṃ viṣayaṃ sthānaṃ jātyākṛtī vayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the hour, region, district, place, caste, appearance, and age,

children.text: sādhyapramāṇaṃ dravyaṃ ca saṃkhyāṃ nāma tathātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: the proof for what is to be established, the property, the number, and also his own name,

children.text: rājñāṃ ca kramaśo nāma nivāsaṃ sādhyanāma ca ||
children.translated_text: and the names of the kings in order, the residence, and the name of what is to be established,

children.text: kramāt pitṝṇāṃ nāmāni pīḍāṃ cāhartṛdāyakau
children.translated_text: the names of the forefathers in sequence, the injury, and both the taker and the giver,

children.text: kṣamāliṅgāni cānyāni pakṣaṃ saṃkīrtya kalpayet ||
children.translated_text: as well as signs of capacity and other details, he should state and formulate the claim.

children.text: deśaś caiva tathā sthānaṃ saṃniveśas tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: The country, and likewise the place, and the arrangement of the settlement,

children.text: jātiḥ saṃjñā nivāsaś ca pramāṇaṃ kṣetranāma ca ||
children.translated_text: caste, designation, residence, measurement, and the name of the field,

children.text: pitṛpaitāmahaṃ caiva pūrvarājānukīrtanam
children.translated_text: the paternal and ancestral connection, and mention of former kings:

children.text: sthāvareṣu vivādeṣu daśaitāni niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: in disputes over immovable property he should enter these ten items.

children.text: rāgādīnāṃ yad ekena kopitaḥ karaṇe vadet
children.translated_text: Whatever, provoked by any one of passion and the rest, he says at the making of the document,

children.text: tad om iti likhet sarvaṃ vādinaḥ phalakādiṣu ||
children.translated_text: all that he should write as exactly affirmed, on the plaintiff's tablets and the like.

children.text: adhikān śodhayed arthān nyūnāṃś ca pratipūrayet
children.translated_text: He should remove excessive points and supply deficient ones;

children.text: bhūmau niveśayet tāvad yāvat pakṣaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should enter it in the basic record until the claim is established.

children.text: pūrvapakṣaṃ svabhāvoktaṃ prāḍvivāko 'bhilekhayet
children.translated_text: The <s>prāḍvivāka</s> should have the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>, as spoken by the party himself, written down;

children.text: pāṇḍulekhena phalake tataḥ patre viśodhitam ||
children.translated_text: first in pale writing on a board, then, when corrected, on a document.

children.text: anyad uktaṃ likhed anyad yo 'rthipratyarthināṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: The man who writes something other than the words spoken by plaintiff and defendant

children.text: cauravacchāsayet taṃ tu dhārmikaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be punished like a thief by the righteous king.

children.text: sollekhanaṃ vā labhate tryahaṃ saptāham eva vā
children.translated_text: Or he may obtain, together with the written memorandum, three days or seven days,

children.text: matir utpadyate yāvad vivāde vaktum icchataḥ ||
children.translated_text: until an intention arises for one who wishes to speak in the dispute.

children.text: yasmāt kāryasamārambhāc cirāt tena viniścayaḥ
children.translated_text: Because, from the commencement of a case, his determination was made long before,

children.text: tasmāt na labhate kālam abhiyuktas tu kālabhāk ||
children.translated_text: therefore that party does not obtain time; the defendant, however, is entitled to time.

children.text: matir notsahate yatra vivāde kāryam icchatoḥ
children.translated_text: Where the mind does not feel able, when both wish to pursue the case,

children.text: dātavyas tatra kālaḥ syād arthipratyarthinor api ||
children.translated_text: there time should be given to both plaintiff and defendant.

children.text: yaś ca rāṣṭraviruddhaś ca yaś ca rājñā vivarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> that is opposed to the realm, or has been rejected by the king,

children.text: anekapadasaṃkīrṇaḥ pūrvapakṣo na sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: or is confused with many points, does not succeed.

children.text: bahupratijñaṃ yat kāryaṃ vyavahāreṣu niścitam
children.translated_text: A case that is settled in legal proceedings as having many allegations

children.text: kāmaṃ tad api gṛhṇīyād rājā tattvabubhutsayā ||
children.translated_text: the king may nevertheless accept, if he wishes, out of desire to know the truth.

children.text: deśakālavihīnaś ca dravyasaṃkhyāvivarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: A claim lacking place and time, and devoid of property and number,

children.text: sādhyapramāṇahīnaś ca pakṣo 'nādeya iṣyate ||
children.translated_text: and lacking proof of what is to be established, is considered unacceptable.

children.text: nyāyasthaṃ necchate kartum anyāyaṃ vā karoty ayam
children.translated_text: If this man does not wish to make the claim stand in justice, or if he commits injustice,

children.text: na lekhayati yat tv evaṃ tasya pakṣo na sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: and does not have it written down in this way, his claim does not succeed.

children.text: aprasiddhaṃ nirābādhaṃ nirarthaṃ niṣprayojanam
children.translated_text: An unrecognized, injuryless, meaningless, or purposeless

children.text: asādhyaṃ vā viruddhaṃ vā pakṣābhāsaṃ vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: or unprovable or contradictory semblance of a claim should be rejected.

children.text: pratijñādoṣanirmuktaṃ sādhyaṃ satkāraṇānvitam
children.translated_text: Those who know claims understand a claim to be free from defects in the proposition, with what is to be proved joined to good reasons,

children.text: niścitaṃ lokasiddhaṃ ca pakṣaṃ pakṣavido viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: certain and established among people.

children.text: svalpākṣaraḥ prabhūtārtho niḥsaṃdigdho nirākulaḥ
children.translated_text: It has few syllables but abundant meaning, is free from doubt and not confused,

children.text: virodhikāraṇair mukto virodhipratiṣedhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: free from contradictory reasons and excluding what is contrary.

children.text: yadā tv evaṃvidhaḥ pakṣaḥ kalpitaḥ pūrvavādinā
children.translated_text: When such a claim has been framed by the first speaker,

children.text: dadyāt tatpakṣasambaddhaṃ prativādī tadottaram ||
children.translated_text: then the defendant should give an answer connected with that claim.

children.text: śrāvyamāṇo 'rthinā yatra yo hy artho na vighātitaḥ
children.translated_text: Where, while it is being heard from the plaintiff, an issue is not contradicted,

children.text: dānakāle 'thavā tūṣṇīṃ sthitaḥ so 'rtho 'numoditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or he remains silent at the time for giving an answer, that issue is approved.

children.text: śrutvā lekhyagataṃ tv arthaṃ pratyarthī kāraṇād yadi
children.translated_text: But if, after hearing the matter contained in the document, the defendant, for a reason,

children.text: kālaṃ vivāde yāceta tasya deyo na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: asks for time in the dispute, it should be given to him, without doubt.

children.text: sadyo vaikāhapañcāhatryahaṃ vā gurulāghavāt
children.translated_text: Immediately, or for one day, five days, or three days, according to the weight or lightness of the case,

children.text: labhetāsau tripakṣaṃ vā saptāhaṃ vā ṛṇādiṣu ||
children.translated_text: he may receive three fortnights, or a week, in matters such as debt.

children.text: kālaṃ śaktiṃ viditvā tu kāryāṇāṃ ca balābalam
children.translated_text: After knowing the time and capacity, and the strength and weakness of the matters,

children.text: alpaṃ vā bahu vā kālaṃ dadyāt pratyarthine prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lord should give the defendant little or much time.

children.text: dinaṃ māsārdhamāsau vā ṛtuḥ saṃvatsaro 'pi vā
children.translated_text: A day, a month, half a month, a season, or even a year:

children.text: kriyāsthityanurūpas tu deyaṃ kālaḥ pareṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: time should be granted according to the state of the proceeding by the superior authority.

children.text: vyapaiti gauravaṃ yatra vināśas tyāga eva vā
children.translated_text: Where the seriousness of the matter slips away, or there is loss or abandonment,

children.text: kālaṃ tatra na kurvīta kāryam ātyayikaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: there he should not cause delay, for that is an urgent matter.

children.text: dhenāv anaḍuhi kṣetre strīṣu prajanane tathā
children.translated_text: In the case of a cow, an ox, a field, and likewise in matters concerning women and procreation,

children.text: nyāse yācitake datte tathaiva krayavikraye ||
children.translated_text: in a deposit, a borrowed article, a gift, and similarly in purchase and sale,

children.text: kanyāyā dūṣaṇe steye kalahe sāhase nidhau
children.translated_text: in the defilement of a maiden, theft, quarrel, violence, treasure-trove,

children.text: upadhau kauṭasākṣye ca sadya eva vivādayet ||
children.translated_text: fraud, and false testimony, he should bring the dispute at once.

children.text: sāhasasteyapāruṣyago'bhiśāpe tathātyaye
children.translated_text: In violence, theft, physical or verbal assault, an accusation concerning cattle, and likewise in an emergency,

children.text: bhūmau vivādayet kṣipram akāle 'pi bṛhaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in a matter concerning land, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> says that one should bring the dispute quickly, even out of the regular time.

children.text: sadyaḥ kṛteṣu kāryeṣu sadya eva vivādayet
children.translated_text: In matters done at once, he should litigate at once;

children.text: kālātīteṣu vā kālaṃ dadyāt pratyarthine prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: but in matters whose time has passed, the ruler should grant time to the defendant.

children.text: sadyaḥ kṛte sadya eva māsātīte dinaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: When the matter has just been done, the hearing is that very day; when a month has passed, it may be one day.

children.text: ṣaḍābdike trirātraṃ syāt saptāhaṃ dvādaśābdike ||
children.translated_text: In a six-year-old matter it should be three nights; in a twelve-year-old matter, a week.

children.text: viṃśatyabde daśāhaṃ tu māsārdhaṃ vā labheta saḥ
children.translated_text: In a twenty-year-old matter he may obtain ten days or half a month;

children.text: māsaṃ triṃśatsamātīte tripakṣaṃ parato bhavet ||
children.translated_text: when thirty years have passed, a month; beyond that, three fortnights.

children.text: kālaṃ saṃvatsarād arvāk svayam eva yathepsitam
children.translated_text: For a period short of a year, he may take time just as he himself wishes;

children.text: saṃvatsaraṃ jaḍonmattamanaske vyādhipīḍite ||
children.translated_text: a year is allowed for one who is dull, insane, mentally disturbed, or afflicted by illness,

children.text: digantaraprapanne vā ajñātārthe ca vastuni
children.translated_text: or for one who has gone to another region, and when the matter is not known,

children.text: mūlaṃ vā sākṣiṇo vātha paradeśe sthitā yadā ||
children.translated_text: or when the original evidence or the witnesses are situated in a foreign country.

children.text: tatra kālo bhavet puṃsām ā svadeśasamāgamāt
children.translated_text: For such men the time should extend until they return to their own country.

children.text: datte 'pi kāle deyaṃ syāt punaḥ kāryasya gauravāt ||
children.translated_text: Even when time has been granted, it should be granted again because of the gravity of the matter.

children.text: pūrvapakṣaśrutārthas tu pratyarthī tadanantaram
children.translated_text: But the defendant, after hearing the substance of the plaintiff's case,

children.text: pūrvapakṣārthasaṃbandhaṃ pratipakṣaṃ nivedayet ||
children.translated_text: should immediately state an answering case connected with the matter of the plaintiff's case.

children.text: ācāradravyadāneṣṭakṛtyopasthānanirṇaye
children.translated_text: When a decision concerns custom, property, gifts, desired rites, duties, or attendance,

children.text: nopasthito yadā kaścic chalaṃ tatra na kārayet ||
children.translated_text: if someone is not present, one should not contrive a pretext there.

children.text: daivarājakṛto doṣas tasmin kāle yadā bhavet
children.translated_text: If, at that time, there is an impediment caused by fate or by the king,

children.text: abādhatyāgamātreṇa na bhavet sa parājitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is not defeated merely by giving up attendance because of an unavoidable obstruction.

children.text: daivarājakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ sākṣibhiḥ pratipādayet
children.translated_text: He should establish by witnesses an impediment caused by fate or by the king.

children.text: jaihmyena vartamānasya daṇḍo dāpyas tu taddhanam ||
children.translated_text: But for one who acts crookedly, the fine should be imposed, namely that sum.

children.text: abhiyukto 'bhiyoktāram abhiyuñjīta karhicit
children.translated_text: The accused may at some point bring an accusation against the accuser,

children.text: anyatra daṇḍapāruṣyasteyasaṃgrahaṇātyayāt ||
children.translated_text: except in an urgent case of physical assault, verbal abuse, theft, or seizure.

children.text: yāvan yasmin samācāraḥ pāraṃparyakramāgataḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever practice in a matter has come down by the order of tradition,

children.text: taṃ pratīkṣya yathānyāyam uttaraṃ dāpayen nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king, having regard to that, should cause an answer to be given according to rule.

children.text: satyaṃ mithyottaraṃ caiva pratyavaskandanaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: A true answer, a false answer, a plea of confession and avoidance,

children.text: pūrvanyāyavidhiś caivam uttaraṃ syāc caturvidham ||
children.translated_text: and the procedure of prior adjudication: thus the answer is fourfold.

children.text: śrutvā bhāṣārtham anyas tu yadā taṃ pratiṣedhati
children.translated_text: When someone, after hearing the meaning of the plaint, denies it,

children.text: arthataḥ śabdato vāpi mithyā tajjñeyam uttaraṃ ||
children.translated_text: whether in substance or even in words, that answer should be known as false.

children.text: abhiyukto 'bhiyogasya yadi kuryāt tu nihnavam
children.translated_text: If the accused makes a denial of the charge,

children.text: mithyā tat tu vijānīyād uttaraṃ vyavahārataḥ ||
children.translated_text: that should be understood, in legal procedure, as a false answer.

children.text: sādhyasya satyavacanaṃ pratipattir udāhṛtā ||
children.translated_text: A truthful statement of what is to be proved is called admission.

children.text: mithyaitan nābhijānāmi tadā tatra na saṃnidhiḥ
children.translated_text: 'This is false,' 'I do not know this,' and 'then there was no presence there,'

children.text: ajātaś cāsmi tatkāla iti mithyā caturvidham ||
children.translated_text: and 'I was not yet born at that time': thus false answer is fourfold.

children.text: yo 'rthinārthaḥ samuddiṣṭaḥ pratyarthī yadi taṃ tathā
children.translated_text: If the defendant, in just that way, accepts the matter stated by the claimant,

children.text: prapadya kāraṇaṃ brūyād ādharyaṃ gurur abravīt ||
children.translated_text: and then states a reason, the teacher said that this is an answer resting on admission.

children.text: ācāreṇāvasanno 'pi punar lekhayate yadi
children.translated_text: If one who has already been overcome by customary procedure causes the case to be written again,

children.text: so 'bhidheyo jitaḥ pūrvaṃ prāṅnyāyas tu sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: he is to be called previously defeated; that is called prior adjudication.

children.text: vibhāvayāmi kulikaiḥ sākṣibhir likhitena vā
children.translated_text: 'I establish it by family arbiters, by witnesses, or by a written document,

children.text: jitaś caiva mayāyaṃ prāk prāṅnyāyastriprakārakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and this man was previously defeated by me': prior adjudication is of three kinds.

children.text: aprasiddhaṃ viruddhaṃ yad atyalpam atibhūri ca
children.translated_text: What is unrecognized, contradictory, too slight, too extensive,

children.text: saṃdigdhāsaṃbhavāvyaktam anyārthaṃ cātidoṣavat ||
children.translated_text: doubtful, impossible, indistinct, directed to another meaning, and very faulty,

children.text: avyāpakaṃ vyastapadaṃ nigūḍhārthaṃ tathākulam
children.translated_text: not comprehensive, with words out of order, hidden in meaning, and also confused,

children.text: vyākhyāgamyam asāraṃ ca nottaraṃ śasyate budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: requiring explanation, and without substance: the wise do not approve such an answer.

children.text: yadvyastapadam avyāpi nigūḍhārthaṃ tathākulam
children.translated_text: What has its words out of order, is not comprehensive, is hidden in meaning, and is confused,

children.text: vyākhyāgamyam asāraṃ ca nottaraṃ svārthasiddhaye ||
children.translated_text: requires explanation, and is without substance, is not an answer for establishing one's own case.

children.text: cihnākārasahasraṃ tu samayaṃ cāvijānatā
children.translated_text: An answer made by one who does not know the many signs, forms, and conventions,

children.text: bhāṣāntareṇa vā proktam aprasiddhaṃ tad uttaram ||
children.translated_text: or stated in another language, is an unrecognized answer.

children.text: pratidattaṃ mayā bālye pratidattaṃ mayā na hi
children.translated_text: 'It was paid back by me in childhood; indeed, it was not paid back by me':

children.text: yad evam āha vijñeyaṃ viruddhaṃ tad ihottaraṃ ||
children.translated_text: when someone speaks in this way, that answer should be known here as contradictory.

children.text: jitaḥ purā mayāyaṃ ca tv arthe 'sminn iti bhāṣitum
children.translated_text: To say, 'This man was defeated by me before in this very matter,'

children.text: purā mayāyam iti yat tad ūnaṃ cottaraṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: but only, 'formerly, by me, this man,' is remembered as an insufficient answer.

children.text: gṛhītam iti vācye tu kāryaṃ tena kṛtaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: When one ought to say, 'It was received,' but says, 'That business was done by me through him,'

children.text: purā gṛhītaṃ yad dravyam iti yac cātibhūri tat ||
children.translated_text: or says, 'the property that was formerly received,' that is an overextended answer.

children.text: deyaṃ mayeti vaktavye mayādeyam itīdṛśam
children.translated_text: When one ought to say, 'It is to be paid by me,' an expression such as 'mayādeyam' is used;

children.text: saṃdigdham uttaraṃ jñeyaṃ vyavahāre budhais tadā ||
children.translated_text: then the wise should know that, in litigation, as a doubtful answer.

children.text: balābalena caitena sāhasaṃ sthāpitaṃ purā
children.translated_text: 'By this assessment of strength and weakness, the act of violence was established before':

children.text: anuktam etan manyante tad anyārtham itīritam ||
children.translated_text: they regard this as not properly stated; it is said to have another meaning.

children.text: asmai dattaṃ mayā sārdhaṃ sahasram iti bhāṣite
children.translated_text: When someone says, 'A thousand and a half were given by me to him,'

children.text: pratidattaṃ tadardhaṃ yat tad ihāvyāpakaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and what was paid back was half of that, that is remembered here as not comprehensive.

children.text: pūrvavādī kriyāṃ yāvat samyaṅ naiva niveśayet
children.translated_text: So long as the original claimant has not properly set forth the procedure,

children.text: mayā gṛhītaṃ pūrvaṃ no tad vyastapadam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: the statement 'it was not formerly received by me' is called one with words out of order.

children.text: tatkiṃ tāmarasaṃ kaścid agṛhītaṃ pradāsyati
children.translated_text: 'What then? Will someone pay a lotus that has not been received?'

children.text: nigūḍhārthaṃ tu tat proktam uttaraṃ vyavahārataḥ ||
children.translated_text: that is declared, in legal procedure, to be an answer hidden in meaning.

children.text: kiṃ tenaiva sadā deyaṃ mayā deyaṃ bhaved iti
children.translated_text: 'Why must it always be paid by that very person? It may be payable by me':

children.text: etad akulam ity uktam uttaraṃ tadvido viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: those who know such answers know that this is called confused.

children.text: kākasya dantā no santi santītyādi yad uttaram
children.translated_text: 'Crows have no teeth,' or 'they do have them,' and the like as an answer:

children.text: asāram iti tattvena samyaṅ nottaram iṣyate ||
children.translated_text: that is not accepted as a proper answer in truth, because it is without substance.

children.text: prastutād alpam avyaktaṃ nyūnādhikam asaṃgatam
children.translated_text: An answer that is too slight for the matter at hand, unclear, deficient or excessive, and irrelevant,

children.text: avyāpyasāraṃ saṃdigdhaṃ pratipakṣaṃ na laṅghayet ||
children.translated_text: that does not cover the essential point or is doubtful, should not overstep the opposing claim.

children.text: saṃdigdham anyatprakṛtād atyalpam atibhūri ca
children.translated_text: What is doubtful, different from the subject, too meager, or too extensive,

children.text: pakṣaikadeśavyāpyeva tat tu naivottaraṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: or reaches only one part of the claim, is not truly an <s>uttara</s> (answer).

children.text: pakṣaikadeśe yat satyam ekadeśe ca kāraṇam
children.translated_text: What is true in one part of the claim and has a reason in one part,

children.text: mithyā caivaikadeśe ca saṅkarāt tad anuttaram ||
children.translated_text: but is false in another part, is no answer, because it is mixed.

children.text: na caikasmin vivāde tu kriyā syād vādinor dvayoḥ
children.translated_text: In a single lawsuit there cannot be one <s>kriyā</s> (proof procedure) for both litigants,

children.text: na cārthasiddhir ubhayor na caikatra kriyādvayam ||
children.translated_text: nor can the success of the case belong to both, nor can there be two procedures in one matter.

children.text: prapadya kāraṇaṃ pūrvam anyadgurutaraṃ yadi
children.translated_text: If, after first adopting one ground, he states another and weightier ground

children.text: prativākyagataṃ brūyāt sādhyate taddhi netarat ||
children.translated_text: contained in the reply, that is what is to be proved, not the other.

children.text: yathārtham uttaraṃ dadyād ayacchantaṃ ca dāpayet
children.translated_text: He should give an answer according to the matter, and should compel one who does not give it to give it,

children.text: sāmabhedādibhir mārgair yāvat so 'rthaḥ samutthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by methods such as conciliation and division, until that matter has been brought out.

children.text: mohād vā yadi vā śāṭhyād yan noktaṃ pūrvavādinā
children.translated_text: What was not stated by the first speaker, whether through confusion or through deceit,

children.text: uttarāntargataṃ cāpi tadgrāhyam ubhayor api ||
children.translated_text: but is nevertheless included within the answer, is to be accepted for both parties.

children.text: upāyaiś codyamānas tu na dadyād uttaraṃ tu yaḥ
children.translated_text: But if someone, though urged by such means, does not give an answer,

children.text: atikrānte saptarātre jito 'sau dātum arhati ||
children.translated_text: when seven nights have passed, he is defeated and is liable to pay.

children.text: śrāvayitvā yathākāryaṃ tyajed anyad vaded asau
children.translated_text: If, after having the case heard as required, he abandons it and states something else,

children.text: anyapakṣāśrayas tena kṛto vādī sa hīyate ||
children.translated_text: then by that he has resorted to another position; that litigant loses.

children.text: na mayābhihitaṃ kāryam abhiyujya paraṃ vadet
children.translated_text: If, after accusing another, he says, 'The case was not stated by me,'

children.text: vibruvaṃś ca bhaved evaṃ hīnaṃ tam api nirdiśet ||
children.translated_text: and contradicts himself in this way, one should declare him too to be defeated.

children.text: lekhayitvā tu yo vākyaṃ hīnaṃ vāpy adhikaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: But if a plaintiff, after having his statement written down, again states something

children.text: vaded vādī sa hīyeta nābhiyogaṃ tu so 'rhati ||
children.translated_text: deficient or excessive, he loses; he is not entitled to bring the charge.

children.text: sabhyāś ca sākṣiṇaś caiva kriyā jñeyā manīṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: The assessors and the witnesses are themselves to be understood by the wise as the <s>kriyā</s> (proof procedure);

children.text: tāṃ kriyāṃ dveṣṭi yo mohāt kriyādveṣī sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: one who, from delusion, objects to that procedure is called a <s>kriyādveṣin</s>, a hater of proof.

children.text: āhvānād anupasthānāt sadya eva prahīyate ||
children.translated_text: If, after a summons, he fails to appear, he is defeated immediately.

children.text: brūhīti yukto 'pi na brūyāt sadyo bandhanam arhati
children.translated_text: If, though directed, 'Speak,' he does not speak, he immediately deserves detention;

children.text: dvitīye 'hani durbuddher vidyāt tasya parājayam ||
children.translated_text: on the second day one should recognize the defeat of that foolish man.

children.text: vyājenaiva tu yatrāsau dīrghakālam abhīpsati
children.translated_text: Where, by a mere pretext, he seeks a long delay,

children.text: sāpadeśaṃ tu tad vidyād vādahānikaraṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: one should know that to be pretextual; it is remembered as causing loss of the lawsuit.

children.text: anyavādī paṇān pañca kriyādveṣī paṇān daśa
children.translated_text: One who pleads another matter is to pay five <s>paṇa</s>s; a hater of proof, ten <s>paṇa</s>s;

children.text: nopasthātā daśa dvau ca ṣoḍaśaiva niruttaraḥ
children.translated_text: one who does not appear, twelve; and one who gives no answer, sixteen;

children.text: āhūtaprapalāyī ca paṇān grāhyas tu viṃśatim ||
children.translated_text: and one who flees after being summoned is to be made to pay twenty <s>paṇa</s>s.

children.text: trir āhūtam anāyāntam āhūtaprapalāyinam
children.translated_text: A person who does not come after being summoned three times, or who flees after summons,

children.text: pañcarātram atikrāntaṃ vinayet taṃ mahīpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king should punish when five nights have passed.

children.text: śrāvitavyavahārāṇām ekaṃ yatra prabhedayet
children.translated_text: Where he causes a split among those whose litigation has been heard,

children.text: vādinaṃ lobhayec caiva hīnaṃ tam iti nirdiśet ||
children.translated_text: or entices a litigant, one should declare him defeated.

children.text: bhayaṃ karoti bhedaṃ vā bhīṣaṇaṃ vā nirodhanam
children.translated_text: If he creates fear, division, intimidation, or obstruction,

children.text: etāni vādinor arthasya vyavahāre sa hīyate ||
children.translated_text: by these acts, in the lawsuit concerning the parties' matter, he loses.

children.text: doṣānurūpaṃ saṃgrāhyaḥ punarvādo na vidyate
children.translated_text: A fine should be collected in proportion to the fault; there is no renewed litigation.

children.text: ubhayor likhite vācye prārabdhe kāryaniścaye
children.translated_text: When the statements of both parties have been written and the determination of the case has begun,

children.text: ayuktaṃ tatra yo brūyāt tasmād arthāt sa hīyate ||
children.translated_text: whoever says something improper there loses that matter.

children.text: sākṣiṇo yas tu nirdiśya kāmato na vivādayet
children.translated_text: But a plaintiff who, after naming witnesses, intentionally does not proceed with the dispute

children.text: sa vādī hīyate tasmāt triṃśadrātrāt pareṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: loses that case after thirty nights have passed.

children.text: palāyanānuttaratvād anyapakṣāśrayeṇa ca
children.translated_text: Because of flight, failure to answer, or resorting to another position,

children.text: hīnasya gṛhyate vādo na svavākyajitasya tu ||
children.translated_text: the plea of a defeated man may be accepted, but not that of one overcome by his own statement.

children.text: yo hīnavākyena jitas tasyoddhāraṃ vidur budhāḥ
children.translated_text: The wise know that there is restoration for one who was defeated through a defective statement;

children.text: svavākyahīno yas tu syāt tasyoddhāro na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: but for one who is deficient through his own statement, there is no restoration.

children.text: āvedya pragṛhītārthāḥ praśamaṃ yānti ye mithaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who, after reporting the case and having the matter taken up, come to a settlement among themselves

children.text: sarve dviguṇadaṇḍyāḥ syuḥ vipralambhān nṛpasya te ||
children.translated_text: should all be fined double, because they have deceived the king.

children.text: kāraṇāt pūrvapakṣo 'pi hy uttaratvaṃ prapadyate
children.translated_text: Because of the ground of action, even the first claim assumes the character of an answer;

children.text: ataḥ kriyā tadā proktā pūrvapakṣaprasādhinī ||
children.translated_text: therefore the proof procedure is then said to establish the first claim.

children.text: śodhite likhite samyag iti nirdoṣa uttare
children.translated_text: When the answer has been examined, written properly, and is thus faultless,

children.text: pratyarthino 'rthino vāpi kriyākaraṇam iṣyate ||
children.translated_text: the making of proof is desired either from the defendant or from the claimant.

children.text: vādinā yad abhipretaṃ svayaṃ sādhayitum sphuṭam
children.translated_text: Whatever the litigant clearly intends to prove by himself,

children.text: tat sādhyaṃ sādhanaṃ yena tat sādhyaṃ sādhyate 'khilam ||
children.translated_text: that is the object to be proved; that by which the whole object is proved is the means of proof.

children.text: likhitaṃ sākṣiṇo bhuktiḥ pramāṇaṃ trividhaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: They know proof to be threefold: document, witnesses, and possession;

children.text: leśoddeśas tu yuktiḥ syād divyānīha viṣādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: circumstantial indication is reasoning, and divine tests here are ordeals such as poison.

children.text: pūrvavāde 'pi likhite yathākṣaram aśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Even when the first pleading has been written exactly, without omission,

children.text: arthī tṛtīyapāde tu kriyayā pratipādayet ||
children.translated_text: the claimant should establish it by proof in the third stage.

children.text: kāryaṃ hi sādhyam ity uktaṃ sādhanaṃ tu kriyocyate
children.translated_text: The case is called the object to be proved, while the means of proof is called <s>kriyā</s>.

children.text: dvibhedā sā punarjñeyā daivikī mānuṣī tathā
children.translated_text: That again is to be known as twofold: divine and human.

children.text: mānuṣī likhyasākṣyādir vadhādir daivikī matā ||
children.translated_text: The human consists of documents, witnesses, and the like; the divine is regarded as ordeals involving deadly tests and the like.

children.text: saṃbhave sākṣiṇāṃ prājño daivikīṃ varjayet kriyāṃ
children.translated_text: When witnesses are available, a wise man should avoid divine proof;

children.text: saṃbhave tu prayuñjāno daivikīṃ hīyate tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: if, when they are available, he employs divine proof, he loses on that account.

children.text: yady eko mānuṣīṃ brūyād anyo brūyāt tu daivikīm
children.translated_text: If one party proposes human proof and another proposes divine proof,

children.text: mānuṣīṃ tatra gṛhṇīyān na tu daivīṃ kriyāṃ nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king should accept the human proof there, not the divine <s>kriyā</s>.

children.text: yady ekadeśavyāptāpi kriyā vidyeta mānuṣī
children.translated_text: If a human proof exists, even though it covers only one part,

children.text: sā grāhyā na tu pūrṇāpi daivikī vadatāṃ nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: that is to be accepted, not a divine proof, even if complete, among disputing men.

children.text: pañcaprakāraṃ daivaṃ syān mānuṣaṃ trividhaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Divine proof is fivefold; human proof is remembered as threefold.

children.text: kriyāṃ balavatīṃ muktvā durbalāṃ yo 'valambate
children.translated_text: One who abandons a strong proof procedure and relies on a weak one,

children.text: sa jaye 'vadhṛte sabhyaiḥ punas tāṃ nāpnuyāt kriyām ||
children.translated_text: after victory has been determined by the assessors, does not obtain that procedure again.

children.text: sārabhūtaṃ padaṃ muktvā asārāṇi bahūny api
children.translated_text: A proof procedure that abandons the essential point

children.text: saṃsādhayet kriyā yā tu tāṃ jahyāt sāravarjitām
children.translated_text: and establishes many inessential things should be rejected as devoid of essence;

children.text: pakṣadvayaṃ sādhayed yā tāṃ jahyād dūrataḥ kriyām ||
children.translated_text: and a proof procedure that establishes both sides should be rejected from far away.

children.text: kriyā na daivikī proktā vidyāmāneṣu sākṣiṣu
children.translated_text: A divine procedure is not prescribed when witnesses are available,

children.text: lekhye ca sati vādeṣu na divyaṃ na ca sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and when a written document exists in lawsuits, neither ordeal nor witnesses are required.

children.text: kālena hīyate lekhyaṃ dūṣitaṃ nyāyatas tathā
children.translated_text: A document loses force through time, and also when it is legally vitiated;

children.text: alekhyasākṣike daivīṃ vyavahāre vinirdiśet
children.translated_text: in a legal proceeding without document or witnesses, he should prescribe the divine procedure.

children.text: daivasādhye pauruṣeyīṃ na lekhyaṃ vā prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: In a matter to be proved by divine means, he should not employ human proof or a document.

children.text: pūgaśreṇigaṇādīnāṃ yā sthitiḥ parikīrtitā
children.translated_text: The established rule that is declared for corporations, guilds, assemblies, and the like,

children.text: tasyās tu sādhanaṃ lekhyaṃ na divyaṃ na ca sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for proving that, the instrument is a document, not ordeal and not witnesses.

children.text: dvāramārgakriyābhogajalavāhādike tathā
children.translated_text: Likewise in matters concerning doorways, paths, legal acts, enjoyment, watercourses, and the like,

children.text: bhuktir eva hi gurvī syān na lekhyaṃ na ca sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: possession itself should have weight, not document and not witnesses.

children.text: dattādatte 'tha bhṛtyānāṃ svāminā nirṇaye sati
children.translated_text: In regard to what was given or not given, and also servants, when there has been a decision by the master,

children.text: vikrayādānasaṃbandhe krītvā dhanam ayacchati ||
children.translated_text: in connection with sale and taking, when someone after buying does not hand over the money,

children.text: dyūte samāhvaye caiva vivāde samupasthite
children.translated_text: and when a dispute has arisen in gambling or a wager,

children.text: sākṣiṇaḥ sādhanaṃ proktaṃ na divyaṃ na ca lekhyakam ||
children.translated_text: witnesses are said to be the proof, not ordeal and not a written document.

children.text: prakrānte sāhase vāde pāruṣye daṇḍavācike
children.translated_text: When a case of violence has begun, or in abusive speech and speech involving punishment,

children.text: balodbhūteṣu kāryeṣu sākṣiṇo divyam eva vā ||
children.translated_text: in matters arising from force, there should be witnesses, or else an ordeal alone.

children.text: gūḍhasāhasikānāṃ tu prāptaṃ divyaiḥ parīkṣaṇam
children.translated_text: For hidden perpetrators of violence, examination by ordeals is appropriate,

children.text: yukticihneṅgitākāravākcakṣuśceṣṭitair nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: and by reasoning, signs, gestures, appearance, speech, eyes, and movements of men.

children.text: uttameṣu ca sarveṣu sāhaseṣu vicārayet
children.translated_text: And in all the gravest acts of violence he should investigate

children.text: sadbhāvaṃ divyadṛṣṭena satsu sākṣiṣu vai bhṛguḥ ||
children.translated_text: the true state by what is seen through ordeal, even when witnesses are present, says <s>Bhṛgu</s>.

children.text: samatvaṃ sākṣiṇāṃ yatra divyais tatrāpi śodhayet
children.translated_text: Where the witnesses are evenly balanced, there too he should test by ordeals;

children.text: prāṇāntikavivādeṣu vidyāmāneṣu sākṣiṣu
children.translated_text: in disputes involving life, even when witnesses are available,

children.text: divyam ālambate vādī na pṛcchet tatra sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if the litigant resorts to an ordeal, he should not question the witnesses there.

children.text: ṛṇe lekhyaṃ sākṣiṇo vā yuktileśādayo 'pi vā
children.translated_text: In a debt case, a document, witnesses, or even slight indications of reasoning and the like,

children.text: daivikī vā kriyā proktā prajānāṃ hitakāmyayā ||
children.translated_text: or a divine procedure is prescribed, out of desire for the welfare of the people.

children.text: codanā pratikālaṃ ca yuktileśas tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Repeated demand, postponement, and likewise a slight indication of reasoning

children.text: tṛtīyaḥ śapathaḥ proktaḥ tair ṛṇaṃ sādhayet kramāt ||
children.translated_text: and, as the third, an oath are prescribed; by these one should prove a debt in sequence.

children.text: abhīkṣṇaṃ codyamāno 'pi pratihanyān na tadvacaḥ
children.translated_text: Even when repeatedly pressed, if he does not refute that statement,

children.text: triścatuḥpañcakṛtvo vā parato 'rthaṃ samācaret ||
