children.translated_text: then after three, four, or five times the matter should be pursued further.

children.text: codanāpratighāte tu yuktileśaiḥ samanviyāt
children.translated_text: But when the demand is resisted, he should connect it with slight evidential reasons,

children.text: deśakālārthasaṃbandhaparimāṇakriyādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: such as place, time, relation to the matter, amount, action, and the like.

children.text: yuktiṣv apy asamarthāsu śapathair eva nirṇayet
children.translated_text: When even the reasonings are insufficient, he should decide solely by oaths,

children.text: arthakālabalāpekṣair agnyambusukṛtādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with fire, water, good works, and the like, according to the amount, time, and strength of the matter.

children.text: yatra syāt sopadhaṃ lekhyaṃ tadrājñaḥ śrāvitaṃ yadi
children.translated_text: Where a document is subject to a condition, if it has been read before the king,

children.text: divyena śodhayet tatra rājā dharmāsanasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there the king, seated on the seat of <s>dharma</s> (justice), should test it by an ordeal.

children.text: vākpāruṣye ca bhūmau ca divyaṃ na parikalpayet ||
children.translated_text: In verbal abuse and in a land matter he should not prescribe an ordeal.

children.text: sthāvareṣu vivādeṣu divyāni paridhārayet
children.translated_text: In disputes over immovable property he should keep ordeals aside;

children.text: sākṣibhir likhitenārthe bhuktyā caiva prasādhayet ||
children.translated_text: he should establish the matter by witnesses, by a written document, and by possession.

children.text: pramāṇair hetunā vāpi divyenaiva tu niścayam
children.translated_text: By proofs, or by an inferential reason, or indeed by ordeal, certainty

children.text: sarveṣv eva vivādeṣu sadā kuryān narādhipaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king should always establish in all disputes.

children.text: likhitaṃ sākṣiṇo bhuktiḥ pramāṇaṃ trividhaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: A written document, witnesses, and possession are remembered as the threefold proof;

children.text: anumānaṃ vidur hetuṃ tarkaṃ caiva manīṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise know inference and also reasoning as the ground.

children.text: pūrvābhāve pareṇaiva nānyathaiva kadācana
children.translated_text: In the absence of the preceding one, only by the following one, and never otherwise,

children.text: pramāṇair vādinirdiṣṭair bhuktyā likhitasākṣibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with the proofs specified by the litigant: possession, written document, and witnesses.

children.text: na kaścid abhiyoktāraṃ divyeṣu viniyojayet
children.translated_text: No one should assign the plaintiff to ordeals;

children.text: abhiyuktāya dātavyaṃ divyaṃ divyaviśāradaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the ordeal is to be given to the accused by those skilled in ordeals.

children.text: mithyoktau sa catuṣpāt syāt pratyavaskandane tathā
children.translated_text: In false pleading it is four-footed, and likewise in counter-pleading;

children.text: prāṅnyāye sa ca vijñeyo dvipāt saṃpratipattiṣu ||
children.translated_text: in prior adjudication and in admissions it should be known as two-footed.

children.text: parājayaś ca dvividhaḥ paroktaḥ svokta eva ca
children.translated_text: Defeat is of two kinds: stated by another and stated by oneself;

children.text: paroktaḥ syād daśavidhaḥ svokta ekavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that stated by another is tenfold, while that stated by oneself is remembered as onefold.

children.text: vivādāntarasaṃkrāntiḥ pūrvottaraviruddhatā
children.translated_text: Shifting into another dispute, contradiction between earlier and later statements,

children.text: dūṣaṇaṃ svakriyotpatteḥ paravākyopapādanam ||
children.translated_text: faulting the origin of one's own action, and establishing the opponent's statement,

children.text: anirdeśaś ca deśasya nirdeśo 'deśakālayoḥ
children.translated_text: failure to specify the place, and specification of improper place and time,

children.text: sākṣiṇām upajāpaś ca vidveṣo vacanasya ca ||
children.translated_text: suborning witnesses, and hostility of speech,

children.text: lekhyaṃ tu dvividhaṃ proktaṃ svahastānyakṛtaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: A document is said to be of two kinds: written by one's own hand and made by another;

children.text: asākṣimatsākṣimac ca siddhir deśasthites tayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: and it may be without witnesses or with witnesses; the validity of those two depends on local established practice.

children.text: grāhakeṇa svahastena likhitaṃ sākṣivarjitam
children.translated_text: Written by the recipient's own hand and devoid of witnesses,

children.text: svahastalekhyaṃ vijñeyaṃ pramāṇaṃ tatsmṛtaṃ budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is to be known as a handwritten document; the wise remember that as proof.

children.text: utpattijātisaṃjñāṃ ca dhanasaṃkhyāṃ ca lekhayet
children.translated_text: He should have origin, caste, name, and the amount of money written down;

children.text: smaraty evaṃ prayuktasya naśyed arthas tv alekhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: thus he remembers what has been transacted, but an unwritten matter would be lost.

children.text: lekhyaṃ tu sākṣimatkāryam aviluptākṣarakramam
children.translated_text: A document should be made with witnesses, with the sequence of letters unobliterated,

children.text: deśācārasthitiyutaṃ samagraṃ sarvavastuṣu ||
children.translated_text: joined with local custom and established rule, complete in all particulars.

children.text: varṇavākyakriyāyuktam asaṃdigdhaṃ sphuṭākṣaram
children.translated_text: It should have proper letters, sentences, and formal acts, be unambiguous, with clear characters,

children.text: ahīnakramacihnaṃ ca lekhyaṃ tat siddhim āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: and not be lacking in sequence or marks; such a document obtains validity.

children.text: cātruvidyapuraśreṇīgaṇapaurādikasthitiḥ
children.translated_text: The established practice of Brahmins learned in the four Vedas, towns, guilds, groups, citizens, and the like,

children.text: tatsiddhyarthaṃ tu yal lekhyaṃ tad bhavet sthitipatrakam ||
children.translated_text: the document for proving that is a <s>sthitipatraka</s> (charter of established practice).

children.text: abhiśāpe samuttīrṇe prāyaścitte kṛte janaiḥ
children.translated_text: When people have passed through an imprecation and performed expiation,

children.text: viśuddhipatrakaṃ jñeyaṃ tebhyaḥ sākṣisamanvitam ||
children.translated_text: a <s>viśuddhipatraka</s> (document of purification), accompanied by witnesses, is to be known for them.

children.text: uttameṣu samasteṣu abhiśāpe samāgate
children.translated_text: When an imprecation has occurred in all the gravest cases,

children.text: vṛttānuvādalekhyaṃ yat taj jñeyaṃ sandhipatrakam ||
children.translated_text: the written record that recounts what happened is to be known as a <s>sandhipatraka</s> (document of settlement).

children.text: sīmāvivāde nirṇīte sīmāpatraṃ vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: When a boundary dispute has been decided, a boundary document is prescribed.

children.text: rājñaḥ svahastasaṃyuktaṃ samudrācihnitaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Bearing the king's own hand and likewise marked with a seal,

children.text: rājakīyaṃ smṛtaṃ lekhyaṃ sarveṣv artheṣu sākṣimat ||
children.translated_text: a royal document is remembered as having witnesses in all matters.

children.text: arthipratyarthivākyāni pratijñā sākṣivāk tathā
children.translated_text: The statements of the plaintiff and defendant, the claim, and likewise the statements of witnesses,

children.text: nirṇayaś ca yathā tasya yathā cāvadhṛtaṃ svayam ||
children.translated_text: and the decision concerning it, just as it has been personally determined,

children.text: etad yathākṣaraṃ lekhye yathāpūrvaṃ niveśayet
children.translated_text: all this should be entered in the document word for word and in the proper previous order.

children.text: abhiyoktṛabhiyuktānāṃ vacanaṃ prāṅ niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: First he should enter the statements of the plaintiff and the defendant.

children.text: sabhyānāṃ prāḍvivākasya kulānāṃ vā tataḥ param
children.translated_text: Then, after that, [he should record the decision] of the assessors, of the chief judge, or of the families;

children.text: niścayaṃ smṛtiśāstrasya mataṃ tatraiva lekhayet ||
children.translated_text: there itself he should write the determination, the opinion of the smṛti-śāstra.

children.text: siddhenārthena saṃyojyo vādī satkārapūrvakam
children.translated_text: Having assigned the claimant to the matter that has been established, with due honor,

children.text: lekhyaṃ svahastasaṃyuktaṃ tasmai dadyāt tu pārthivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king should give him a document furnished with his own signature.

children.text: sabhāsadaś ca ye tatra smṛtiśāstravidaḥ sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: And those court members who are present there and know the smṛti-śāstra

children.text: yathālekhyavidhau tadvat svahastaṃ tatra dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: should likewise be made to place their own signatures there, according to the rule for documents.

children.text: anena vidhinā lekhyaṃ paścātkāraṃ vidur budhāḥ
children.translated_text: The wise know a document made by this procedure as a <s>paścātkāra</s> (post-judgment record).

children.text: nirastā tu kriyā yatra pramāṇenaiva vādinā
children.translated_text: But where the legal action has been set aside by the claimant himself through proof,

children.text: paścātkāro bhavet tatra na sarvāsu vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: there a <s>paścātkāra</s> may occur; it is not prescribed in every case.

children.text: anyavādyādihīnebhya itareṣāṃ pradīyate
children.translated_text: It is given to the others, except those deficient because of another claimant and the like;

children.text: vṛttānuvādasaṃsiddhaṃ tac ca syāj jayapatrakam ||
children.translated_text: and, when established by a narration of what has occurred, that is a <s>jayapatraka</s> (victory document).

children.text: rājājñayā samāhūya yathānyāyaṃ vicārayet
children.translated_text: Having summoned them by royal order, he should examine the matter according to law:

children.text: lekhyācāreṇa likhitaṃ sākṣyācāreṇa sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: what is written by the procedure for documents, and witnesses by the procedure for testimony.

children.text: varṇavākyakriyāyuktam asaṃdigdhaṃ sphuṭākṣaram
children.translated_text: A document that has letters, sentences, and formal acts, that is unambiguous and has clear characters,

children.text: ahīnakramacihnaṃ ca lekhyaṃ tatsiddhim āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: and that lacks no sequence or mark, attains validity for that matter.

children.text: deśācārayutaṃ varṣamāsapakṣādivṛddhimat
children.translated_text: A document joined with local custom and furnished with year, month, fortnight, and the like,

children.text: ṛṇisākṣilekhakānām hastāṅgam lekhyam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and bearing the hand-marks of the debtor, witnesses, and scribe, is called a document.

children.text: sthānabhraṣṭās tv apaṅktisthāḥ saṃdigdhā lakṣaṇacyutāḥ
children.translated_text: But when the letters are displaced, out of line, doubtful, and deprived of their marks,

children.text: yadā tu saṃsthitā varṇāḥ kūṭalekhyaṃ tadā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: then, when they are so arranged, it becomes a forged document.

children.text: deśācāraviruddhaṃ yat saṃdigdhaṃ kramavarjitam
children.translated_text: What is contrary to local custom, doubtful, and devoid of proper sequence,

children.text: kṛtam asvāminā yac ca sādhyahīnaṃ ca duṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and what is made by a non-owner and lacks the matter to be proved, is invalid.

children.text: mattenopādhibhītena tathonmattena pīḍitaiḥ
children.translated_text: A document made by a drunk person, by one frightened through fraud, likewise by an insane person, or by oppressed persons,

children.text: strībhir bālāsvatantraiś ca kṛtaṃ lekhyaṃ na sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: and one made by women, children, or dependent persons, does not become valid.

children.text: khyāpitaṃ ced dvitīye 'hni na kaścid vinivartayet
children.translated_text: If, when it has been publicly announced on the second day, no one sets it aside,

children.text: tathā tat syāt pramāṇaṃ tu mattonmattakṛtād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: then it becomes proof, except for one made by a drunk or insane person.

children.text: sākṣidoṣād bhaved duṣṭaṃ patraṃ vai lekhakasya vā
children.translated_text: A document may be defective because of a fault in the witness or in the scribe,

children.text: dhanikasyopadhādoṣāt tathā dhāraṇikasya vā ||
children.translated_text: and likewise because of a fault of fraud in the creditor or the debtor.

children.text: duṣṭair duṣṭaṃ bhavel lekhyaṃ śuddhaṃ śuddhair vinirdiśet
children.translated_text: A document becomes defective through defective persons; through pure persons one should declare it pure.

children.text: tat patram upadhāduṣṭaiḥ sākṣilekhakakārakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That document is defective when its witnesses, scribe, or makers are tainted by fraud.

children.text: pramāṇasya hi ye doṣā vaktavyās te vivādinā
children.translated_text: The defects that belong to a proof must be stated by the disputant;

children.text: gūḍhās tu prakaṭāḥ sabhyaiḥ kāle śāstrapradarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: but hidden defects are to be made manifest by the assessors at the proper time, by showing the śāstra.

children.text: sākṣilekhakakartāraḥ kūṭatāṃ yānti te yathā
children.translated_text: In whatever way the witnesses, scribe, and makers come to the status of forgers,

children.text: tathā doṣāḥ prayoktavyā duṣṭair lekhyaṃ praduṣyāta ||
children.translated_text: in that way the defects are to be alleged; through defective persons the document becomes corrupted.

children.text: na lekhakena likhitaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ sākṣibhis tathā
children.translated_text: 'It was not written by the scribe, nor was it seen by the witnesses':

children.text: evaṃ pratyarthinokte tu kūṭalekhyaṃ prakīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: when the opponent has spoken in this way, it is called a forged document.

children.text: nātathyena pramāṇaṃ tu doṣeṇaiva tu dūṣayet
children.translated_text: One should impeach a proof not by falsehood, but only by an actual defect.

children.text: mithyābhiyoge daṇḍyaḥ syāt sādhyārthāc cāpi hīyate ||
children.translated_text: In a false accusation he should be fined, and he also loses the matter to be proved.

children.text: evaṃ duṣṭaṃ nṛpasthāne yasmiṃs taddhi vicāryate
children.translated_text: When such a defective document is examined in the king's court,

children.text: vimṛśya brāhmaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ patradoṣān nirūpayet ||
children.translated_text: after considering it together with Brahmins, he should determine the defects of the document.

children.text: yena te kūṭatāṃ yānti sākṣilekhakakārakāḥ
children.translated_text: By whatever [faults] the witnesses, scribe, and makers become forgers,

children.text: tena duṣṭaṃ bhavel lekhyaṃ śuddhaiḥ śuddhiṃ vinirdiśet ||
children.translated_text: by those the document becomes defective; through pure persons one should declare its purity.

children.text: dhanikena svahastena likhitaṃ sākṣivarjitam
children.translated_text: A document written in the creditor's own hand and lacking witnesses

children.text: bhavet kūṭaṃ na cet kartā kṛtaṃ hīti vibhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: would be forged, unless the maker establishes, 'It was indeed made.'

children.text: dattaṃ lekhye svahastaṃ tu ṛṇiko yadi nihnute
children.translated_text: If the debtor denies the signature given in the document as his own,

children.text: patrasthaiḥ sākṣibhir vācyo lekhakasya matena vā ||
children.translated_text: he should be refuted by the witnesses standing in the document or by the opinion of the scribe.

children.text: kṛtākṛtavivādeṣu sākṣibhiḥ patranirṇayaḥ
children.translated_text: In disputes over whether something was made or not made, the document is decided by witnesses.

children.text: dūṣite patrake vādī tadārūḍhāṃs tu nirdiśet ||
children.translated_text: When the document has been impeached, the claimant should point out those recorded on it.

children.text: trividhasyāpi lekhyasya bhrāntiḥ saṃjāyate nṛṇām
children.translated_text: Confusion arises among people regarding all three kinds of document;

children.text: ṛṇisākṣilekhakānāṃ hastoktyā sādhayet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: thereafter one should establish it by the hand-statements of the debtor, witnesses, and scribe.

children.text: atha pañcatvam āpanno lekhakaḥ saha sākṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: But if the scribe, together with the witnesses, has died,

children.text: tatsvahastādibhis teṣāṃ viśudhyet tu na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is certainly to be validated by their signatures and the like; there is no doubt.

children.text: ṛṇisvahastasaṃdehe jīvato vā mṛtasya vā
children.translated_text: When there is doubt about a debtor's signature, whether he is living or dead,

children.text: tatsvahastakṛtair anyaiḥ patrais tallekhyanirṇayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the determination of that document is by other documents made in his own hand.

children.text: samudre 'pi lekhye mṛtāḥ sarve 'pi te sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Even when, in the case of a document, all those recorded there have died,

children.text: likhitaṃ tatpramāṇaṃ tu mṛteṣv api hi teṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: that writing is proof, even when they are dead.

children.text: pratyakṣam anumānena na kadācit prabādhyate
children.translated_text: Direct perception is never overruled by inference.

children.text: tasmāl lekhyasya duṣṭasya vacobhiḥ sākṣiṇāṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the case of a defective document, by the statements of witnesses there should be

children.text: nirṇayaḥ svadhanārthaṃ hi patraṃ dūṣayati svayam
children.translated_text: a decision; for the sake of his own property a man himself impeaches a document.

children.text: likhitaṃ likhitenaiva sākṣimatsākṣibhir haret ||
children.translated_text: One should defeat a writing only by a writing, and a witnessed document by witnesses.

children.text: kūṭoktau sākṣiṇāṃ vākyāl lekhakasya ca patrakam
children.translated_text: When forgery is alleged, the document should be brought to purity by the statements of the witnesses and the scribe;

children.text: nayec chuddhiṃ na yaḥ kūṭaṃ sa dāpyo damam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: the man who alleges as forged what is not forged should be made to pay the highest fine.

children.text: āḍhyasya nikaṭasthasya yac chaktena na yācitam
children.translated_text: A document concerning a wealthy man who is nearby, which was not demanded when demand was possible,

children.text: śuddharṇaśaṅkayā tat tu lekhyaṃ durbalatām iyāt ||
children.translated_text: becomes weak because of suspicion that the debt has been cleared.

children.text: lekhyaṃ triṃśatsamātītam adṛṣṭāśrāvitaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: A document that has passed beyond thirty years and has not been seen or heard of

children.text: na tat siddhim avāpnoti tiṣṭhatsv api hi sākṣiṣu ||
children.translated_text: does not attain validity, even when the witnesses are still alive.

children.text: prayukte śāntalābhe tu likhitaṃ yo na darśayet
children.translated_text: If, when the loan is in use but gain has ceased, a man does not show the writing

children.text: naiva yāceta ṛṇikaṃ na tat siddhim avāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: and does not ask the debtor at all, that does not attain validity.

children.text: paścāt kāranibaddhaṃ yat tad yatnena vicārayet
children.translated_text: What is bound to a later cause should be examined carefully.

children.text: yadi syād yuktiyuktaṃ tu pramāṇaṃ likhitaṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: If it is furnished with sound reasoning, then the written proof is valid.

children.text: anyathā dūrataḥ kāryaṃ punar eva vinirṇayet
children.translated_text: Otherwise, the matter should be set aside at a distance and judged again.

children.text: atathyaṃ tathyabhāvena sthāpitaṃ jñānavibhramāt
children.translated_text: A proof that, through an error of understanding, has been established as true though it is not true

children.text: nivartyaṃ tatpramāṇaṃ syād yatnenāpi kṛtaṃ nṛpaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be set aside, even if it has been made with effort by kings.

children.text: mudrāśuddhaṃ kriyāśuddhaṃ bhuktiśuddhaṃ sacihnakam
children.translated_text: A deed whose seal is valid, whose procedure is valid, whose possession is valid, and which bears identifying marks,

children.text: rājñaḥ svahastasaṃśuddhaṃ śuddhim āyāti śāsanam ||
children.translated_text: being authenticated by the king's own hand, attains validity.

children.text: nirdoṣaṃ prathitaṃ yat tu lekhyaṃ tat siddhim āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: But whatever document is faultless and publicly recognized obtains legal success.

children.text: dṛṣṭe patre sphuṭān doṣān noktavān ṛṇiko yadi
children.translated_text: If a debtor, after seeing the document, has not stated its obvious defects,

children.text: tato viṃśativarṣāṇi sthitaṃ patraṃ sthiraṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: then, after the document has stood for twenty years, it becomes firm.

children.text: śaktasya saṃnidhāv arthe yena lekhyena bhujyate
children.translated_text: When property is possessed by means of a document in the presence of one who is able to challenge it,

children.text: varṣāṇi viṃśatiṃ yāvat tat patraṃ doṣavarjitam ||
children.translated_text: for as long as twenty years, that document is free from defect.

children.text: atha viṃśativarṣāṇi ādhir bhuktaḥ suniścitam
children.translated_text: And if a pledge or mortgage has certainly been enjoyed for twenty years,

children.text: tena lekhyena tatsiddhir lekhyadoṣavivarjitā ||
children.translated_text: its establishment by that document is free from defects in the document.

children.text: sīmāvivāde nirṇīte sīmāpatraṃ vidhīyate
children.translated_text: When a boundary dispute has been decided, a boundary document is to be made;

children.text: tasya doṣāḥ pravaktavyā yāvad varṣāṇi viṃśatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: its defects may be declared for as long as twenty years.

children.text: ādhānasahitaṃ yatra ṛṇaṃ lekhye niveśitam
children.translated_text: Where a debt together with a security has been entered in a document,

children.text: mṛtasākṣi pramāṇaṃ tu svalpabhogeṣu tadviduḥ ||
children.translated_text: they know a document whose witnesses have died to be proof in cases of limited possession.

children.text: prāptaṃ vānena cet kiṃcid dānaṃ cāpy anirūpitam
children.translated_text: If anything has been received by means of it, or if a gift too has not been fully specified,

children.text: vināpi mudrayā lekhyaṃ pramāṇaṃ mṛtasākṣikam ||
children.translated_text: a document whose witnesses are dead is proof even without a seal.

children.text: yadi labdhaṃ bhavet kiṃcit prajñaptir vā kṛtā bhavet
children.translated_text: If anything has been obtained, or if an acknowledgment has been made,

children.text: pramāṇam eva likhitaṃ mṛtā yady api sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the written document is indeed proof, even if the witnesses have died.

children.text: darśitaṃ pratikālaṃ yad grāhitaṃ smāritaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: What has been shown at each proper time, accepted, and likewise recalled,

children.text: lekhyaṃ sidhyati sarvatra mṛteṣv api ca sākṣiṣu ||
children.translated_text: that document is valid everywhere, even when the witnesses have died.

children.text: na divyaiḥ sākṣibhir vāpi hīyate likhitaṃ kvacit
children.translated_text: A written document is never defeated by ordeals or even by witnesses;

children.text: lekhyadharmaḥ sadā śreṣṭho hy ato nānyena hīyate ||
children.translated_text: for the rule of documents is always superior, and therefore it is not defeated by another proof.

children.text: tadyuktapratilekhyena tadviśiṣṭena vā sadā
children.translated_text: By a corresponding counter-document, or by one superior to it,

children.text: lekhyakriyā nirasyeta nirasyānyena na kvacit ||
children.translated_text: the legal force of a document may always be set aside; it is never set aside by anything else.

children.text: darpaṇasthaṃ yathā bimbam asatsad iva dṛśyate
children.translated_text: Just as an image in a mirror, though unreal, appears as if real,

children.text: tathā lekhyasya bimbāni kurvanti kuśalā janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so skilled people make images or copies of a document.

children.text: dravyaṃ gṛhītvā yal lekhyaṃ parasmai sampradīyate
children.translated_text: A document which, after property has been taken, is handed over to another,

children.text: channam anyena cārūḍhaṃ saṃyataṃ cānyaveśmani ||
children.translated_text: or is concealed, written over by another, or kept in another house,

children.text: datte vṛtte 'thavā dravye kvacillikhitapūrvake
children.translated_text: whether in a gift, a completed transaction, or property previously written down somewhere,

children.text: eṣa eva vidhir jñeyo lekhyaśuddhivinirṇaye ||
children.translated_text: this same rule should be known for deciding the validity of the document.

children.text: sthāvare vikrayādhāne lekhyaṃ kūṭaṃ karoti yaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever makes a false document for the sale or mortgage of immovable property,

children.text: sa samyagbhāvitaḥ kāryo jihvāpāṇyaṅghrivarjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when he has been properly convicted, should be made deprived of tongue, hand, and foot.

children.text: malair yad bheditaṃ dagdhaṃ chidritaṃ vītam eva vā
children.translated_text: If a document has been split by stains, burnt, pierced, faded away,

children.text: tad anyat kārayel lekhyaṃ svedenollikhitaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: or likewise rubbed out by sweat, one should have another document made.

children.text: likhitaṃ sākṣiṇo bhuktiḥ pramāṇatrayam iṣyate
children.translated_text: Writing, witnesses, and possession are accepted as the three kinds of proof;

children.text: pramāṇeṣu smṛtā bhukteḥ sallekhasamatā nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: among proofs, possession is remembered for people as equal in force to a written deed.

children.text: rathyānirgamanadvārajalavāhādisaṃśaye
children.translated_text: In uncertainty about a road, an exit, a doorway, a watercourse, and the like,

children.text: bhuktir eva tu gurvī syāt pramāṇeṣv iti niścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: possession itself is weightiest among proofs: this is the settled rule.

children.text: anumānād guruḥ sākṣī sākṣibhyo likhitaṃ guru
children.translated_text: A witness is stronger than inference, and a written document is stronger than witnesses;

children.text: avyāhatā tripuruṣī bhuktir ebhyo garīyasī ||
children.translated_text: uninterrupted possession over three generations is stronger than these.

children.text: nopabhoge balaṃ kāryam āhartrā tatsutena vā
children.translated_text: No force should be assigned to mere use by the first acquirer or by his son,

children.text: paśustrīpuruṣādīnām iti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in the case of cattle, women, men, and the like: this is the established rule of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: bhuktis tu dvividhā proktā sāgamānāgamā tathā
children.translated_text: Possession is said to be twofold: with title and also without title.

children.text: tripuruṣī yā svatantrā sā ced alpā tu sāgamā ||
children.translated_text: That which extends over three generations is independent; but if it is shorter, it must be with title.

children.text: mukhyā paitāmahī bhuktiḥ paitṛkī cāpi saṃmatā
children.translated_text: Possession from the grandfather is principal, and possession from the father also is accepted;

children.text: tribhir etair avicchinnā sthirā ṣaṣṭyābdikī matā ||
children.translated_text: when uninterrupted through these three, possession for sixty years is considered firm.

children.text: sāgamena tu bhuktena samyagbhuktaṃ yadā tu yat
children.translated_text: When something has been properly possessed with title,

children.text: āhartā labhate tat tu nāpahāryaṃ tu tat kvacit ||
children.translated_text: whatever the acquirer obtains in that way is never to be taken away.

children.text: pranaṣṭāgamalekhyena bhogārūḍhena vādinā
children.translated_text: A litigant established in possession whose title-document has been lost

children.text: kālaḥ pramāṇaṃ dānaṃ ca kīrtanīyāni saṃsadi ||
children.translated_text: must state in court the duration, the proof, and the transfer.

children.text: smārtakāle kriyā bhūmeḥ sāgamā bhuktir iṣyate
children.translated_text: Within remembered time, the proof for land is possession with title;

children.text: asmārte 'nugamābhāvāt kramāt tripuruṣāgatā ||
children.translated_text: beyond remembered time, because no title follows, it is possession come down successively through three generations.

children.text: ādau tu kāraṇaṃ madhye bhuktis tu sāgamā
children.translated_text: At the beginning the ground of title is decisive; in the middle, possession together with title is so.

children.text: kāraṇaṃ bhuktir evaikā saṃtatā yā tripauruṣī ||
children.translated_text: The ground of title is possession alone when it has continued through three generations.

children.text: āhartā bhuktiyukto 'pi lekhyadoṣān viśodhayet
children.translated_text: An acquirer, though joined with possession, must clear defects in the document;

children.text: tatsuto bhuktidoṣāṃs tu lekhyadoṣāṃs tu nāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: his son must clear defects in possession, but he does not incur defects in the document.

children.text: yenopāttaṃ hi yad dravyaṃ so 'bhiyuktas tad uddharet
children.translated_text: Whatever property has been acquired by someone, that person, when sued, must substantiate it;

children.text: cirakālopabhoge 'pi bhuktis tasyaiva neṣyate ||
children.translated_text: even with long use, possession is not accepted for that very person alone.

children.text: cirantanam avijñātaṃ bhogaṃ lobhān na cālayet ||
children.translated_text: One should not, out of greed, disturb an ancient possession whose origin is unknown.

children.text: pitrā bhuktaṃ tu yad dravyaṃ bhuktyācāreṇa dharmataḥ
children.translated_text: But property that was possessed by one's father according to the practice of possession and lawfully,

children.text: tasmin prete na vācyo 'sau bhuktyā prāptaṃ hi tasya tat ||
children.translated_text: when that father has died, should not be challenged, for it was obtained by him through possession.

children.text: tribhir eva tu yā bhuktā puruṣair bhūr yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: Land that has been possessed according to rule by three generations

children.text: lekhyābhāve 'pi tāṃ tatra caturthaḥ samavāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: is obtained there by the fourth generation, even in the absence of a document.

children.text: yathā kṣīraṃ janayati dadhi kālād rasānvitam
children.translated_text: Just as milk, with time, produces curd endowed with flavor,

children.text: dānahetus tathā kālād bhogas tripuruṣāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: so, with time, possession descending through three generations becomes a ground equivalent to conveyance.

children.text: bhuktir balavatī śāstre saṃtatā yā cirantanī
children.translated_text: Possession is powerful in the treatise when it is continuous and ancient;

children.text: vicchinnāpi sā jñeyā yā tu pūrvaprasādhitā ||
children.translated_text: even if interrupted, it should be recognized when it has been previously established.

children.text: na bhogaṃ kalpayet strīṣu devarājadhaneṣu ca
children.translated_text: One should not construct title from possession in the case of women, and in the property of gods or the king,

children.text: bālaśrotriyavitte ca mātṛtaḥ pitṛtaḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: nor in the wealth of minors and learned Brahmins, nor in maternal and paternal property in due order.

children.text: brahmacārī caret kaścid avrataṃ ṣaṭtriṃśadābdikam
children.translated_text: A <s>brahmacārin</s> may observe his vow for thirty-six years,

children.text: arthārthī cānyaviṣaye dīrghakālaṃ vasen naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and a man seeking wealth may live for a long time in another region.

children.text: samāvṛtto 'vratī kuryāt svadhanānveṣaṇaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: After returning, one whose vow is completed should then search for his own property;

children.text: pañcāśadābdiko bhogas taddhanasyāpahārakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: possession for fifty years takes away his right to that property.

children.text: pravivedaṃ dvādaśābdaḥ kālo vidyārthināṃ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: For students, a period of twelve years for each Veda is remembered;

children.text: śilpavidyārthināṃ caiva grahaṇāntaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and for students of crafts, the endpoint is declared to be mastery.

children.text: suhṛdbhir bandhubhiś caiṣāṃ yat svaṃ bhuktam apaśyatām
children.translated_text: Whatever property of these persons, while they were not seeing it, has been enjoyed by friends and relatives,

children.text: nṛpāparādhināṃ caiva na tat kālena hīyate ||
children.translated_text: and also of those who have offended against the king, that is not lost through lapse of time.

children.text: sanābhibhir bāndhavaiś ca yad bhuktaṃ svajanais tathā
children.translated_text: What has been enjoyed by agnates, kinsmen, and one's own people likewise,

children.text: bhogāt tatra na siddhiḥ syād bhogam anyatra kalpayet ||
children.translated_text: there is no establishment of title from possession in that case; possession should be reckoned in other cases.

children.text: arthinābhyarthito yas tu vighātaṃ na prayojayet
children.translated_text: But if the other party, when requested by the claimant, does not put forward an objection,

children.text: tricatuḥpañcakṛtvo vā paras tadṛṇī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: even after three, four, or five times, he becomes liable for that debt.

children.text: dānaṃ prajñāpanā bhedaḥ saṃpralobhakriyā ca yā
children.translated_text: Giving, disclosure, division, and the act of enticing,

children.text: cittāpanayanaṃ caiva hetavo hi vibhāvakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also the turning away of the mind, are indeed grounds that make the matter evident.

children.text: eṣām anyatamo yatra vādinā bhāvito bhavet
children.translated_text: Where any one of these has been established by the plaintiff,

children.text: mūlakriyā tu tatra syād bhāvite vādinihnave ||
children.translated_text: there the original <s>kriyā</s> (proof procedure) applies, when the litigant's denial has been proved.

children.text: na kālaharaṇaṃ kāryaṃ rājñā sākṣiprabhāṣaṇe
children.translated_text: The king should not cause delay when witnesses are to speak,

children.text: mahān doṣo bhavet kālād dharmavyāvṛttilakṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for from delay there would be a great fault, marked by the obstruction of justice.

children.text: upasthitān parīkṣeta sākṣiṇo nṛpatiḥ svayam
children.translated_text: The king himself should examine the witnesses who are present;

children.text: sākṣibhir bhāṣitaṃ vākyaṃ sabhyaiḥ saha parīkṣayet ||
children.translated_text: he should examine the statement spoken by the witnesses together with the assessors.

children.text: samyakkriyāparijñāne deyaḥ kālas tu sākṣiṇām
children.translated_text: Time should be given to the witnesses for a proper understanding of the procedure;

children.text: saṃdigdhaṃ yatra sākṣyaṃ syāt sadyaḥ spaṣṭaṃ vivādayet ||
children.translated_text: where testimony is doubtful, he should have it made clear at once.

children.text: sabhāntaḥ sākṣiṇaḥ sarvān arthipratyarthisaṃnidhau
children.translated_text: Inside the court, in the presence of the claimant and the defendant,

children.text: prāḍvivāko niyuñjīta vidhinānena sāntvayan ||
children.translated_text: the <s>prāḍvivāka</s> (presiding judge) should appoint all the witnesses by this rule, reassuring them.

children.text: yad dvayor anayor vettha kārye 'smiṃś ceṣṭitaṃ mithaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever you know of the conduct between these two in this matter,

children.text: tad brūta sarvaṃ satyena yuṣmākaṃ hy atra sākṣitā ||
children.translated_text: speak all that truthfully, for here you have the role of witnesses.

children.text: devabrāhmaṇasānnidhye sākṣyaṃ pṛcched ṛtaṃ dvijān
children.translated_text: In the presence of deities and Brahmins, he should ask twice-born men for truthful testimony,

children.text: udaṅmukhān prāṅmukhān vā pūrvāhṇe vai śuciḥ śucīn ||
children.translated_text: facing north or east, in the forenoon, himself pure and questioning those who are pure.

children.text: āhūya sākṣiṇaḥ pṛcchen niyamya śapathair bhṛśam
children.translated_text: Having summoned the witnesses, he should question them, strictly binding them with oaths,

children.text: samastān viditācārān vijñātārthān pṛthakpṛthak ||
children.translated_text: all of them whose conduct is known and who know the matter, each separately.

children.text: arthipratyarthisāṃnidhyād anubhūtaṃ tu yad bhavet
children.translated_text: But whatever has been experienced in the presence of the claimant and the defendant,

children.text: tad grāhyaṃ sākṣiṇo vākyam anyathā na bṛhaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that statement of a witness is admissible, and not otherwise, according to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: prakhyātakulaśīlāś ca lobhamohavivarjitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who are of renowned family and character, and free from greed and delusion,

children.text: āptāḥ śuddhā viśiṣṭā ye teṣāṃ sākṣyam asaṃśayam ||
children.translated_text: trustworthy, pure, and distinguished, their testimony is beyond doubt.

children.text: vibhāvyo vādinā yādṛk sadṛśair eva bhāvayet
children.translated_text: Whatever kind of matter is to be proved by the litigant, he should prove it only by similar persons;

children.text: notkṛṣṭaś cāvakṛṣṭas tu sākṣibhir bhāvayet sadā ||
children.translated_text: he should always prove it by witnesses who are neither superior nor inferior.

children.text: liṅginaḥ śreṇipūgāś ca vaṇigvrātās tathāpare
children.translated_text: Religious mendicants, guilds, associations, merchant bands, and others likewise,

children.text: samūhasthāś ca ye cānye vargās tān abravīd bhṛguḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whatever other people stand in groups, those <s>Bhṛgu</s> called classes.

children.text: dāsacāraṇamallānāṃ hastyaśvāyudhajīvinām
children.translated_text: For slaves, bards, wrestlers, and those who live by elephants, horses, and weapons,

children.text: pratyekaikaṃ samūhānāṃ nāyakā vargiṇas tathā
children.translated_text: the leaders of each separate group, and likewise the members of the class,

children.text: teṣāṃ vādaḥ svavargeṣu vargiṇas teṣu sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: their lawsuit belongs within their own classes, and members of that class are witnesses in them.

children.text: strīṇāṃ sākṣyaṃ striyaḥ kuryur dvijānāṃ sadṛśā dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Women should give testimony for women, and similar twice-born men for twice-born men;

children.text: śūdrāś ca santaḥ śūdrāṇām antyānām antyayonayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: respectable <s>śūdra</s>s for <s>śūdra</s>s, and lowest-born men for those of lowest birth.

children.text: aśakya āgamo yatra videśaprativāsinām
children.translated_text: Where attendance is impossible for those who live in another region,

children.text: traividyaprahitaṃ tatra lekhyasākṣyaṃ pravādayet ||
children.translated_text: there he should have written testimony, sent through a man versed in the three Vedas, presented.

children.text: abhyantaras tu nikṣepe sākṣyam eko 'pi vācyate
children.translated_text: But in the case of a deposit, even one insider may be called as witness;

children.text: arthinā prahitaḥ sākṣī bhavaty eko 'pi dūtakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a messenger sent by the claimant also becomes a witness, even if he is alone.

children.text: saṃskṛtaṃ yena yat paṇyaṃ tat tenaiva vibhāvayet
children.translated_text: Whatever merchandise has been prepared by someone, he should establish it by that very person;

children.text: eka eva pramāṇaṃ sa vivāde tatra kīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he alone is declared to be the proof in a dispute about it.

children.text: lekhakaḥ prāḍvivākaś ca sabhyāś caivānupūrvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: The scribe, the <s>prāḍvivāka</s> (presiding judge), and the assessors in order,

children.text: nṛpe paśyati yat kāryaṃ sākṣiṇaḥ samudāhṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when the king observes the case, are declared to be witnesses.

children.text: anye punar anirdiṣṭāḥ sākṣiṇaḥ samudāhṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Others again, though not specifically designated, are declared to be witnesses:

children.text: grāmaś ca prāḍvivākaś ca rājā ca vyavahāriṇām ||
children.translated_text: the village community, the <s>prāḍvivāka</s> (presiding judge), and the king for litigants.

children.text: kāryeṣv abhyantaro yaś ca arthinā prahitaś ca yaḥ
children.translated_text: In cases, the insider and the one who has been sent by the claimant,

children.text: kulyāḥ kulavivādeṣu bhaveyus te 'pi sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and kinsmen in family disputes, may also be witnesses.

children.text: rikthabhāgavivāde tu saṃdehe samupasthite
children.translated_text: But in a dispute over shares of inheritance, when doubt has arisen,

children.text: kulyānāṃ vacanaṃ tatra pramāṇaṃ tadviparyaye ||
children.translated_text: the statement of the kinsmen is proof there, unless the contrary is established.

children.text: sākṣiṇāṃ likhitānāṃ tu nirdiṣṭānāṃ ca vādinā
children.translated_text: Of witnesses written down and also specified by the litigant,

children.text: teṣām eko 'nyathāvādī bhedāt sarve na sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if one of them speaks otherwise, then because of the discrepancy none of them are witnesses.

children.text: anyena hi kṛtaḥ sākṣī naivānyastaṃ vivādayet
children.translated_text: For a witness appointed by one person should not be made to testify by another;

children.text: tadabhāve niyukto vā bāndhavo vā vivādayet ||
children.translated_text: in that person's absence, an authorized agent or a kinsman may conduct the case.

children.text: tadvṛttijīvino ye ca tatsevāhitakāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who live by his livelihood and those who act for his service or benefit,

children.text: tadbandhusuhṛdo bhṛtyā āptās te tu na sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his relatives, friends, servants, and trusted dependents, are not witnesses.

children.text: mātṛṣvasṛsutāś caiva sodaryāsutamātulāḥ
children.translated_text: Sons of a maternal aunt, sons of a full sister, and maternal uncles:

children.text: ete sanābhayas tūktāḥ sākṣyaṃ teṣu na yojayet ||
children.translated_text: these are said to be close kin; one should not assign testimony among them.

children.text: kulyāḥ saṃbandhinaś caiva vivāhyo bhaginīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Family members, affinal relatives, one connected by marriage, and the sister's husband,

children.text: pitā bandhuḥ pitṛvyaś ca śvaśuro guravas tathā ||
children.translated_text: the father, a relative, a paternal uncle, a father-in-law, and teachers likewise,

children.text: nagaragrāmadeśeṣu niyuktā ye padeṣu ca
children.translated_text: and those appointed to offices in towns, villages, and districts,

children.text: vallabhāś ca na pṛccheyur bhaktās te rājapūruṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and favorites should not be questioned, for those royal officers are devoted dependents.

children.text: ṛṇādiṣu parīkṣeta sākṣiṇaḥ sthirakarmasu
children.translated_text: In matters such as debts and in settled transactions he should examine witnesses;

children.text: sāhasātyayike caiva parīkṣā kutracit smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: in cases of violence and emergency, examination is prescribed only in some circumstances.

children.text: vyāghāteṣu nṛpājñāyāḥ saṃgrahe sāhaseṣu ca
children.translated_text: In obstructions of the king's command, in forcible seizure, and in acts of violence,

children.text: steyapāruṣyayoś caiva na parīkṣeta sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also in theft and assault, he should not examine witnesses.

children.text: antarveśmani rātrau ca bahirgrāmāc ca yad bhavet
children.translated_text: Whatever occurs inside the house, at night, or outside the village,

children.text: eteṣv evābhiyogaś cen na parīkṣeta sākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if the accusation concerns just these, he should not examine witnesses.

children.text: na sākṣyaṃ sākṣibhir vācyam apṛṣṭair arthinā sadā
children.translated_text: Witnesses should never state testimony when they have not been questioned by the claimant;

children.text: na sākṣyaṃ teṣu vidyeta svayam ātmani yojayet ||
children.translated_text: if testimony is not found among them, one should attach the matter to oneself.

children.text: lekhyārūḍhaś cottaraś ca sākṣī mārgadvayānvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A witness entered in a document and a subsequent witness are furnished with two procedures.

children.text: atha svahastenārūḍhas tiṣṭhaṃś caikaḥ sa eva tu
children.translated_text: Now if a single witness himself is entered there by his own hand and stands present,

children.text: na cet pratyabhijānīyāt tatsvahastaiḥ prasādhayet ||
children.translated_text: but does not recognize it, one should establish it by his own handwriting.

children.text: arthinā svayam ānīto yo lekhye saṃniveśyate
children.translated_text: The witness whom the claimant himself has brought and who is entered in the document

children.text: sa sākṣī likhito nāma smāritaḥ patrakād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: is called a written witness; apart from a document, he is a remembered witness.

children.text: yas tu kāryaprasiddhyarthaṃ dṛṣṭvā kāryaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: But the witness who, for the sake of establishing the case, has seen the matter again and again

children.text: smāryate hy arthinā sākṣī sa smārita ihocyate ||
children.translated_text: and is then reminded by the claimant is here called a remembered witness.

children.text: prayojanārtham ānītaḥ prasaṅgād āgataś ca yaḥ
children.translated_text: One who is brought for a particular purpose, and one who has come incidentally,

children.text: dvau sākṣiṇau tv alikhitau pūrvapakṣasya sādhakau ||
children.translated_text: are two unwritten witnesses who establish the plaintiff's claim.

children.text: arthinā svārthasiddhyarthaṃ pratyarthivacanaṃ sphuṭam
children.translated_text: He whom the claimant, for the sake of proving his own interest, has made clearly hear the defendant's statement

children.text: yaḥ śrāvitaḥ sthito gūḍho gūḍhasākṣī sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: while he stood hidden, is called a hidden witness.

children.text: sākṣiṇām api yaḥ sākṣyam uparyupari bhāṣate
children.translated_text: One who gives testimony over and above the witnesses' own testimony,

children.text: śravaṇāc chrāvaṇād vāpi sa sākṣyuttarasaṃjñitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether from hearing it himself or from being made to hear it, is designated a supplementary witness.

children.text: ullapyaṃ yasya viśrambhāt kāryaṃ vā viniveditam
children.translated_text: One to whom, through trust, something to be spoken has been disclosed, or a case has been reported,

children.text: gūḍhacārī sa vijñeyaḥ kāryamadhyagatas tathā ||
children.translated_text: is to be known as a hidden observer, and likewise one who has been present in the midst of the case.

children.text: arthī yatra vipannaḥ syāt tatra sākṣī mṛtāntaraḥ
children.translated_text: Where the claimant has died, there the witness is one after a death;

children.text: pratyarthī ca mṛto yatra tatrāpy evaṃ prakalpyate ||
children.translated_text: and where the defendant has died, the same rule is also to be applied.

children.text: lekhyadoṣās tu ye kecit sākṣiṇāṃ caiva ye smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever defects there may be in documents, and whatever defects of witnesses are remembered,

children.text: vādakāle tu vaktavyāḥ paścād uktān na dūṣayet ||
children.translated_text: they must be stated at the time of litigation; objections stated afterward do not vitiate them.

children.text: ukter arthe sākṣiṇo yas tu dūṣayet prāgdūṣitān
children.translated_text: But whoever, once the matter has been stated, assails witnesses not objected to before,

children.text: na ca tatkāraṇaṃ brūyāt prāpnuyāt pūrvasāhasam ||
children.translated_text: and does not state the reason for that, incurs the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine.

children.text: nātathyena pramāṇaṃ tu doṣeṇaiva tu dūṣayet
children.translated_text: One should not impugn a proof by falsehood, but only by a genuine defect;

children.text: mithyābhiyoge daṇḍyaḥ syāt sādhyārthāc cāpi hīyate ||
children.translated_text: on a false accusation one should be punished, and one also loses the object to be proved.

children.text: pratyarthinārthinā vāpi sākṣidūṣaṇasādhane
children.translated_text: When the defendant or the claimant proves a defect in witnesses,

children.text: prastutārthopayogitvād vyavahārāntaraṃ na ca ||
children.translated_text: because it is useful to the matter at hand, it is not a separate lawsuit.

children.text: sākṣidoṣāḥ pravaktavyāḥ saṃsadi prativādinā
children.translated_text: Defects of witnesses must be declared by the defendant in the assembly;

children.text: patre vilikhya tān sarvān vācyaḥ pratyuttaraṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: after writing all of them in a document, he should then state his reply.

children.text: pratipattau tu sākṣitvam arhanti na kadācana
children.translated_text: When there is admission, they never qualify as witnesses;

children.text: ato 'nyathā bhāvanīyāḥ kriyayā prativādinā ||
children.translated_text: otherwise, therefore, the defendant must establish the defects by a <s>kriyā</s> (proof procedure).

children.text: abhāvayan dhanam dāpyaḥ pratyarthī sākṣiṇaḥ sphuṭam
children.translated_text: If he fails to establish them, the defendant is plainly to be made to pay the money, and the witnesses stand clear;

children.text: bhāvitāḥ sākṣiṇaḥ sarve sākṣidharmanirākṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: if they are proved defective, all the witnesses are excluded from the rule governing witnesses.

children.text: ākāro 'ṅgitaceṣṭābhis tasya bhāvaṃ vibhāvayet
children.translated_text: By appearance, gestures, and movements one should discern his disposition;

children.text: prativādī bhaveddhīnaḥ so 'numānena lakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: the defendant may become deficient, and he is recognized by inference.

children.text: kampaḥ svedo 'tha vaikalyam oṣṭhaśoṣābhimarśane
children.translated_text: Trembling, sweating, incapacity, and touching parched lips,

children.text: bhūlekhanaṃ sthānahānis tiryagūrdhvanirīkṣaṇam
children.translated_text: scratching on the ground, loss of place, and looking sideways and upward,

children.text: svarabhedaś ca duṣṭasya cihnāny āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and a change of voice are said by the wise to be signs of a tainted person.

children.text: sabhāntaḥsthais tu vaktavyaṃ sākṣyaṃ nānyatra sākṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Witnesses must give testimony while standing inside the court, not elsewhere;

children.text: sarvasākṣyeṣv ayaṃ dharmo hy anyatra sthāvareṣu tu ||
children.translated_text: this rule applies to all testimony, except in matters concerning immovable property.

children.text: arthipratyarthisāṃnidhye sādhyārthasya ca saṃnidhau
children.translated_text: In the presence of the claimant and defendant, and in the presence of the object to be proved,

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ deśayet sākṣyaṃ parokṣaṃ na kathaṃcana ||
children.translated_text: one should present direct testimony, never indirect testimony in any way.

children.text: arthasyopari vaktavyaṃ tayor api vinā kvacit
children.translated_text: The statement should be made over the object itself, sometimes even without those two parties;

children.text: catuṣpadeṣv ayaṃ dharmo dvipadasthāvareṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: this rule applies to quadrupeds, bipeds, and immovable property.

children.text: taulyagaṇimameyānām abhāve 'pi vivādayet
children.translated_text: Even in the absence of goods to be weighed, counted, or measured, one may conduct the dispute;

children.text: kriyākāreṣu sarveṣu sākṣitvaṃ na tato 'nyathā ||
children.translated_text: in all formal undertakings, witnesshood applies, and not otherwise than from that.

children.text: vadhe cet prāṇināṃ sākṣyaṃ vādayecchivasaṃnidhau
children.translated_text: If the testimony concerns the killing of living beings, one should have it given in the presence of the body;

children.text: tadabhāve tu cihnasya nānyathaiva pravādayet ||
children.translated_text: but in its absence, at the mark of it; one should not have testimony given otherwise.

children.text: svabhāvoktaṃ vacas teṣāṃ grāhyaṃ yad doṣavarjitam
children.translated_text: The statement they naturally utter, if free from defect, is to be accepted;

children.text: ukte tu sākṣiṇo rājñā na praṣṭavyāḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: once the witnesses have spoken before the king, they should not be questioned again and again.

children.text: svabhāvenaiva yad brūyus tad grāhyaṃ vyāvahārikam
children.translated_text: What they say naturally is to be accepted as valid for legal proceedings;

children.text: ato yad anyad vibrūyur dharmārthaṃ tad apārthakam ||
children.translated_text: anything else they say, even for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, is without purpose.

children.text: samavetais tu yad dṛṣṭaṃ vaktavyaṃ tat tathaiva tu
children.translated_text: What they have seen together must be stated exactly as it was;

children.text: vibhinnaikaikakāryaṃ yad vaktavyaṃ tat pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: but a different matter belonging to each one separately must be stated separately.

children.text: bhinnakāle tu yat kāryaṃ vijñātaṃ tatra sākṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Where a matter has been known by witnesses at different times,

children.text: ekaikaṃ vādayet tatra bhinnakālaṃ tu tad bhṛguḥ ||
children.translated_text: there one should have each speak individually; <s>Bhṛgu</s> says that such a matter is divided by time.

children.text: ṛṇādiṣu vivādeṣu sthiraprāyeṣu niścitam
children.translated_text: In disputes such as debts, which are generally fixed and certain,

children.text: ūne vāpy adhike vārthe prokte sādhyaṃ na sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: if the matter is stated as less or as more, the object to be proved is not established.

children.text: sādhyārthāṃśe 'pi gadite sākṣibhiḥ sakalaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Even when only a part of the matter to be proved is stated by the witnesses, it becomes complete

children.text: strīsaṅge sāhase caurye yat sādhyaṃ parikalpitam ||
children.translated_text: in the alleged matter of intercourse with a woman, violent assault, or theft.

children.text: ūnādhikaṃ tu yatra syāt tat sākṣyaṃ tatra varjayet
children.translated_text: But wherever testimony is deficient or excessive, that testimony should be rejected there;

children.text: sākṣī tatra na daṇḍyaḥ syād abruvan daṇḍam arhati ||
children.translated_text: the witness there should not be punished, but one who says nothing deserves punishment.

children.text: deśaṃ kālaṃ dhanaṃ saṃkhyāṃ rūpaṃ jātyākṛtī vayaḥ
children.translated_text: Place, time, money, number, form, class, shape, and age:

children.text: visaṃvaded yatra sākṣye tad anuktaṃ vidur budhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: where testimony contradicts these, the wise know it as not having been stated.

children.text: nirdiṣṭeṣv arthajāteṣu sākṣī cet sākṣya āgate
children.translated_text: When kinds of matters have been specified and a witness has come to testify,

children.text: na brūyād akṣarasamaṃ na tan nigaditaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: if he does not speak exactly, syllable for syllable, that is not considered declared.

children.text: ūnam abhyadhikaṃ vārthaṃ vibrūyur yatra sākṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Where witnesses state the matter as deficient or excessive,

children.text: tad apy ayuktaṃ vijñeyam eṣa sākṣiviniścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that too should be known as improper; this is the determination concerning witnesses.

children.text: apṛṣṭaḥ sarvavacane pṛṣṭasyākathane tathā
children.translated_text: For saying everything when not questioned, and likewise for not telling when questioned,

children.text: sākṣiṇaḥ saṃniroddhavyā garhyā daṇḍyāś ca dharmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: witnesses are to be restrained; by law they are blameworthy and punishable.

children.text: vākpāruṣye chale vāde dāpyāḥ syus triśataṃ damam
children.translated_text: In cases of verbal abuse or fraudulent argument, they should be made to pay a fine of three hundred;

children.text: ṛṇādivādeṣu dhanaṃ te syur dāpyā ṛṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: in disputes such as debts, they should be made to pay the money, and likewise the debt.

children.text: yaḥ sākṣī naiva nirdiṣṭā nāhūto nāpi darśitaḥ
children.translated_text: A witness who was not designated, not summoned, and not presented,

children.text: brūyān mithyeti tathyaṃ vā daṇḍyaḥ so 'pi narādhamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet says, 'This is false,' or, 'This is true,' is punishable too, that lowest of men.

children.text: sākṣī sākṣyaṃ na ced brūyāt samadaṇḍaṃ vahed ṛṇam
children.translated_text: If a witness does not give his testimony, he should bear the debt together with an equal fine;

children.text: ato 'nyeṣu vivādeṣu triśataṃ daṇḍam arhati ||
children.translated_text: in other disputes than this, he deserves a fine of three hundred.

children.text: uktvānyathā bruvāṇāś ca daṇḍyāḥ syur vākchalānvitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who, after having spoken, speak otherwise, and those engaged in verbal trickery, should be punished.

children.text: yena kāryasya lobhena nirdiṣṭāḥ kūṭasākṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The man by whom false witnesses have been appointed out of greed for a lawsuit

children.text: gṛhītvā tasya sarvasvaṃ kuryān nirviṣayaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: should have all his property seized, and thereafter he should be made an exile.

children.text: yatra vai bhāvitaṃ kāryaṃ sākṣibhir vādinā bhavet
children.translated_text: When a case has been established by witnesses on behalf of the plaintiff,

children.text: prativādī yadā tatra bhāvayet kāryam anyathā
children.translated_text: and the defendant then establishes the matter otherwise there,

children.text: bahubhiś ca kulīnair vā pūrvāḥ syuḥ kūṭasākṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the earlier witnesses, even if numerous or of good family, are false witnesses.

children.text: yadā śuddhā kriyā nyāyāt tadā tadvākyaśodhanam
children.translated_text: When the procedure is pure according to law, then there is purification of that statement.

children.text: śuddhāc ca vākyād yaḥ śuddhaḥ sa śuddho 'rtha iti sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And one who is cleared by a pure statement is cleared in the matter; such is the settled rule.

children.text: saptāhāt tu pratīyeta yatra sākṣy anṛtaṃ vadet
children.translated_text: Where a witness speaks falsely, it may become evident after a week:

children.text: rogo 'gnir jñātimaraṇaṃ dvisaptāhāt trisapta vā
children.translated_text: disease, fire, or the death of a kinsman may occur after two weeks, three weeks,

children.text: ṣaṭcatvāriṃśake vāpi dravyajātyādibhedataḥ ||
children.translated_text: or even on the forty-sixth day, according to differences of property, class, and the like.

children.text: na kaścid abhiyoktāraṃ divyeṣu viniyojayet
children.translated_text: No one should subject the accuser to ordeals.

children.text: abhiyuktāya dātavyaṃ divyaṃ divyaviśāradaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>divya</s> (ordeal) is to be given to the accused by experts in ordeals.

children.text: pārthivaiḥ śaṅkitānāṃ tu tulādīni niyojayet
children.translated_text: For those under suspicion, kings should prescribe the balance and similar ordeals.

children.text: ātmaśuddhividhāne ca na śiras tatra kalpayet ||
children.translated_text: And in the rite for establishing personal purity, one should not prescribe the head-ordeal there.

children.text: lokāpavādaduṣṭānāṃ śaṅkitānāṃ ca dasyubhiḥ
children.translated_text: For those tainted by public reproach and suspected as robbers,

children.text: tulādīni niyojyāni na śiras tatra vai bhṛguḥ ||
children.translated_text: the balance and similar ordeals are to be prescribed, not the head-ordeal there, says <s>Bhṛgu</s>.

children.text: na śaṅkāsu śiraḥ kośe kalpayet tu kadācana
children.translated_text: In cases of suspicion, and in the <s>kośa</s> ordeal, one should never prescribe the head-ordeal.

children.text: aśirāṃsi ca divyāni rājabhṛtyeṣu dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: And headless ordeals should be administered to royal servants.

children.text: śaṅkāviśvāsasaṃdhāne vibhāge rikthināṃ sadā
children.translated_text: In reconciling suspicion and trust, in the division of heirs' property,

children.text: kriyāsamūhakartṛtve kośam eva pradāpayet ||
children.translated_text: and whenever joint agency in an act is at issue, one should administer only the <s>kośa</s>.

children.text: dattasyāpahnavo yatra pramāṇaṃ tatra kalpayet
children.translated_text: Where there is denial of something given, one should arrange a means of proof there.

children.text: steyasāhasayor divyaṃ svalpe 'py arthe pradāpayet ||
children.translated_text: In cases of theft and violent assault, an ordeal should be imposed even for a small amount.

children.text: sarvadravyapramāṇaṃ tu jñātvā hema prakalpayet
children.translated_text: Having ascertained the full value of the property, one should set it in terms of gold.

children.text: hemapramāṇayuktaṃ tu tadā divyaṃ niyojayet ||
children.translated_text: When it is furnished with a measure in gold, one should then assign the ordeal.

children.text: jñātvā saṃkhyāṃ suvarṇānāṃ śatanāśe viṣaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: Having determined the number of <s>suvarṇas</s>, poison is prescribed for the loss of a hundred.

children.text: aśītes tu vināśe vai dadyāc caiva hutāśanam ||
children.translated_text: For the loss of eighty, one should give the fire ordeal.

children.text: ṣaṣṭyā nāśe jalaṃ deyaṃ catvāriṃśati vai ghaṭam
children.translated_text: For the loss of sixty, water is to be given; for forty, the pot ordeal.

children.text: viṃśaddaśavināśe vai kośapānaṃ vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: For the loss of twenty or ten, drinking the <s>kośa</s> is prescribed.

children.text: pañcādhikasya vā nāśe tadardhārdhasya tandulāḥ
children.translated_text: For a loss of five or more, or of half and half of that, rice grains are prescribed.

children.text: tadardhārdhasya nāśe tu spṛśet putrādimastakam ||
children.translated_text: For a loss of half and half of that, he should touch the head of a son and the like.

children.text: tadardhārdhasya nāśe tu laukikāś ca kriyāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: For a loss of half and half of that, ordinary procedures are prescribed.

children.text: evaṃ vicārayan rājā dharmārthābhyāṃ na hīyate ||
children.translated_text: Judging in this way, the king does not fall away from <s>dharma</s> and practical interest.

children.text: rājanye 'gniṃ ghaṭaṃ vipre vaiśye toyaṃ niyojayet
children.translated_text: For a Kṣatriya he should prescribe fire; for a Brahmin, the pot; for a Vaiśya, water.

children.text: sarveṣu sarvadivyaṃ vā viṣaṃ varjya dvijottame ||
children.translated_text: Or he may prescribe any ordeal for all, except poison for an excellent twice-born man.

children.text: gorakṣakān vāṇijakāṃs tathā kārukuśīlavān
children.translated_text: Cowherds, merchants, and likewise artisans and performers,

children.text: preṣyān vārddhuṣikāṃś caiva grāhayecchūdravad dvijān ||
children.translated_text: servants and moneylenders, even if twice-born, he should make undergo the ordeal like Śūdras.

children.text: na lohaśilpinām agniṃ salilaṃ nāmbusevinām
children.translated_text: He should not give fire to metalworkers, nor water to those whose livelihood is in water.

children.text: mantrayogavidāṃ caiva viṣaṃ dadyāc ca na kvacit
children.translated_text: And he should never give poison to those who know mantra and yoga.

children.text: taṇḍulair na niyuñjīta vratinaṃ mukharogiṇam ||
children.translated_text: He should not employ rice grains for one under a vow or for one suffering from disease of the mouth.

children.text: kuṣṭhināṃ varjayed agniṃ salilaṃ śvāsakāsinām
children.translated_text: He should avoid fire for lepers, and water for those with asthma or cough.

children.text: pittaśleṣmavatāṃ nityaṃ viṣaṃ tu parivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: For those afflicted with bile or phlegm, he should always avoid poison.

children.text: madyapastrīvyasanināṃ kitavānāṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: To those addicted to drink and women, and likewise to gamblers,

children.text: kośaḥ prājñair na dātavyo ye ca nāstikavṛttayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and to those who follow atheistic conduct, the wise should not give the <s>kośa</s>.

children.text: mātāpitṛdvijagurubālastrīrājaghātinām
children.translated_text: For killers of mother, father, twice-born men, gurus, children, women, or kings,

children.text: mahāpātakayuktānāṃ nāstikānāṃ viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: for those connected with great sins, and especially for atheists,

children.text: liṅgināṃ praśaṭhānāṃ tu mantrayogakriyāvidām
children.translated_text: for wearers of religious marks, the very deceitful, and those skilled in mantra, yoga, and ritual techniques,

children.text: varṇasaṃkarajātānāṃ pāpābhyāsapravartinām ||
children.translated_text: for those born of mixed social classes and those engaged in habitual sin,

children.text: eteṣv evābhiyogeṣu nindyeṣv eva ca yatnataḥ
children.translated_text: in these very accusations, and carefully in blameworthy cases,

children.text: divyaṃ prakalpayen naiva rājā dharmaparāyaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a king devoted to <s>dharma</s> should not prescribe an ordeal at all.

children.text: etair eva niyuktānāṃ sādhūnāṃ divyam arhati
children.translated_text: For good men accused by these very persons, an ordeal is proper.

children.text: necchanti sādhavo yatra tatra śodhyāḥ svakair naraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Where good men do not wish it, there they should be cleared by their own people.

children.text: mahāpātakayukteṣu nāstikeṣu viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: For those connected with great sins, and especially for atheists,

children.text: na deyaṃ teṣu divyaṃ tu pāpābhyāsarateṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: and for those devoted to habitual sin, an ordeal should not be given.

children.text: eṣu vādeṣu divyāni pratiṣiddhāni yatnataḥ
children.translated_text: In these disputes ordeals are carefully forbidden.

children.text: kārayet sajjanais tāni nābhiśastaṃ tyajen manuḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should have them performed by good people; <s>Manu</s> says that an accused person should not be abandoned.

children.text: aspṛśyādhamadāsānāṃ mlecchānāṃ pāpakāriṇām
children.translated_text: For untouchables, the low-born, slaves, mlecchas, and evil-doers,

children.text: prātilomyaprasūtānāṃ niścayo na tu rājani
children.translated_text: and for those born from inverse unions, the decision does not lie simply with the king.

children.text: tatprasiddhāni divyāni saṃśaye teṣu nirdiśet ||
children.translated_text: When there is doubt regarding them, he should prescribe the ordeals customary among them.

children.text: indrasthāne 'bhiśastānāṃ mahāpātakināṃ nṛṇām
children.translated_text: For accused men who are great sinners, the ordeal should be at the place of <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: nṛpadrohe pravṛttānāṃ rājadvāre prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: For those engaged in treason against the king, it should be administered at the royal gate.

children.text: prātilomyaprasūtānāṃ divyaṃ deyaṃ catuṣpathe
children.translated_text: For those born from inverse unions, the ordeal should be given at a crossroads.

children.text: ato 'nyeṣu sabhāmadhye divyaṃ deyaṃ vidur budhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For others, the wise know that the ordeal should be given in the middle of the assembly.

children.text: kāladeśavirodhe tu yathāyuktaṃ prakalpayet
children.translated_text: But when there is conflict of time and place, he should prescribe it as is appropriate.

children.text: anyena hārayed divyaṃ vidhir eṣa viparyaye ||
children.translated_text: In a contrary case, he should have another undergo the ordeal; this is the rule.

children.text: adeśakāladattāni bahirvāsakṛtāni ca
children.translated_text: Ordeals given in the wrong place or at the wrong time,

children.text: vyabhicāraṃ sadārtheṣu kurvantīha na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those performed outside the proper conditions, undoubtedly produce irregularity in all matters here.

children.text: sādhayet tat punaḥ sādhyaṃ vyāghāte sādhanasya hi
children.translated_text: When the means of proof has been obstructed, he should establish again what is to be established.

children.text: dattāny api yathoktāni rājā divyāni varjayet
children.translated_text: Even ordeals given as prescribed should be set aside by the king

children.text: mūrkhair lubdhaiś ca duṣṭaiś ca punar deyāni tāni vai ||
children.translated_text: when they have been given by fools, greedy men, or corrupt men; they must then be given again.

children.text: tasmād yathoktavidhinā divyaṃ deyaṃ viśāradaiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore an ordeal should be given by experts according to the prescribed rule.

children.text: ayathoktaprayuktaṃ tu na śaktaṃ tasya sādhane ||
children.translated_text: But one applied contrary to prescription is not capable of establishing that matter.

children.text: śikyacchede tulābhaṅge tathā vāpi guṇasya vā
children.translated_text: If the sling breaks, or the balance breaks, or likewise if its cord breaks,

children.text: śuddhes tu saṃśaye caiva parīkṣeta punar naram ||
children.translated_text: and whenever there is doubt about purification, he should examine the man again.

children.text: praskhalaty abhiyuktaś cet sthānād anyatra dahyate
children.translated_text: If the accused stumbles, or is burned somewhere other than the prescribed spot,

children.text: na dagdhaṃ tu vidur devās tasya bhūyo 'pi dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: the gods do not regard him as burned; one should make him undergo the ordeal again.

children.text: śarāṃs tv anāyasair agraiḥ prakurvīta viśuddhaye
children.translated_text: For determining purity, he should make arrows with non-iron tips,

children.text: veṇakāṇḍamayāṃś caiva kṣeptā ca sudṛḍhaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: and made of bamboo stalks; the thrower should throw them very firmly.

children.text: kṣipte tu majjanaṃ kāryaṃ gamanaṃ samakālikam
children.translated_text: Once the arrow has been thrown, the immersion must be made, and the going must occur at the same time.

children.text: gamane tv āgamaḥ kāryaḥ pumān anyo jale viśet ||
children.translated_text: When the going is done, the return must be done; another man should enter the water.

children.text: śiromānaṃ tu dṛśyeta na karṇau nāpi nāsikā
children.translated_text: Only the top of the head should be visible, not the ears nor the nose,

children.text: apsu praveśane yasya śuddhaṃ tam api nirdiśet ||
children.translated_text: and when a man enters the waters in this way, one should declare him pure.

children.text: nimajjyotplavate yas tu dṛṣṭaś cet prāṇibhir naraḥ
children.translated_text: If a man, having submerged, rises up and is seen by people,

children.text: punas tatra nimajjet sa deśacihnavibhāvite ||
children.translated_text: he should submerge again there, at a place identified by markers.

children.text: ajāśṛṅganibhaṃ śyāmaṃ supīnaṃ śṛṅgasaṃbhavam
children.translated_text: The <s>śṛṅgin</s>-poison is like a goat's horn, dark, stout, and horn-shaped;

children.text: bhaṅge ca śṛṅgaverābhaṃ khyātaṃ tacchṛṅgiṇāṃ viṣam ||
children.translated_text: when broken it resembles ginger; that is the known poison of the horned class.

children.text: raktaṃ tadasitaṃ kuryāt kaṭinaṃ caiva tallakṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: It should make red blood black and hard: by that characteristic,

children.text: anena vidhinā jñeyaṃ divyaṃ divyaviśāradaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by this procedure, the <s>divya</s> should be recognized by experts in ordeals.

children.text: vatsanābhanibhaṃ pītaṃ varṇajñānena niścayaḥ
children.translated_text: Resembling <s>vatsanābha</s>, yellow: certainty comes from knowledge of its color;

children.text: śuktiśaṅkhākṛtir bhaṅge vidyāt tadvatsanābhakam ||
children.translated_text: if at the break it has the form of an oyster shell or conch, one should know it as <s>vatsanābha</s>.

children.text: madhukṣīrasamāyuktaṃ svacchaṃ kurvīta tatkṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: Mixed with honey and milk, it should become clear at once;

children.text: bāhyam evaṃ samākhyātaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ dharmasādhakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: thus the external mark has been described by those who establish <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: pūrvāhṇe śītale deśe viṣaṃ dadyāt tu dehinām
children.translated_text: In the forenoon, in a cool place, one should give poison to the persons,

children.text: ghṛtena yojitaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ piṣṭaṃ triṃśadguṇena tu ||
children.translated_text: made smooth by being mixed with ghee and ground with thirty times as much.

children.text: viṣasya palaṣaḍbhāgād bhāgo viṃśatim astu yaḥ
children.translated_text: Of poison, the dose should be a twentieth part of a sixth of a <s>pala</s>;

children.text: tam aṣṭabhāgahīnaṃ śodhye deyaṃ ghṛtāplutam ||
children.translated_text: that, reduced by one-eighth and covered with ghee, should be given to the one under examination.

children.text: svalpe 'parādhe devānāṃ snāpayitvāyudhodakam
children.translated_text: For a minor offense, after bathing the deities, consecrated weapon-water should be given to drink;

children.text: pāyyo vikāre cāśuddho niyamyaḥ śucir anyathā ||
children.translated_text: if there is an alteration he is impure and to be restrained; otherwise he is pure.

children.text: devatāsnānapānīyadivye taṇḍulabhakṣaṇe
children.translated_text: In the ordeal of drinking the water from a deity's bath and in the eating of rice,

children.text: śuddhaniṣṭhīvanācchuddho niyamyo 'śucir anyathā ||
children.translated_text: he is pure if he spits it out cleanly; otherwise he is impure and to be restrained.

children.text: avaṣṭambhābhiyuktasya viśuddhasyāpi kośataḥ
children.translated_text: When one has accused a person of obstruction, even if he is cleared by the <s>kośa</s> ordeal,

children.text: sadaṇḍam abhiyogaṃ ca dāpayed abhiyojakam
children.translated_text: the accuser should be made to pay the claim together with a fine;

children.text: divyena śuddhaṃ puruṣaṃ satkuryād dhārmiko nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a righteous king should honor a man who has been purified by an ordeal.

children.text: śoṇitaṃ dṛśyate yatra hanuvālaṃ ca sīdati
children.translated_text: Where blood is seen and the jaw-region sinks,

children.text: gātraṃ ca kampate yasya tam aśuddhaṃ vinirdiśet ||
children.translated_text: and whose body trembles, him one should declare impure.

children.text: atha daivavisaṃvādāt trisaptāhāt tu dāpayet
children.translated_text: But if, through failure of the divine sign, after three weeks,

children.text: abhiyuktaṃ tu yatnena tam arthaṃ daṇḍam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: one should carefully make the accused pay that amount and the fine.

children.text: tasyaikasya na sarvasya janasya yadi tad bhavet
children.translated_text: If that happens to him alone and not to the whole community,

children.text: rogo 'gnir jñātimaraṇam ṛṇaṃ dāpyo damaṃ ca saḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether disease, fire, or death of a kinsman occurs, he should be made to pay the debt and the penalty.

children.text: kṣayātisāravisphoṭās tālvasthiparipīḍanam
children.translated_text: Wasting disease, diarrhea, eruptions, oppression of the palate and bones,

children.text: netraruggalarogaś ca tathonmādaḥ prajāyate
children.translated_text: eye-pain, disease of the throat, and likewise madness arise,

children.text: śirorugbhujabhaṅgaś ca daivikā vyādhayo nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: as well as headache and fracture of the arm; these are men's divine illnesses.

children.text: śatārdhaṃ dāpayecchuddham aśuddho daṇḍabhāg bhavet ||
children.translated_text: A purified man should be made to pay fifty; the impure one becomes liable to the fine.

children.text: viṣe toye hutāśe ca tulākośe ca taṇḍule
children.translated_text: In poison, water, fire, the balance, the <s>kośa</s>, and rice,

children.text: taptamāṣakadivye ca kramād daṇḍaṃ prakalpayet ||
children.translated_text: and in the ordeal of the heated <s>māṣaka</s>, one should prescribe the fines in order.

children.text: sahasraṃ ṣaṭśataṃ caiva tathā pañca śatāni ca
children.translated_text: One thousand, six hundred, and likewise five hundred,

children.text: catustridvyekam evaṃ ca hīnaṃ hīneṣu kalpayet ||
children.translated_text: then four, three, two, and one hundred: so should he prescribe lower amounts for the lower cases.

children.text: yatropadiśyate karma kartur aṅgaṃ na tūcyate
children.translated_text: Where an act is prescribed but the agent's limb is not stated,

children.text: dakṣiṇas tatra vijñeyaḥ karmaṇāṃ pāragaḥ karaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there the right hand, skilled in actions, should be understood.

children.text: ā caturdaśakād ahno yasya no rājadaivikam
children.translated_text: Up to the fourteenth day, if no terrible calamity,

children.text: vyasanaṃ jāyate ghoraṃ sa jñeyaḥ śapathe śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether royal or divine, befalls him, he should be known as pure in the oath.

children.text: unmattenaiva mattena tathā bhāvāntareṇa vā
children.translated_text: What is given or done by a madman, by an intoxicated man,

children.text: yad dattaṃ yat kṛtaṃ vātha pramāṇaṃ naiva tad bhavet ||
children.translated_text: or by someone in an altered state, is not valid proof.

children.text: asvatantrakṛtaṃ kāryaṃ tasya svāmī nivartayet
children.translated_text: A transaction done by a dependent person should be annulled by his master;

children.text: na bhartrā vivadetānyo bhītonmattakṛtād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: no one else should litigate with the master, except over what was done by a frightened or mad person.

children.text: pitāsvatantraḥ pitṛmān bhrātā bhrātṛvya eva vā
children.translated_text: A man with a father is dependent on his father, and a brother may be dependent on a brother or brother's son;

children.text: kaniṣṭho vāvibhaktasvo dāsaḥ karmakaras tathā ||
children.translated_text: so too a younger undivided co-owner, a slave, and a hired servant.

children.text: na kṣetragṛhadāsānāṃ dānādhamanavikrayāḥ
children.translated_text: Gifts, mortgages, or sales of fields, houses, and slaves,

children.text: asvatantrakṛtāḥ siddhiṃ prāpnuyur nānuvarṇitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when made by dependent persons, do not become valid unless they have been approved.

children.text: pramāṇaṃ sarva evaite paṇyānāṃ krayavikraye
children.translated_text: All these are valid authority in the purchase and sale of merchandise,

children.text: yadi saṃvyavahāraṃ te kurvanto 'py anumoditāḥ ||
