children.translated_text: But when a taxpayer has fled, together with the surety for the tax,

children.text: karārthaṃ karadakṣetraṃ vikrīṇīyuḥ sabhāsadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the judges should sell the taxpayer's field for the sake of the tax.

children.text: samavetais tu sāmantair abhijñaiḥ pāpabhīrubhiḥ
children.translated_text: By assembled neighbors who are competent and fear wrongdoing,

children.text: kṣetrārāmagṛhādīnāṃ dvipadāṃ ca catuṣpadām ||
children.translated_text: for fields, gardens, houses and the like, and for bipeds and quadrupeds,

children.text: kalpitaṃ mūlyam ity āhur bhāgaṃ kṛtvā tad aṣṭadhā
children.translated_text: they say the value is fixed; after dividing that into eight shares,

children.text: ekabhāgātiriktaṃ vā hīnaṃ vānucitaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: more than one share beyond it, or less, is remembered as improper.

children.text: samāḥ śatam atīte 'pi sarvaṃ tad vinivartate
children.translated_text: Even after a hundred years have passed, all that is rescinded,

children.text: krayavikrayaṇe krayyaṃ yan mūlyaṃ dharmato 'rhati ||
children.translated_text: in a sale and purchase, when the saleable thing legally deserves a certain price.

children.text: tat turye pañcame ṣaṣṭhe saptame 'ṃśe 'ṣṭame 'pi vā
children.translated_text: If, of that price, by a fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, or even eighth share,

children.text: hīne yadi vinirvṛtte krayavikrāyaṇe sati ||
children.translated_text: it is deficient when the sale and purchase have been completed,

children.text: hīnamūlyaṃ tu tat sarvaṃ kṛtam apy akṛtaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: then that whole low-priced transaction, though done, becomes as not done.

children.text: uktād alpatare hīne krayo naiva praduṣyati ||
children.translated_text: If the deficiency is less than what has been stated, the purchase is not at all vitiated.

children.text: tenāpy aṃśena hīyeta mūlyataḥ krayavikraye
children.translated_text: By that share too, in a sale and purchase, the price would be reduced;

children.text: katam apy akṛtaṃ prāhur anye dharmavido janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: other people learned in <s>dharma</s> say that even what has been done is undone.

children.text: ardhādhike krayaḥ sidhyed uktalābho daśādhikaḥ
children.translated_text: A purchase is valid when there is an excess of half; the stipulated gain may be an additional ten.

children.text: avakrayas tribhāgena sadya eva rucikrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A repurchase is by a third, and a purchase made by preference takes effect immediately.

children.text: mūlyāt svalpapradāne 'pi krayasiddhiḥ kṛtā bhavet
children.translated_text: Even when a small part of the price has been paid, the purchase is considered completed.

children.text: cakravṛddhyāṃ pradātavyaṃ deyaṃ tat samayād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: In compound interest, what is owed must be paid, except as fixed by agreement.

children.text: yas tu na grāhayecchilpaṃ karmāṇy anyāni kārayet
children.translated_text: But one who does not have a craft taught, and makes the pupil do other tasks,

children.text: prāpnuyāt sāhasaṃ pūrvaṃ tasmācchiṣyo nivartate ||
children.translated_text: incurs the first <s>sāhasa</s> (amercement); therefore the pupil withdraws from him.

children.text: śikṣito 'pi śritaṃ kāmam antevāsī samācaret
children.translated_text: Even after being trained, a resident pupil should willingly do what he has undertaken.

children.text: tatra karma ca yat kuryād ācāryasyaiva tatphalam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever work he performs there, its fruit belongs only to the teacher.

children.text: svatantrasyātmano dānād dāsatvaṃ dāravad bhṛguḥ
children.translated_text: According to <s>Bhṛgu</s>, slavery arises from an independent person giving himself, as with a wife.

children.text: triṣu varṇeṣu vijñeyaṃ dāsyaṃ viprasya na kvacit ||
children.translated_text: Among the three varṇas slavery is to be recognized; for a Brahmin, never in any case.

children.text: varṇānām anulāmyena dāsyaṃ na pratilomataḥ
children.translated_text: Slavery follows the regular order of the varṇas, not the reverse order,

children.text: rājanyavaiśyaśūdrāṇāṃ tyajatāṃ hi svatantratām ||
children.translated_text: for Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras who abandon their independence.

children.text: samavarṇo 'pi vipraṃ tu dāsatvaṃ naiva kārayet
children.translated_text: Even one of the same varṇa must not make a Brahmin enter slavery,

children.text: brāhmaṇasya hi dāsatvān nṛpatejo vihanyate ||
children.translated_text: for through the slavery of a Brahmin the king's splendor is impaired.

children.text: kṣatraviśśūdradharmas tu samavarṇe kadācana
children.translated_text: But the rule for Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras applies at times within the same varṇa;

children.text: kārayed dāsakarmāṇi brāhmaṇaṃ na bṛhaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: according to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, one may make them perform slave-labor, but not a Brahmin.

children.text: śīlādhyayanasampanne tadūnaṃ karma kāmataḥ
children.translated_text: If a man endowed with conduct and Vedic study willingly undertakes work below that,

children.text: tatrāpi nāśubhaṃ kiṃcit prakurvīta dvijottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even then the best of the twice-born should not perform anything impure.

children.text: viṇmūtronmārjanaṃ caiva nagnatvaparimardanam
children.translated_text: Cleaning away feces and urine, and rubbing or massaging while naked,

children.text: prāyo dāsīsutāḥ kuryur gavādigrahaṇaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: and such tasks as taking cattle and the like, are generally to be done by sons of slave-women.

children.text: pravrajyāvasitā yatra trayo varṇā dvijādayaḥ
children.translated_text: Where the three varṇas beginning with twice-born men have fallen from renunciant life,

children.text: nirvāsaṃ kārayed vipraṃ dāsatvaṃ kṣatraviḍ nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king should have a Brahmin exiled, but impose slavery on a Kṣatriya or Vaiśya.

children.text: śūdraṃ tu kārayed dāsaṃ krītam akrītam eva vā
children.translated_text: But he should make a Śūdra a slave, whether bought or not bought,

children.text: dāsyāyaiva hi sṛṣṭaḥ sa svayam eva svayambhuvā ||
children.translated_text: for he was created for slavery by <s>Svayambhū</s> himself.

children.text: svadāsīṃ yas tu saṃgacchet prasūtā ca bhavet tataḥ
children.translated_text: If a man has intercourse with his own slave-woman and she gives birth from that,

children.text: avekṣya bījaṃ kāryā syān na dāsī sānvayā tu sā ||
children.translated_text: then, considering the seed, she should be dealt with accordingly; she is not a slave, together with her descendants.

children.text: dāsasya tu dhanaṃ yat syāt svāmī tasya prabhuḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever property a slave may have, his master is remembered as lord of it.

children.text: prakāśaṃ vikrayād yat tu na svāmī dhanam arhati ||
children.translated_text: But the master is not entitled to property obtained from an open sale.

children.text: dāsenoḍhā svadāsī yā sāpi dāsītvam āpnuyāt
children.translated_text: A woman married by a slave also attains the condition of a slave,

children.text: yasmād bhartā prabhus tasyāḥ svāmyadhīnaḥ prabhur yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: because her husband is her lord, and that lord is under the master.

children.text: ādadyād brāhmaṇīṃ yas tu cikrīṇīta tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Whoever takes a Brahmin woman, and likewise whoever sells her,

children.text: rājñā tad akṛtaṃ kāryaṃ daṇḍyāḥ syuḥ sarva eva te ||
children.translated_text: the king should make that act void; all of them are punishable.

children.text: kāmāt tu saṃśritāṃ yas tu dāsīṃ kuryāt kulastriyam
children.translated_text: But whoever, out of desire, makes a woman of good family who has come for refuge into a slave,

children.text: saṃkrāmayeta vānyatra daṇḍyas tac cākṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: or transfers her elsewhere, is punishable, and that act becomes void.

children.text: bāladhātrīm adāsīṃ ca dāsīm iva bhunakti yaḥ
children.translated_text: He who treats a child-nurse who is not a slave as though she were a slave,

children.text: paricārakapatnīṃ vā prāpnuyāt pūrvasāhasam ||
children.translated_text: or likewise a servant's wife, incurs the first <s>sāhasa</s> (amercement).

children.text: vikrośamānāṃ yo bhaktāṃ dāsīṃ vikretum icchati
children.translated_text: One who wishes to sell a dependent slave-woman while she is crying out,

children.text: anāpadisthaḥ śaktaḥ san prāpnuyād dviśataṃ damam ||
children.translated_text: though he is not in distress and is able, incurs a fine of two hundred.

children.text: tavāham iti cātmānaṃ yo 'svatantraḥ prayacchati
children.translated_text: And an unfree man who offers himself, saying, 'I am yours,'

children.text: na sa taṃ prāpnuyāt kāmaṃ pūrvasvāmī labheta tam ||
children.translated_text: does not obtain that wish; his former master should get him.

children.text: pravrajyāvasito dāso moktavyaś ca na kenacit
children.translated_text: A slave who has left renunciant life is not to be released by anyone;

children.text: anākālabhṛto dāsyān mucyate goyugaṃ dadat ||
children.translated_text: one maintained in a time of calamity is freed from slavery by giving a pair of cattle.

children.text: ādhikyaṃ nyūnatā cāṃśe astināstitvam eva ca
children.translated_text: Excess, deficiency in share, existence and nonexistence,

children.text: abhogabhuktiḥ sīmā ca ṣaṭ bhūvād asya hetavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: non-enjoyment or enjoyment, and boundary: these are the six causes of a land dispute.

children.text: tasmin bhogaḥ prayoktavyaḥ sarvasākṣiṣu tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: In that matter possession should be adduced; it stands among all witnesses.

children.text: lekhyārūḍhaś cetaraś ca sākṣī mārgadvayānvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Entered in a document and otherwise as witness, it has two modes.

children.text: kṣetravāstutaḍāgeṣu kūpopavanasetuṣu
children.translated_text: In fields, house-sites, tanks, wells, groves, and embankments,

children.text: dvayor vivāde sāmantaḥ pratyayaḥ sarvavastuṣu ||
children.translated_text: when two parties dispute, a neighboring landholder is proof in all matters.

children.text: sāmantabhāve 'sāmantaiḥ kuryāt kṣetrādinirṇayam
children.translated_text: In the absence of neighboring landholders, one should decide fields and the like by non-neighbors;

children.text: grāmasīmāsu ca tathā tadvan nagaradeśayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: so too in village boundaries, and likewise in the case of towns and districts.

children.text: grāmo grāmasya sāmantaḥ kṣetraṃ kṣetrasya kīrtitam
children.translated_text: A village is called the neighbor of a village, and a field of a field;

children.text: gṛhaṃ gṛhasya nirdiṣṭaṃ samantāt parirabhya hi ||
children.translated_text: a house is specified as the neighbor of a house, when it encloses it on every side.

children.text: teṣām abhāve sāmantamaulavṛddhoddhṛtādayaḥ
children.translated_text: In their absence, original residents, elders, excavated marks, and the like serve as proof.

children.text: sthāvare ṣaṭprakāre 'pi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: In the case of immovable property, even in its six forms, no inquiry is to be made here.

children.text: saṃsaktās tv atha sāmantās tatsaṃsaktās tathottarāḥ
children.translated_text: But the adjoining neighbors are the <s>sāmanta</s>s; those adjoining them are the next group,

children.text: saṃsaktasaktasaṃsaktāḥ padmākārāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those adjoining the persons attached to them are declared to be arranged like a lotus.

children.text: svārthasiddhau praduṣṭeṣu sāmanteṣv arthagauravāt
children.translated_text: When the neighboring landholders have become corrupt in pursuing their own interest, because the matter is weighty,

children.text: tatsaṃsaktais tu kartavya uddhāro nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the ascertainment should be made by those adjoining them; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: saṃsaktasaktadoṣe tu tatsaṃsaktāḥ prakīrtitāḥ
children.translated_text: But when there is fault among those attached to the adjoining neighbors, those attached to them are specified;

children.text: kartavyā na praduṣṭās tu rājñā dharmaṃ vijānatā ||
children.translated_text: the uncorrupted ones are to be used by a king who understands <s>dharma</s> (law).

children.text: nājñānena hi mucyante sāmantā nirṇayaṃ prati
children.translated_text: For neighboring landholders are not excused by ignorance with respect to a decision.

children.text: ajñānoktau daṇḍayitvā punaḥ sīmāṃ vicārayet
children.translated_text: If they declare ignorance, after fining them he should examine the boundary again;

children.text: kīrtite yadi bhedaḥ syād daṇḍyās tūttamasāhasam ||
children.translated_text: if a discrepancy appears in what has been stated, they are to be fined the <s>uttamasāhasa</s> fine.

children.text: tyaktvā duṣṭāṃs tu sāmantān anyān maulādibhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Leaving aside corrupt neighboring landholders, together with others such as the original witnesses,

children.text: saṃmiśraya kārayet sīmām evaṃ dharmavido viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should have the boundary established by a mixed body; so those who know <s>dharma</s> understand it.

children.text: ye tatra pūrvaṃ sāmantāḥ paścād deśāntaraṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who were formerly neighboring landholders there and later went to another region,

children.text: tanmūlatvāt tu te maulā ṛṣibhiḥ saṃprakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: because they have that place as their root, are proclaimed by the seers to be <s>maula</s> (original witnesses).

children.text: niṣpādyamānaṃ yair dṛṣṭaṃ tat kāryaṃ nṛguṇānvitaiḥ
children.translated_text: Those by whom the matter being carried out was seen, men endowed with good qualities,

children.text: vṛddhā vā yadi vāvṛddhās te vṛddhāḥ parikīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether aged or not aged, are called <s>vṛddha</s> (elders).

children.text: upaśravaṇasaṃbhogakāryākhyānopacihnitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those marked by hearing about it, by use and enjoyment, and by narration of the matter,

children.text: uddharanti tato yasmād uddhṛtās te tataḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: because they draw the decision out from that, are therefore remembered as <s>uddhṛta</s>.

children.text: sāmantāḥ sādhanaṃ pūrvam aniṣṭoktau guṇānvitāḥ
children.translated_text: Neighboring landholders who possess good qualities are the first evidence when an unwelcome statement is made;

children.text: dviguṇās tūttarā jñeyā tato 'nye triguṇā matāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the next group should be known as double in number, and those after that are held to be triple.

children.text: eko yadvan nayet sīmām ubhayor īpsitaḥ kvacit
children.translated_text: Where a single man, acceptable to both parties, is to trace the boundary,

children.text: mastake kṣitim āropya raktavāsāḥ samāhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should place earth on his head, wear red garments, and be composed.

children.text: bhayavarjitabhūpena sarvābhāve svayaṃkṛtā ||
children.translated_text: When all witnesses are absent, the act is to be done by the king himself, free from fear.

children.text: kṣetrakūpataḍāgānāṃ kedārārāmayor api
children.translated_text: This applies to fields, wells, tanks, cultivated plots, and gardens,

children.text: gṛhaprāsādāvasathanṛpadevagṛheṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: and also to houses, mansions, dwellings, royal buildings, and temples.

children.text: bahūnāṃ tu gṛhītānāṃ na sarve nirṇayaṃ yadi
children.translated_text: But if, among many persons who have been summoned, not all make the decision,

children.text: kuryur bhayād vā lobhād vā dāpyās tūttamasāhasam ||
children.translated_text: whether from fear or from greed, they are to be made to pay the <s>uttamasāhasa</s> fine.

children.text: sīmācaṅkramaṇe kośe pādasparśe tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: In boundary-walking, in the <s>kośa</s> ordeal, and likewise in touching with the foot,

children.text: tripakṣapakṣasaptāhaṃ daivarājikam iṣyate ||
children.translated_text: the divine and royal periods are held to be three fortnights, a fortnight, and seven days.

children.text: mekhalābhramaniṣkāsagavākṣān noparodhayet
children.translated_text: One should not obstruct a belt-space, passage, outlet, or window,

children.text: praṇālīṃ gṛhavāstuṃ ca pīḍayan daṇḍabhāg bhavet ||
children.translated_text: nor a drain or house-site; one who causes obstruction becomes liable to a fine.

children.text: niveśasamayād ūrdhvaṃ naite yojyāḥ kadācana
children.translated_text: After the time of settlement, these should never be newly imposed;

children.text: dṛṣṭipātaṃ praṇālīṃ ca na kuryāt paraveśmasu ||
children.translated_text: one should not make an overlooking view or a drain into another's house.

children.text: viṇmūtrodakavapraṃ ca vahniśvabhraniveśanam
children.translated_text: For a latrine, urine-channel, water embankment, fire-place, or pit,

children.text: aratnidvayam utsṛjya parakuḍyān niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: one should set it down after leaving two <s>aratni</s>s from another's wall.

children.text: sarve janāḥ sadā yena prayānti sa catuṣpathaḥ
children.translated_text: A place by which all people always pass is a crossroads;

children.text: aniruddho yathākālaṃ rājamārgaḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: when unobstructed at the proper times, it is called a royal road.

children.text: na tatra ropayet kiṃcin nopahanyāt tu kenacit
children.translated_text: No one should plant anything there, nor should it be damaged by anyone;

children.text: gurvācāryanṛpādīnāṃ mārgādānāt tu daṇḍabhāk ||
children.translated_text: one is liable to a fine for taking away the road of elders, teachers, kings, and the like.

children.text: yas tatra saṃkaraśvabhrān vṛkṣāropaṇam eva ca
children.translated_text: Whoever there intentionally makes rubbish pits, plants trees,

children.text: kāmāt purīṣaṃ kuryāc ca tasya daṇḍas tu māṣakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or defecates at will, his fine is a <s>māṣaka</s>.

children.text: taṭākodyānatīrthāni yo 'medhyena vināśayet
children.translated_text: Whoever destroys tanks, parks, and sacred fords with impure matter,

children.text: amedhyaṃ śodhayitvā tu daṇḍayet pūrvasāhasam ||
children.translated_text: after making the impurity cleaned away, he should be fined the <s>pūrvasāhasa</s>.

children.text: dūṣayet siddhatīrthāni sthāpitāni mahātmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: If he pollutes established sacred fords, founded by great men,

children.text: puṇyāni pāvanīyāni prāpnuyāt pūrvasāhasam ||
children.translated_text: holy and purifying, he should incur the <s>pūrvasāhasa</s> fine.

children.text: sīmāmadhye tu jātānāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ kṣetrayor dvayoḥ
children.translated_text: For trees growing in the middle of the boundary between two fields,

children.text: phalaṃ puṣpaṃ ca sāmānyaṃ kṣetrasvāmiṣu nirdiśet ||
children.translated_text: one should declare the fruit and flowers common to the owners of the fields.

children.text: anyakṣetre tu jātānāṃ śākhā yatrānyasaṃśritāḥ
children.translated_text: For trees growing in another field, where their branches extend into someone else's land,

children.text: svāminaṃ taṃ vijānīyād yasya kṣetreṣu saṃśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should know the owner to be the person in whose field they are situated.

children.text: asvāmyanumatenaiva saṃskāraṃ kurute tu yaḥ
children.translated_text: But if someone makes repairs without the owner's permission,

children.text: gṛhodyānataṭākānāṃ saṃskartā labhate na tu ||
children.translated_text: the repairer of houses, gardens, or tanks does not thereby receive repayment;

children.text: vyayaṃ svāmini cāyāte na nivedya nṛpe yadi
children.translated_text: he does not receive the expense when the owner has arrived, if he had not reported it to the king.

children.text: athāvedya prayuktas tu tadgataṃ labhate vyayam ||
children.translated_text: But if he undertook it after reporting it, he receives the expense spent on it.

children.text: aśaktito na dadyāc cet khilārtho yat kṛto vyayaḥ
children.translated_text: If through inability the owner does not pay the expense made for reclaiming fallow land,

children.text: tadaṣṭabhāgahīnaṃ tu karṣakaḥ phalam āpnuyāt
children.translated_text: then the cultivator should receive the produce, less one eighth of that amount;

children.text: varṣāṇy aṣṭau sa bhoktā syāt parataḥ svāmine tu tat ||
children.translated_text: he shall be its enjoyer for eight years; after that it belongs to the owner.

children.text: aśaktapretanaṣṭeṣu kṣetrikeṣv anivāritaḥ
children.translated_text: When the landholders are unable, dead, or lost, and no one forbids him,

children.text: kṣetraṃ ced vikṛṣet kaścid aśnuvīta sa tatphalam ||
children.translated_text: if someone cultivates a field, he may enjoy its produce.

children.text: vikṛṣyamāṇe kṣetre ca kṣetrikaḥ punar āvrajet
children.translated_text: And if, while the field is being cultivated, the landholder should return,

children.text: śīlopacāraṃ tat sarvaṃ dattvā kṣetramavāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: after giving all the customary consideration, he obtains the field.

children.text: tadaṣṭabhāgāpacayād yāvat sapta gatāḥ samāḥ
children.translated_text: With one eighth of that deducted as each year passes, up to seven years,

children.text: samāpte 'ṣṭame varṣe bhuktakṣetraṃ labheta saḥ ||
children.translated_text: at the completion of the eighth year he obtains the field that has been enjoyed.

children.text: huṅkāraḥ kāsanaṃ caiva loke yac ca vigarhitam
children.translated_text: A grunt, coughing, and whatever else is censured in the world,

children.text: anukuryād anubrūyād vākpāruṣyaṃ tad ucyate ||
children.translated_text: if one imitates or repeats it, that is called <s>vākpāruṣya</s> (verbal harshness).

children.text: niṣṭhurāślīlatīvratvāt tad api trividhaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: Because it may be harsh, obscene, or severe, that too is remembered as threefold.

children.text: ākṣepo niṣṭhuraṃ jñeyam aślīlaṃ nyaṅgasaṃjñitam
children.translated_text: An accusation is to be known as harsh; what is obscene is termed degrading;

children.text: patanīyair upākrośais tīvram āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise say that severe speech consists of reproaches involving offenses that cause a fall.

children.text: yat tv asatsaṃjñitair aṅgaiḥ paramākṣipati kvacit
children.translated_text: When someone assails another with terms for disreputable bodily defects,

children.text: abhūtair vātha bhūtair vā niṣṭhurā vāksmṛtā budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether false or true, that is remembered by the learned as harsh speech.

children.text: nyagbhāvakaraṇaṃ vācā krodhāt tu kurute yadā
children.translated_text: When out of anger he causes humiliation by speech

children.text: vṛttadeśakulādīnām aślīlā sā budhaiḥ smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: concerning livelihood, region, family, and the like, the learned remember that as obscene.

children.text: mahāpātakayoktrī ca rāgadveṣakarī ca yā
children.translated_text: Speech that alleges great sins and produces passion or hatred,

children.text: jātibhraṃśakārī vātha tīvrā sā prathitā tu vāk ||
children.translated_text: or that causes loss of caste, is known as severe speech.

children.text: yo 'guṇān kīrtayet krodhān niguṇo vā guṇajñatām
children.translated_text: They know as verbally corrupt the man who, out of anger, proclaims faults,

children.text: anyasaṃjñānuyogī vā vāgduṣṭaṃ taṃ naraṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: or who, though without qualities, claims knowledge of qualities, or applies a wrong designation to another.

children.text: aduṣṭasyaiva yo doṣān kīrtayed doṣakāraṇāt
children.translated_text: Whoever, from a motive of blame, proclaims faults of one who is in fact faultless,

children.text: anyāpadeśavādī ca vāgduṣṭaṃ taṃ naraṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whoever speaks by insinuating another meaning: people know that man as guilty in speech.

children.text: mohāt pramādāt saṃgharṣāt prītyā coktaṃ mayeti yat
children.translated_text: If he says, 'This was said by me through delusion, negligence, quarrel, or affection,

children.text: nāham evaṃ punar vakṣye daṇḍārdhaṃ tasya kalpayet ||
children.translated_text: I will not speak so again,' one should prescribe half the fine for him.

children.text: yatra syāt parihārārthaṃ patitas tena kīrtanam
children.translated_text: Where mention of someone as fallen is made by him for the sake of exculpation,

children.text: vacanāt tatra na syāt tu doṣo yatra vibhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: there is no fault there on account of the statement, when he proves the matter.

children.text: anyathā tulyadoṣaḥ syān mithyoktau tūttamaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Otherwise he would have equal guilt; but for a false statement the highest fine is prescribed.

children.text: mahatā praṇidhānena vāgduṣṭaṃ sādhayen naram ||
children.translated_text: With very careful investigation one should establish a man as guilty in speech.

children.text: atathyaṃ śrāvitaṃ rājā prayatnena vicārayet
children.translated_text: When an untrue report has been heard, the king should examine it with effort.

children.text: anṛtākhyānaśīlānāṃ jihvāchedo viśodhanam ||
children.translated_text: For those whose habit is telling falsehood, cutting off the tongue is the purification.

children.text: hetvādibhir na paśyec ced daṇḍapāruṣyakāraṇam
children.translated_text: If, by reasons and the like, he does not discern the cause of physical violence,

children.text: tatra sākṣikṛtaṃ caiva divyaṃ vā viniyojayet ||
children.translated_text: there he should employ proof made by witnesses, or else a <s>divya</s> (ordeal).

children.text: ābhīṣaṇena daṇḍena prahared yas tu mānavaḥ
children.translated_text: If a man strikes a person with a terrifying rod or weapon,

children.text: pūrvaṃ cāpīḍito vātha sa daṇḍyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or even if he has first been oppressed, he is declared punishable.

children.text: karṇauṣṭhaghrāṇapādākṣijihvāśiśnakarasya ca
children.translated_text: For cutting off an ear, lip, nose, foot, eye, tongue, penis, or hand,

children.text: chedane cottamo daṇḍo bhedane madhyamo bhṛguḥ ||
children.translated_text: the highest fine is due; for splitting or breaking, the middle fine, says <s>Bhṛgu</s>.

children.text: manuṣyāṇāṃ paśūnāṃ ca duḥkhāya prahate sati
children.translated_text: When a blow causes pain to human beings or animals,

children.text: yathā yathā bhaved duḥkhaṃ daṇḍaṃ kuryāt tathā tathā ||
children.translated_text: just as the pain may be, so should the fine be imposed.

children.text: aspṛśyadhūrtadāsānāṃ mlecchānāṃ pāpakāriṇām
children.translated_text: For untouchables, rogues, slaves, <s>mlecchas</s>, evildoers,

children.text: pratilomaprasūtānāṃ tāḍanaṃ nārthato damaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those born from <s>pratiloma</s> unions, beating is the correction, not a monetary penalty.

children.text: chardimūtrapurīṣādyair āpādyaḥ sa caturguṇaḥ
children.translated_text: With vomit, urine, feces, and the like, the penalty is fourfold if it reaches the feet;

children.text: ṣaḍguṇaḥ kāyamadhye syān mūrdhni tv aṣṭaguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is sixfold on the middle of the body, but on the head it is prescribed as eightfold.

children.text: udgūraṇe tu hastasya kāryo dvādaśako damaḥ
children.translated_text: For raising the hand threateningly, a fine of twelve is to be imposed.

children.text: sa eva dviguṇaḥ proktaḥ pātaneṣu svajātiṣu ||
children.translated_text: That same fine is said to be doubled when people of one's own caste are thrown down.

children.text: vākpāruṣye yathaivoktāḥ prātilomyānulomataḥ
children.translated_text: Just as the fines have been stated for verbal abuse, according to inverse or direct caste order,

children.text: tathaiva daṇḍapāruṣye pātyā daṇḍā yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: so too in physical assault the fines are to be assigned in due sequence.

children.text: dehendriyavināśe tu yathā daṇḍaṃ prakalpayet
children.translated_text: But in the destruction of body or sense organs, one should prescribe the fine accordingly.

children.text: tathā tuṣṭikaraṃ deyaṃ samutthānaṃ ca paṇḍitaiḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise satisfaction-compensation and recovery should be given, according to the learned,

children.text: samutthānavyayaṃ cāsau dadyād ā vraṇaropaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: and that man should also pay the cost of recovery until the wound has healed.

children.text: vāgdaṇḍas tāḍanaṃ caiva yeṣūktam aparādhiṣu
children.translated_text: In the case of offenders for whom a verbal fine and beating have been prescribed,

children.text: hṛtaṃ bhagnaṃ pradāpyās te śodhyaṃ niḥsvais tu karmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: they should be made to restore what was taken or broken; but the destitute should be corrected by labor.

children.text: śrāntāṃs tṛṣārtān kṣudhitān akāle vāhayen naraḥ
children.translated_text: If a man makes donkeys, cows, buffaloes, camels, and the like work

children.text: kharagomahiṣoṣṭrādīn prāpnuyāt pūrvasāhasam ||
children.translated_text: when they are weary, thirsty, hungry, or at an improper time, he incurs the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine.

children.text: dvipaṇo dvādaśapaṇo vadhe tu mṛgapakṣiṇām
children.translated_text: For the killing of wild animals and birds there is a fine of two <s>paṇas</s> or twelve <s>paṇas</s>;

children.text: sarpamārjāranakulaśvasūkaravadhe nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: the same applies to men for killing a snake, cat, mongoose, dog, or pig.

children.text: gokumārīdevapaśumukṣāṇaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: If one makes a cow, a young cow, an animal belonging to a deity, a breeding ox, or a bull carry loads,

children.text: vāhayan sāhasaṃ pūrvaṃ prāpnuyād uttamaṃ vadhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he incurs the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine; for killing one of them, the highest fine is incurred.

children.text: pramāpaṇe prāṇabhṛtāṃ dadyāt tatpratirūpakam
children.translated_text: On causing the death of living beings, he should give a corresponding replacement,

children.text: tasyānurūpaṃ mūlyaṃ vā dadyād ity abravīn manuḥ ||
children.translated_text: or he should give a price appropriate to it; so said <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: vanaspatīnāṃ sarveṣām upabhogo yathā yathā
children.translated_text: For all trees, according as their use may be,

children.text: tathā tathā damaḥ kāryo hiṃsāyām iti dhāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: so in each case the fine should be imposed for injuring them: this is the settled rule.

children.text: śiṣyaṃ krodhena hanyāc ced ācāryo latayā vinā
children.translated_text: If a teacher, in anger, should strike a pupil with something other than a switch,

children.text: yenātyarthaṃ bhavet pīḍā vādaḥ syācchiṣyataḥ pituḥ ||
children.translated_text: so that excessive pain results, there may be a complaint by the pupil's father.

children.text: sahasā yat kṛtaṃ karma tat sāhasam udāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: An act done suddenly and violently is called <s>sāhasa</s>.

children.text: sānvayas tv apahāro yaḥ prasahya haraṇaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: An open seizure with accomplices, and whatever taking is done by force,

children.text: sāhasaṃ ca bhaved evaṃ steyam uktaṃ vinihnavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is likewise <s>sāhasa</s>; <s>steya</s> (theft) is said to be concealed appropriation.

children.text: vinā cihnais tu yat kāryaṃ sāhasākhyaṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: But when a case proceeding under the name <s>sāhasa</s> is without visible marks,

children.text: śapathaiḥ sa viśodhyaḥ syāt sarvavādeṣv ayaṃ vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: it should be cleared by oaths; this is the rule in all disputes.

children.text: ekaṃ ced bahavo hanyuḥ saṃrabdhāḥ puruṣaṃ narāḥ
children.translated_text: If many enraged men beat a single person,

children.text: marmaghātas tu yas teṣāṃ sa ghātaka iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the one among them whose blow strikes a vital spot is regarded as the killer.

children.text: vyāpādanena tatkārī vadhaṃ citram avāpnuyāt
children.translated_text: By killing, the doer of that act incurs a severe form of execution.

children.text: vināśahetum āyāntaṃ hanyād evāvicārayan ||
children.translated_text: One should kill without deliberation a person who is approaching as a cause of destruction.

children.text: udyatānāṃ tu pāpānāṃ hantur doṣo na vidyate
children.translated_text: In the case of wicked men with weapons raised, there is no fault for the slayer.

children.text: nivṛttās tu yadārambhād grahaṇaṃ na vadhaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when they have desisted from the undertaking, arrest, not killing, is prescribed.

children.text: ātatāyini cotkṛṣṭe tapaḥsvādhyāyajanmataḥ
children.translated_text: In the case of an <s>ātatāyin</s> (aggressor) who is eminent by austerity, Vedic study, or birth,

children.text: vadhas tatra tu naiva syāt pāpe hīne vadho bhṛguḥ ||
children.translated_text: there should be no killing there; but for a wicked inferior person there is killing, says <s>Bhṛgu</s>.

children.text: udyatāsiviṣāgniś ca cāpodyatakaras tathā
children.translated_text: One with a raised sword, poison, or fire, and likewise one whose hand is raised with a bow,

children.text: ātharvaṇena hantā ca piśunaś caiva rājani ||
children.translated_text: a killer by Atharvan rites, and an informer against someone before the king,

children.text: bhāryātikramakārī ca randhrānveṣaṇatatparaḥ
children.translated_text: one who transgresses with another's wife, and one devoted to searching out vulnerabilities,

children.text: evamādyān vijānīyāt sarvān evātatāyinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should know all such persons and others like them as <s>ātatāyins</s> (aggressors).

children.text: yaśovṛttaharān pāpān āhur dharmārthahārakān
children.translated_text: The wicked who take away reputation and conduct are said to take away <s>dharma</s> and wealth.

children.text: anākṣāritapūrvo yas tv aparādhe pravartate
children.translated_text: One who, without having first been accused, proceeds to an offense,

children.text: prāṇadravyāpahāre ca taṃ vidyād ātatāyinam ||
children.translated_text: and to the seizure of life or property, should be known as an <s>ātatāyin</s> (aggressor).

children.text: nakhināṃ śṛṅgiṇāṃ caiva daṃṣṭriṇāṃ cātatāyinām
children.translated_text: In the killing of clawed, horned, and fanged aggressors,

children.text: hastyaśvānāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ vadhe hantā na doṣabhāk ||
children.translated_text: and likewise of elephants, horses, and others, the killer does not share in guilt.

children.text: garbhasya pātane steno brāhmaṇyāṃ śastrapātena
children.translated_text: For causing the miscarriage of a fetus, and for striking down a Brahmin woman with a weapon,

children.text: aduṣṭāṃ yoṣitaṃ hatvā hantavyo brāhmaṇo 'pi hi ||
children.translated_text: after killing an innocent woman, even a Brahmin is indeed to be put to death.

children.text: kṣataṃ bhaṅgopamardau ca kuryād dravyeṣu yo naraḥ
children.translated_text: A man who causes a cut, breakage, or crushing in property

children.text: prāpnuyāt sāhasaṃ pūrvaṃ dravyabhāksvāmyudāhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: incurs the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine; the owner is declared entitled to the property.

children.text: hared bhindyād dahed vāpi devānāṃ pratimāṃ yadi
children.translated_text: If someone carries off, breaks, or burns an image of the gods,

children.text: tadgṛhaṃ caiva yo bhindyāt prāpnuyāt pūrvasāhasam ||
children.translated_text: or if he breaks their temple, he incurs the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine.

children.text: prākāraṃ bhedayed yas tu pātayec chātayet tathā
children.translated_text: Whoever breaks a wall, makes it fall, or damages it,

children.text: badhnīyād ambhaso mārgaṃ prāpnuyāt pūrvasāhasam ||
children.translated_text: or blocks the course of water, incurs the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine.

children.text: pracchannaṃ vā prakāśaṃ vā niśāyām athavā divā
children.translated_text: Whether hidden or open, whether by night or by day,

children.text: yat paradravyaharaṇaṃ steyaṃ tat parikīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: whatever taking of another's property occurs is declared to be <s>steya</s> (theft).

children.text: anyahastāt paribhraṣṭam akāmād uddhṛtaṃ bhuvi
children.translated_text: Stolen property that has fallen from another's hand, or has been picked up from the ground without intent,

children.text: caureṇa vā parikṣiptaṃ loptraṃ yatnāt parīkṣayet ||
children.translated_text: or has been cast away by a thief, should be carefully examined.

children.text: tulāmānapratimānapratirūpakalakṣitaiḥ
children.translated_text: One who operates with false balances, measures, standards, and counterfeits,

children.text: carann alakṣitair vāpi prāpnuyāt pūrvasāhasam ||
children.translated_text: whether marked or unmarked, should incur the first <s>sāhasa</s> fine.

children.text: gṛhe tu muṣitaṃ rājā cauragrāhāṃs tu dāpayet
children.translated_text: But when a house has been robbed, the king should make the thief-catchers pay,

children.text: ārakṣakāṃś ca dikpālān yadi cauro na labhyate ||
children.translated_text: as well as the guards and wardens of the quarters, if the thief is not found.

children.text: grāmāntare hṛtaṃ dravyaṃ grāmādhyakṣaṃ pradāpayet
children.translated_text: Property stolen within another village should be charged to the village headman.

children.text: vivīte svāminā deyaṃ cauroddhartā vivītake ||
children.translated_text: In pasture land it is to be paid by the owner; in a wild tract, by the officer who suppresses thieves.

children.text: svadeśe yasya yat kiṃciddhṛtaṃ deyaṃ nṛpeṇa tu
children.translated_text: Whatever is stolen in a man's own country is to be paid by the king.

children.text: gṛhṇīyāt tat svayaṃ naṣṭaṃ prāptam anviṣya pārthivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ruler should himself take up the lost matter, after searching it out and recovering it.

children.text: caurair hṛtaṃ prayatnena svarūpaṃ pratipādayet
children.translated_text: He should diligently restore, in its own form, what has been taken by thieves.

children.text: tadabhāve tu mūlyaṃ syād anyathā kilbiṣī nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If that is absent, its value must be given; otherwise the king is guilty.

children.text: labdhe 'pi caure yadi tu moṣas tasmān na labhyate
children.translated_text: Even when the thief has been found, if the stolen goods are not obtained from him,

children.text: dadyāt tam athavā cauraṃ dāpayet tu yatheṣṭataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king should pay that amount, or else make the thief pay as he thinks fit.

children.text: tasmiṃś ced dāpyamānānāṃ bhaved doṣe tu saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: If, while they are being made to pay, doubt arises about the fault in that case,

children.text: muṣitaḥ śapathaṃ dāpyo bandhubhir vā viśodhayet ||
children.translated_text: the robbed man should be made to take an oath, or he should clear the matter through his kinsmen.

children.text: yasmād apahṛtāl labdhaṃ dravyāt svalpaṃ tu svāminā
children.translated_text: If the owner has recovered only a small part of property taken by someone,

children.text: taccheṣam āpnuyāt tasmāt pratyaye svāminā kṛte ||
children.translated_text: he should obtain the remainder from that person, once the owner has furnished proof.

children.text: svadeśaghātino ye syus tathā mārganirodhakāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who are destroyers of their own country, and likewise those who block the roads,

children.text: teṣāṃ sarvasvam ādāya rājā śūle niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: the king should take all their property and impale them on a stake.

children.text: acorād dāpitaṃ dravyaṃ caurānveṣaṇatatparaiḥ
children.translated_text: If property has been made to be paid by a non-thief by men intent on tracking thieves,

children.text: upalabdhe labheraṃs te dviguṇaṃ tatra dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: then, when the thief is discovered, they should recover it, and the king should make double payment there.

children.text: yena yena paradrohaṃ karoty aṅgena taskaraḥ
children.translated_text: With whatever limb a thief does harm to another,

children.text: chindyād aṅgaṃ nṛpas tasya na karoti yathā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the king should cut off that limb of his, so that he does not do it again.

children.text: trapuṣe vāruke dve tu pañcāmraṃ pañcadāḍimam
children.translated_text: A person is not at fault for taking two cucumbers or gourds, five mangoes, five pomegranates,

children.text: kharjūrabadarādīnāṃ muṣṭiṃ gṛhṇan na duṣyati ||
children.translated_text: or a handful of dates, jujubes, and the like.

children.text: mānavāḥ sadya evāhuḥ sahoḍhānāṃ pravāsanam
children.translated_text: The <s>Mānavas</s> say that those caught with stolen goods should be banished immediately;

children.text: gautamānām aniṣṭaṃ yat prāṇyucchedād vigarhitam ||
children.translated_text: for the <s>Gautamas</s> this is not approved, since the killing of living beings is condemned.

children.text: sahoḍham asahoḍhaṃ vā tattvāgamitasāhasam
children.translated_text: Whether one is caught with the stolen goods or not, if the violent offense has been established by fact,

children.text: pragṛhyācchinnam āvedya sarvasvair viprayojayet ||
children.translated_text: one should arrest him, report him unmutilated, and deprive him of all his property.

children.text: ayaḥsaṃdānaguptās tu mandabhaktā balānvitāḥ
children.translated_text: But those who are confined in iron fetters, kept on scanty food, and possessed of strength

children.text: kuryuḥ karmāṇi nṛpater ā mṛtyor iti kauśikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should perform the king's work until death, says <s>Kauśika</s>.

children.text: paradeśāddhṛtaṃ dravyaṃ vaideśyena yadā bhavet
children.translated_text: When property has been taken from a foreign country by a foreigner,

children.text: gṛhītvā tasya taddravyam adaṇḍaṃ taṃ visarjayet ||
children.translated_text: one should take that property from him and release him without a fine.

children.text: corāṇāṃ bhaktadā ye syus tathāgnyudakadāyakāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who give food to thieves, and likewise those who give them fire and water,

children.text: kretāraś caiva bhāṇḍānāṃ pratigrāhiṇa eva ca
children.translated_text: as well as buyers of their goods and those who receive them,

children.text: samadaṇḍāḥ smṛtā hy ete ye ca pracchādayanti tān ||
children.translated_text: and those who conceal them, are remembered as liable to the same punishment.

children.text: avidvān yājako vā syāt pravaktā cānavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: If a sacrificial priest is ignorant, or an expounder is unstable,

children.text: tau ubhau coradaṇḍena vinīya sthāpayet pathi ||
children.translated_text: both of them should be disciplined with the punishment for thieves and set on the right path.

children.text: dūtopacārayuktaś ced avelāsthānasaṃsthitiḥ
children.translated_text: If there is use of messengers and attentions, or staying at improper times and places,

children.text: kaṇṭhakeśāṇcalagrāhaḥ karṇanāsākarādiṣu
children.translated_text: or grasping the throat, hair, or hem of the garment, or touching the ears, nose, hands, and the like,

children.text: ekasthānāsanāhārāḥ saṃgraho navadhā smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or sharing one place, seat, or meal, illicit association is remembered as ninefold.

children.text: strīṣu vṛttopabhogaḥ syāt prasahya puruṣo yadā
children.translated_text: When a man forcibly has actual sexual enjoyment among women,

children.text: vadhe tatra pravarteta kāryātikramaṇaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: execution should proceed in that case, for that is an overstepping of proper conduct.

children.text: kāmārtā svairiṇī yā tu svayam eva prakāmayet
children.translated_text: But a wanton woman, tormented by desire, who herself solicits,

children.text: rājādeśena moktavyā vikhyāpya janasaṃnidhau ||
children.translated_text: should be released by the king's order after public proclamation in the presence of the people.

children.text: ārambhakṛtsahāyaś ca tathā mārgānudeśakaḥ
children.translated_text: The initiator of the act, the helper, and likewise the one who points out the road,

children.text: āśrayaḥ śastradātā ca bhaktadātā vikarmiṇām ||
children.translated_text: the shelterer, the giver of weapons, and the giver of food to wrongdoers,

children.text: yuddhopadeśakaś caiva tadvināśapradarśakaḥ
children.translated_text: the instructor in fighting, the one who shows how to destroy them,

children.text: upekṣākāryayuktaś ca doṣavaktranumokakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the one whose duty is neglected, and the speaker of faults and approver of them,

children.text: aniṣeddhākṣamo yaḥ syāt sarve tatkāryakāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: and one who, though able, does not prevent it: all these are doers of that deed.

children.text: yathāśaktyanurūpaṃ tu daṇḍam eṣāṃ prakalpayet ||
children.translated_text: Punishment should be prescribed for them in accordance with each one's capacity.

children.text: patyā cāpy aviyoginyā śuśrūṣyo 'gnir vinītayā
children.translated_text: By a woman not separated from her husband, obedient and disciplined, the sacred fire too is to be tended,

children.text: saubhāgyavadavaidhavyakāmyayā bhartṛbhaktayā ||
children.translated_text: by one devoted to her husband and desiring good fortune and freedom from widowhood.

children.text: matiśuśrūṣayaiva strī sarvān kāmān samaśnute
children.translated_text: By devotion in thought and by service alone, a woman obtains all her desires.

children.text: divaḥ punar ihāyātā sukhānāṃ śevadhir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Having returned here again from heaven, she becomes a storehouse of happiness.

children.text: mṛte bhartari yā sādhvī brahmacarye vyavasthitā
children.translated_text: When her husband has died, a virtuous woman who remains established in celibate discipline,

children.text: sārundhatīsamācārā brahmaloke mahīyate ||
children.translated_text: conducting herself like <s>Arundhatī</s>, is honored in <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: sakalaṃ dravyajātaṃ yad bhāgair gṛhṇanti tat samaiḥ
children.translated_text: When fathers and brothers take every kind of property in equal shares,

children.text: pitaro bhrātaraś caiva vibhāgo dharmya ucyate ||
children.translated_text: that is called a lawful division.

children.text: paitāmahaṃ samānaṃ syāt pituḥ putrasya cobhayoḥ
children.translated_text: Ancestral property from the grandfather is common alike to father and son.

children.text: svayaṃ copārjite pitrā na putraḥ svāmyam arhati ||
children.translated_text: But in property acquired by the father himself, the son does not deserve ownership.

children.text: paitāmahaṃ ca pitryaṃ ca yac cānyat svayam arjitam
children.translated_text: Ancestral property, paternal property, and whatever else has been acquired by oneself,

children.text: dāyādānāṃ vibhāge tu sarvam etad vibhajyate ||
children.translated_text: all this is divided when there is a partition among heirs.

children.text: dṛśyamānaṃ vibhajyeta gṛhaṃ kṣetraṃ catuṣpadam
children.translated_text: What is visible should be divided: a house, a field, and four-footed animals.

children.text: gūḍhadravyābhiśaṅkāyāṃ pratyayas tatra kīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When there is suspicion of hidden property, proof is prescribed in that case.

children.text: gṛhopaskaravāhyāś ca dohyābharaṇakarmiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Household equipment, draft animals, milch animals, ornaments, and workers,

children.text: dṛśyamānā vibhajyante kośaṃ gūḍhe 'bravīd bhṛguḥ ||
children.translated_text: when visible, are divided; <s>Bhṛgu</s> spoke of the treasury in the case of hidden property.

children.text: jīvadvibhāge tu pitā naikaṃ putraṃ viśeṣayet
children.translated_text: In a division made while he is alive, the father should not favor one son,

children.text: nirbhājayen na caivaikam akasmāt kāraṇaṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: nor should he exclude one son without cause and without a reason.

children.text: samprāptavyavahārāṇāṃ vibhāgaś ca vidhīyate
children.translated_text: Division is prescribed for those who have attained legal capacity.

children.text: puṃsāṃ ca ṣoḍaśe varṣe jāyate vyavahāritā ||
children.translated_text: For males, legal capacity arises in the sixteenth year.

children.text: aprāptavyavahārāṇāṃ ca dhanaṃ vyayavivarjitam
children.translated_text: The wealth of those who have not attained legal capacity, free from expenditure,

children.text: nyaseyur bandhumitreṣu proṣitānāṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: should be deposited among relatives and friends, and likewise that of those who are abroad.

children.text: proṣitasya tu yo bhāgo rakṣeyuḥ sarva eva tam
children.translated_text: All of them should protect the share of a man who is abroad.

children.text: bālaputre mṛte rikthaṃ rakṣyaṃ tat tantubandhubhiḥ
children.translated_text: When a man dies leaving a child-son, that <s>riktha</s> (inheritance) should be guarded by his lineage-kinsmen.

children.text: paugaṇḍāḥ paratas taṃ tu vibhajeran yathāṃśataḥ ||
children.translated_text: When they have reached boyhood, they should then divide it according to the proper shares.

children.text: bhrātrā pitṛvyamātṛbhyāṃ kuṭumbārtham ṛṇaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: A debt incurred by a brother, paternal uncle, or mother for the sake of the household

children.text: vibhāgakāle deyaṃ tadrikthibhiḥ sarvam eva tu ||
children.translated_text: must all be paid by the heirs at the time of partition.

children.text: tad ṛṇaṃ dhanine deyaṃ nānyathaiva pradāpayet
children.translated_text: That debt is to be paid to the creditor; he should not make it be paid in any other way

children.text: bhāvitaṃ cet pramāṇena virodhāt parato yadā ||
children.translated_text: when, after a dispute, it has been established by evidence.

children.text: dharmārthaṃ prītidattaṃ ca yad ṛṇaṃ syān niyojitam
children.translated_text: A debt that has been assigned for a religious purpose, or what was given out of affection,

children.text: tad dṛśyamānaṃ vibhajen na dānaṃ paitṛkād dhanāt ||
children.translated_text: should be apportioned when it is evident; but a gift should not be made from paternal wealth.

children.text: pitryaṃ pitryarṇasaṃśuddham ātmīyaṃ cātmanā kṛtam
children.translated_text: Paternal wealth that has been cleared of paternal debt, and personal wealth produced by oneself,

children.text: ṛṇam evaṃvidhaṃ śodhyaṃ vibhāge bandhubhiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: and debt of this kind should be cleared at partition together with the kinsmen.

children.text: ṛṇaṃ prītipradānaṃ ca dattvā śeṣaṃ vibhājayet ||
children.translated_text: After paying the debt and the affectionate gift, one should divide the remainder.

children.text: dvyaṃśaharo 'rdhaharo vā putravittārjanāt pitā
children.translated_text: A father takes two shares, or half, from wealth acquired by a son;

children.text: mātāpi pitari prete putratulyāṃśabhāginī ||
children.translated_text: and when the father is dead, the mother too receives a share equal to a son's.

children.text: yathā yathā vibhāgāptaṃ dhanaṃ yāgārthatām iyāt
children.translated_text: In whatever way wealth obtained by partition comes to be used for sacrifice,

children.text: tathā tathā vidhātavyaṃ vidvadbhir bhāgagauravam ||
children.translated_text: in that same way learned men should determine the weight of the shares.

children.text: loke rikthavibhāge 'pi na kaścit prabhutām iyāt
children.translated_text: Even in the worldly division of inheritance, no one should gain absolute ownership;

children.text: bhoga eva tu kartavyo na dānaṃ na ca vikrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: only enjoyment of use is to be made, not gift and not sale.

children.text: vibhaktā avibhaktā vā dāyādāḥ sthāvare samāḥ
children.translated_text: Whether divided or undivided, heirs are equal with regard to immovable property;

children.text: eko hy anīśaḥ sarvatra dānādhamanavikraye ||
children.translated_text: one person alone has no authority anywhere to give, mortgage, or sell it.

children.text: avibhakte 'nuje prete tatsutaṃ rikthabhāginam
children.translated_text: When an undivided younger brother has died, one should make his son a sharer in the inheritance,

children.text: kurvīta jīvanaṃ yena labdhaṃ naiva pitāmahāt ||
children.translated_text: so that he may have a livelihood, even if it was not obtained from the grandfather.

children.text: labhetāṃśaṃ sa pitryaṃ tu pitṛvyāt tasya vā sutāt
children.translated_text: He should receive his paternal share from his paternal uncle or from that uncle's son;

children.text: sa evāṃśas tu sarveṣāṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ nyāyato bhavet
children.translated_text: for that very share should legally belong to all the brothers.

children.text: labheta tat suto vāpi nivṛttiḥ parato bhavet ||
children.translated_text: His son too may receive it; beyond that succession should cease.

children.text: utpanne caurase putre caturthāṃśaharāḥ sutāḥ
children.translated_text: When an <s>aurasa</s> son has been born, the other sons take a fourth share;

children.text: savarṇā asavarṇās tu grāsācchādanabhājanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those of the same class do so, but those of a different class are entitled to food and clothing.

children.text: kanyakānāṃ tv adattānāṃ caturtho bhāga iṣyate
children.translated_text: For unmarried daughters, however, a fourth share is prescribed;

children.text: putrāṇāṃ tu trayo bhāgāḥ sāmyaṃ tv alpadhane smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: for sons there are three shares, but equality is remembered where the wealth is small.

children.text: kṣetrikasya matenāpi phalam utpādayet tu yaḥ
children.translated_text: Even with the consent of the field-owner, the man who causes fruit to be produced

children.text: tasyeha bhāginau tau tu na phalaṃ hi vinaikataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he are both sharers here, for the fruit does not exist without either one.

children.text: klībaṃ vihāya patitaṃ yā punar labhate patim
children.translated_text: A woman who, leaving an impotent or fallen man, obtains another husband

children.text: tasyāṃ paunarbhavo jāto vyaktam utpādakasya saḥ ||
children.translated_text: bears a <s>paunarbhava</s> son; he clearly belongs to the begetter.

children.text: na mūtraṃ phenilaṃ yasya viṣṭhā cāpsu nimajjati
children.translated_text: He whose urine is not foamy and whose feces sinks in water,

children.text: meḍhraś conmādaśukrābhyāṃ hīnaḥ klībaḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and whose penis is devoid of arousal and semen, is called a <s>klība</s> (impotent man).

children.text: akramoḍhāsutaś caiva sagotrādyas tu jāyate
children.translated_text: A son of a woman married out of order, and one born from a same-<s>gotra</s> union and the like,

children.text: pravrajyāvasitaś caiva na rikthaṃ teṣu cārhati ||
children.translated_text: and one who has returned from renunciation: among these, none is entitled to inheritance.

children.text: akramoḍhāsutas tv ṛkthī savarṇaś ca yadā pituḥ
children.translated_text: But the son of a woman married out of order is an heir when he is of the same class as his father,

children.text: asavarṇaprasūtaś ca kramoḍhāyāṃ ca yo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and so is one born from a different-class woman if she was married in due order.

children.text: pratilomaprasūtā yā tasyāḥ putro na rikthabhāk
children.translated_text: But the son of a woman born from a reverse-caste union is not a sharer in the inheritance;

children.text: grāsācchādanam atyantaṃ deyaṃ tadbandhubhir matam ||
children.translated_text: his relatives are held bound to give him food and clothing permanently.

children.text: bandhūnām apy abhāve tu pitṛdravyaṃ tad āpnuyāt
children.translated_text: If even relatives are absent, however, he may obtain his father's property;

children.text: apitryaṃ draviṇaṃ prāptaṃ dāpanīyā na bāndhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: but relatives are not to be compelled to hand over wealth not derived from the father.

children.text: svaśaktyapahṛtaṃ naṣṭaṃ svayam āptaṃ ca yad bhavet
children.translated_text: What has been recovered by one's own power after being taken or lost, and what one has acquired by oneself,

children.text: etat sarvaṃ pitā putrair vibhāge naiva dāpyate ||
children.translated_text: all this a father is not to be made to hand over to his sons at partition.

children.text: parabhaktopayogena vidyā prāptān yatas tu yā
children.translated_text: Knowledge that has been acquired by using another's food or support

children.text: tayā prāptaṃ dhanaṃ yat tu vidyāprāptaṃ tad ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and whatever wealth is obtained through it: that is called wealth acquired by learning.

children.text: upanyaste tu yal labdhaṃ vidyayā paṇapūrvakam
children.translated_text: What is obtained through learning, after a stake has first been set down,

children.text: vidyādhanaṃ tu tad vidyād vibhāge na vibhajyate ||
children.translated_text: should be known as <s>vidyādhana</s> (learning-wealth); it is not divided at partition.

children.text: śiṣyād ārtvijyataḥ praśnāt saṃdigdhapraśnanirṇayāt
children.translated_text: What is gained from a pupil, from priestly officiating, from answering questions, from settling doubtful questions,

children.text: svajñānaśaṃsanād vādāl labdhaṃ prādhyayanāc ca yat
children.translated_text: from proclaiming one's own knowledge, from debate, and from teaching,

children.text: vidyādhanaṃ tu tat prāhur vibhāge na vibhajyate ||
children.translated_text: that they call <s>vidyādhana</s>; it is not divided at partition.

children.text: śilpiṣv api hi dharmo 'yaṃ mūlyād yac cādhikaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Among artisans too this is the same rule: whatever exceeds the basic price or wage

children.text: paraṃ nirasya yal labdhaṃ vidyāto dyūtapūrvakam
children.translated_text: and what is won by casting down another through skill, after a wager,

children.text: vidyādhanaṃ tu tad vidyān na vibhājyaṃ bṛhaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> says one should know that as <s>vidyādhana</s>, not divisible property.

children.text: vidyāpratijñayā labdhaṃ śiṣyād āptaṃ ca yad bhavet
children.translated_text: What is obtained by a pledge of learning, and what is received from a pupil,

children.text: ṛtviṅnyāyena yal labdham etad vidyādhanaṃ bhṛguḥ ||
children.translated_text: and what is obtained in the manner of a ritual priest: <s>Bhṛgu</s> calls this <s>vidyādhana</s>.

children.text: vidyābalakṛtaṃ caiva yājyataḥ śiṣyatas tathā
children.translated_text: What is produced by the power of learning, and likewise from a sacrificer or from a pupil,

children.text: etad vidyādhanaṃ prāhuḥ sāmānyaṃ yad ato 'nyathā ||
children.translated_text: they call this <s>vidyādhana</s>; whatever is otherwise than this is common property.

children.text: kule vinītavidyānāṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ pitṛto 'pi vā
children.translated_text: In a family of brothers trained in learning, whether by the family or by the father,

children.text: śauryaprāptaṃ tu yad vittaṃ vibhājyaṃ tad bṛhaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> says that wealth obtained by valor is divisible.

children.text: nāvidyānāṃ tu vaidyena deyaṃ vidyādhanāt kvacit
children.translated_text: A learned man should never give any part of <s>vidyādhana</s> to those without learning;

children.text: samavidyādhikānāṃ tu deyaṃ vaidyena tad dhanam ||
children.translated_text: that wealth should be given by the learned man to those with equal or superior learning.

children.text: āruhya saṃśayaṃ yatra prasabhaṃ karma kurvate
children.translated_text: Where men take on danger and forcibly perform a deed,

children.text: tasmin karmaṇi tuṣṭena prasādaḥ svāminā kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: and, pleased with that deed, the master grants a favor,

children.text: tatra labdhaṃ tu yat kiṃcit dhanaṃ śauryeṇa tad bhavet ||
children.translated_text: whatever wealth is obtained there is wealth obtained by valor.

children.text: śauryaprāptaṃ vidyayā ca strīdhanaṃ caiva yat smṛtam
children.translated_text: What is remembered as obtained by valor, obtained by learning, and also as <s>strīdhana</s> (woman's property),

children.text: etat sarvaṃ vibhāge tu vibhājyaṃ naiva rikthibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: all this is not to be divided by the heirs at partition.

children.text: dhvajāhṛtaṃ bhaved yat tu vibhājyaṃ naiva tat smṛtam
children.translated_text: What is <s>dhvajāhṛta</s> (taken under the banner) is likewise remembered as not divisible;

children.text: saṃgrāmād āhṛtaṃ yat tu vidrāvya dviṣatāṃ balam
children.translated_text: what is brought from battle after routing the enemy's army,

children.text: svāmyarthe jīvitaṃ tyaktvā tad dhvajāhṛtam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: after risking one's life for the master's sake, is called <s>dhvajāhṛta</s>.

children.text: yal labdhaṃ dānakāle tu svajātyā kanyayā saha
children.translated_text: What is received at the time of the gift, together with a maiden of one's own class,

children.text: kanyāgataṃ tu tad vittaṃ śuddhaṃ vṛddhikaraṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: that wealth brought with the bride is remembered as pure and productive of increase.

children.text: vaivāhikaṃ tu tad vidyād bhāryayā yat sahāgatam
children.translated_text: One should know as marriage-property what came together with the wife,

children.text: dhanam evaṃvidhaṃ sarvaṃ vijñeyaṃ dharmasādhakam ||
children.translated_text: and all property of this sort is to be understood as serving <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: vivāhakāle yat kiṃcid varāyoddiśya dīyate
children.translated_text: Whatever is given at the time of marriage with reference to the bridegroom,

children.text: kanyāyās tad dhanaṃ sarvam avibhājyaṃ ca bandhubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: all that is the girl's property, and is not to be divided by her relatives.

children.text: dhanaṃ patraniviṣṭaṃ tu dharmārthaṃ ca nirūpitam
children.translated_text: Property entered in a document and assigned for the sake of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: udakaṃ caiva dāsaś ca nibandho yaḥ kramāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also water, a slave, and an endowment that has come down in succession,

children.text: dhṛtaṃ vastram alaṃkāro nānurūpaṃ tu yad bhavet
children.translated_text: a retained garment or ornament, but whatever would be unsuitable,

children.text: yathā kālopayogyāni tathā yojyāni bandhubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be arranged by the relatives according as it is useful at the proper time.

children.text: gopracāraś ca rakṣā ca vastraṃ yac cāṅgayojitam
children.translated_text: Pasture for cattle, protection, and clothing fitted to the body,

children.text: prayojyaṃ na vibhajyeta dharmārthaṃ ca bṛhaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: being intended for use, should not be divided; and what is for <s>dharma</s> also, says <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: deśasya jāteḥ saṅghasya dharmo grāmasya yo bhṛguḥ
children.translated_text: The law of a country, caste, corporation, or village, says <s>Bhṛgu</s>,

children.text: uditaḥ syāt sa tenaiva dāyabhāgaṃ prakalpayet ||
children.translated_text: when it has been declared, one should determine the division of inheritance by that very rule.

children.text: pracchāditaṃ yadi dhanaṃ punar āsādya tat samam
children.translated_text: If concealed property is later recovered, then equally

children.text: bhajeran bhrātṛbhiḥ sārdham abhāve hi pituḥ sutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sons should divide it along with their brothers, if the father is absent.

children.text: anyonyāpahṛtaṃ dravyaṃ durvibhaktaṃ ca yad bhavet
children.translated_text: Property taken away from one another, or what has been badly divided,

children.text: paścāt prāptaṃ vibhajyeta samabhāgena tad bhṛguḥ ||
children.translated_text: when obtained afterward, should be divided in equal shares; so says <s>Bhṛgu</s>.

children.text: vibhaktenaiva yat prāptaṃ dhanaṃ tasyaiva tad bhavet
children.translated_text: Property acquired by one who has already been separated belongs to that very man.

children.text: hṛtaṃ naṣṭaṃ ca yal labdhaṃ prāg uktaṃ ca punar bhajet ||
children.translated_text: But what was carried off, lost, and then found, as stated before, he should divide again.

children.text: bandhunāpahṛtaṃ dravyaṃ balān naiva pradāpayet
children.translated_text: Property taken away by a relative should not be forcibly made to be handed over.

children.text: bandhūnām avibhaktānāṃ bhogaṃ naiva pradāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Nor should one compel enjoyment from undivided relatives.

children.text: kṣetraṃ sādhāraṇaṃ tyaktvā yo 'nyadeśaṃ samāśritaḥ
children.translated_text: If a man has abandoned a common field and resorted to another country,

children.text: tadvaṃśyasyāgatasyāṃśaḥ pradātavyo na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the share of his descendant, when he arrives, must be given; there is no doubt.

children.text: tṛtīyaḥ pañcamo vāpi saptamaś cāpi yo bhavet
children.translated_text: Whether he is third, fifth, or even seventh

children.text: janmanām aparijñāne labhetāṃśaṃ kramāgatam ||
children.translated_text: in generations, when the births are not known, he should obtain the share that has come down in succession.

children.text: yaṃ paraṃparayā maulāḥ sāmantāḥ svāminaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: Whom the ancestral local men and neighbors know by tradition as lord,

children.text: tadanvayasyāgatasya dātavyā gotajair mahī ||
children.translated_text: to the descendant of that line, when he has come, the land must be given by the members of the clan.

children.text: vibhaktāḥ pitṛvittāc ced akatra prativāsinaḥ
children.translated_text: If men separated from their father's wealth live together in one place,

children.text: vibhajeyuḥ punar dvyaṃśaṃ sa labhetodayo yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and they divide again, he should receive a double share from which there is increase.

children.text: vaseyur daśa varṣāṇi pṛthagdharmāḥ pṛthakkriyāḥ
children.translated_text: If brothers live for ten years with separate duties and separate rites,

children.text: bhrātaras te 'pi vijñeyā vibhaktāḥ paitṛkād dhanāt ||
children.translated_text: they too should be known as separated from the paternal property.

children.text: adhyagnyadhyāvāhanikaṃ dattaṃ ca prītitaḥ striyaiḥ
children.translated_text: What is given to a woman before the nuptial fire, what is given at the bridal procession, what is given out of affection,

children.text: bhrātṛmātṛpitṛprāptaṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ strīdhanaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and what is received from brother, mother, or father: these are remembered as the six kinds of <s>strīdhana</s>.

children.text: vivāhakāle yat strībhyo dīyate hy agnisaṃnidhau
children.translated_text: What is given to women at the time of marriage in the presence of fire,

children.text: tad adhyagnikṛtaṃ sadbhiḥ strīdhanaṃ parikīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: that is proclaimed by good people as <s>strīdhana</s> made before the nuptial fire.

children.text: yat punar labhate nārī nīyamānā pitur gṛhāt
children.translated_text: Again, what a woman receives while being led from her father's house,

children.text: adhyāvāhanikaṃ caiva strīdhanaṃ tad udāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: that too is called bridal-procession property and is declared to be <s>strīdhana</s>.

children.text: prītyā dattaṃ tu yat kiṃcit śvaśrvā vā śvaśureṇa vā
children.translated_text: Whatever is given out of affection by the mother-in-law or by the father-in-law,

children.text: pādavandanikaṃ caiva prītidattaṃ tad ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and also a gift for bowing at the feet, that is called a gift of affection.

children.text: gṛhopaskaravāhyānāṃ dohyābharaṇakarmiṇām
children.translated_text: Whatever value is obtained for household utensils, conveyances, milch animals, ornaments, and servants,

children.text: mūlyaṃ labdhaṃ tu yat kiṃcicchulkaṃ tat parikīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: that is proclaimed as <s>śulka</s> (bride-price).

children.text: vivāhāt parato yat tu labdhaṃ bhartṛkulāt striyā
children.translated_text: But what is received by a woman from her husband's family after marriage,

children.text: anvādheyaṃ tad uktaṃ tu labdhaṃ bandhukulāt tathā ||
children.translated_text: that is said to be <s>anvādheya</s>; likewise what is received from her relatives' family.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ labdhaṃ tu yat kiṃcit saṃskārāt prītitaḥ striyā
children.translated_text: Whatever is received afterward by a woman, out of affection, after the sacrament,

children.text: bhartuḥ pitroḥ sakāśād vā anvādheyaṃ tu tad bhṛguḥ ||
children.translated_text: from her husband or from her parents, that is <s>anvādheya</s>, says <s>Bhṛgu</s>.

children.text: ūḍhayā kanyayā vāpi bhartuḥ pitṛgṛhe 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Whether by a married woman or by a maiden, even in the house of her husband's father,

children.text: bhrātuḥ sakāśāt pitror vā labdhaṃ saudāyikaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: what is received from her brother or from her parents is remembered as <s>saudāyika</s>.

children.text: pitṛmātṛpatibhrātṛjñātibhiḥ strīdhanaṃ striyai
children.translated_text: <s>Strīdhana</s> should be given to a woman by father, mother, husband, brother, and kinsmen,

children.text: yathāśaktyā dvisāhasrād dātavyaṃ sthāvarād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: according to their ability, up to two thousand, except from immovable property.

children.text: yat tu sopādhikaṃ dattaṃ yac ca yogavaśena vā
children.translated_text: But what is given with a condition, or what is given under the force of a connection,

children.text: pitrā bhrātrātha vā patyā na tat strīdhanam iṣyate ||
children.translated_text: by her father, brother, or husband, is not regarded as <s>strīdhana</s>.

children.text: prāptaṃ śilpais tu yad vittaṃ prītyā caiva yad anyataḥ
children.translated_text: Property that is obtained through crafts, and what else is received out of affection,

children.text: bhartuḥ svāmyaṃ tadā tatra śeṣaṃ tu strīdhanaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: over that the husband then has ownership; the rest is remembered as <s>strīdhana</s>.

children.text: saudāyikaṃ dhanaṃ prāpya strīṇāṃ svātantryam iṣyate
children.translated_text: When <s>saudāyika</s> property has been obtained, independence is accepted for women,

children.text: yasmāt tadānṛśasyārthaṃ tair dattam upajīvanam ||
children.translated_text: because it was given by them as a means of livelihood for the sake of compassion.

children.text: saudāyike sadā strīṇāṃ svātantryaṃ parikīrtitam
children.translated_text: In regard to <s>saudāyika</s>, women's independence is always proclaimed,

children.text: vikraye caiva dāne ca yatheṣṭaṃ sthāvareṣv api ||
children.translated_text: in sale and in gift, as they wish, even in the case of immovable property.

children.text: bhartṛdāyaṃ mṛte patyau vinyaset strī yatheṣṭataḥ
children.translated_text: After her husband has died, a woman may dispose of her husband's inheritance as she wishes.

children.text: vidyamāne tu saṃrakṣet kṣapayet tat kule 'nyathā ||
children.translated_text: But while he is alive she should preserve it; otherwise she would waste it in the family.

children.text: atha cet sa dvibhāryaḥ syān na ca tāṃ bhajate punaḥ
children.translated_text: Now if he has two wives and does not share with her again,

children.text: prītyā nisṛṣṭam api cet pratidāpyaḥ sa tadbalāt ||
children.translated_text: even if it was released out of affection, he must be compelled to give it back by force.

children.text: grāsācchādanavāsānām ācchedo yatra yoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Where there is deprivation of a woman's food, clothing, and residence,

children.text: tatra svam ādadīta strī vibhāgaṃ rikthināṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: there the woman may take her own property, and likewise a share among the heirs.

children.text: likhitasyeti dharmo 'yaṃ prāpte bhartṛkule vaset
children.translated_text: This is the rule concerning what is written: when she has reached the husband's family she should dwell there.

children.text: vyādhitā pretakāle tu gacched bandhujanaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when sick, or at the time of death, she may then go to her relatives.

children.text: na bhartā naiva ca suto na pitā bhrātaro na ca
children.translated_text: Neither husband, nor son, nor father, nor brothers

children.text: ādāne vā visarge vā strīdhane prabhaviṣṇavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: have authority over taking or giving away a woman's <s>strīdhana</s>.

children.text: yadi hy ekataro 'py eṣāṃ strīdhanaṃ bhakṣayed balāt
children.translated_text: For if even one of these should consume a woman's <s>strīdhana</s> by force,

children.text: savṛddhikaṃ pradāpyaḥ syād daṇḍaṃ caiva samāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: he must be made to repay it with interest and should also incur a fine.

children.text: tad eva yady anujñāpya bhakṣayet prītipūrvakam
children.translated_text: But if, having obtained her permission, he consumes that very property out of affection,

children.text: mūlyam eva pradāpyaḥ syād yady asau dhanavān bhavet ||
children.translated_text: he should be made to repay only its value, if he is a man of means.

children.text: vyādhitaṃ vyasanasthaṃ ca dhanikair vopapīḍitam
children.translated_text: One who is sick, in distress, or oppressed by creditors,

children.text: jñātvā nisṛṣṭaṃ yat prītyā dadyād ātmecchayā tu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever he gives out of affection, by his own wish, knowing it to have been relinquished.

children.text: jīvantyāḥ patiputrās tu devarāḥ pitṛbāndhavāḥ
children.translated_text: While a woman is alive, her husband, sons, brothers-in-law, and paternal kinsmen

children.text: anīśāḥ strīdhanasyoktā daṇḍyās tv apaharanti ye ||
children.translated_text: are said to have no ownership over her <s>strīdhana</s> (woman's property); those who seize it are punishable.

children.text: bhartrā pratiśrutaṃ deyam ṛṇavat strīdhanaṃ sutaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>strīdhana</s> promised by the husband must be paid by the sons, like a debt.

children.text: tiṣṭhed bhartṛkule yā tu na sā pitṛkule vaset ||
children.translated_text: But a woman who remains in her husband's family should not live in her father's family.

children.text: bhaginyo bāndhavaiḥ sārdhaṃ vibhajeran sabhartṛkāḥ
children.translated_text: Sisters, together with their kinsmen and with their husbands living, should divide it.

children.text: strīdhanasyeti dharmo 'yaṃ vibhāgas tu prakalpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This rule concerning <s>strīdhana</s> has been stated; the division is thus prescribed.

children.text: duhitṝṇām abhāve tu rikthaṃ putreṣu tad bhavet
children.translated_text: In the absence of daughters, that inheritance should pass to the sons.

children.text: bandhudattaṃ tu bandhūnām abhāve bhrtṛgāmi tat ||
children.translated_text: What was given by kinsmen belongs to the kinsmen; in their absence it goes to the husband.

children.text: pitṛbhyāṃ caiva yad dattaṃ duhituḥ sthāvaraṃ dhanam
children.translated_text: And whatever immovable property has been given to a daughter by her parents,

children.text: aprajāyām atātāyāṃ bhrātṛgāmi tu sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: if she dies childless, it always goes to her brothers.

children.text: āsurādiṣu yal labdhaṃ strīdhanaṃ paitṛkaṃ striyā
children.translated_text: The ancestral <s>strīdhana</s> that a woman receives in an <s>Āsura</s> or similar marriage

children.text: abhāve tadapatyānāṃ mātāpitros tad iṣyate ||
children.translated_text: is held, in the absence of her offspring, to belong to her mother and father.

children.text: aputrā śayanaṃ bhartuḥ pālayantī gurau sthitā
children.translated_text: A childless woman who guards her husband's bed and remains under her elders,

children.text: bhuñjīta ā maraṇāt kṣāntā dāyādā ūrdhvam āpnuyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: being patient, may enjoy it until death; afterwards the heirs should receive it.

children.text: svaryāte svāmini strī tu grāsācchādanabhāginī
children.translated_text: When her lord has gone to heaven, a woman is entitled to food and clothing;

children.text: avibhakte dhanāṃśe tu prāpnoty āmaraṇāntikam ||
children.translated_text: but when the property-share is undivided, she obtains it until the end of her life.

children.text: bhoktum arhati kﾱptāṃśaṃ guruśuśrūṣaṇe ratā
children.translated_text: A woman devoted to serving her elders deserves to enjoy the allotted share.

children.text: na kuryād yadi śuśrūṣāṃ cailapiṇḍe niyojayet ||
children.translated_text: If she does not perform service, one should assign her only clothing and food.

children.text: mṛte bhartari bhartṛaṃśaṃ labheta kulapālikā
children.translated_text: When her husband has died, a woman who preserves the family should receive her husband's share;

children.text: yāvajjīvaṃ na hi svāmyaṃ dānādhamanavikraye ||
children.translated_text: but for life only; she has no ownership for gift, pledge, or sale.

children.text: vratopavāsaniratā brahmacarye vyavasthitā
children.translated_text: Devoted to vows and fasts, established in celibate discipline,

children.text: damadānaratā nityam aputrāpi divaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: always intent on self-control and giving, even a childless woman goes to heaven.

children.text: patnī bhartur dhanaharī yā syād avyabhicāriṇī
children.translated_text: The wife who is free from unfaithfulness is the taker of her husband's wealth;

children.text: tadabhāve tu duhitā yady anūḍhā bhavet tadā ||
children.translated_text: in her absence, the daughter takes it, if she is then unmarried.

children.text: aputrasyātha kulajā patnī duhitaro 'pi vā
children.translated_text: For a sonless man, the wife born in a good family, or the daughters, are heirs;

children.text: tadabhāve pitā mātā bhrātā putrāś ca kīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: in their absence, the father, mother, brother, and brother's sons are named.

children.text: vibhakte saṃsthite dravyaṃ putrābhāve pitā haret
children.translated_text: When a divided man has died, in the absence of sons the father takes the property;

children.text: bhrātā vā jananī vātha mātā vā tat pituḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: after the father, the brother or the mother takes it in order.

children.text: apacārakriyyayuktā nirlajjā vārthanāśikā ||
children.translated_text: A woman engaged in misconduct, shameless, or destructive of wealth,

children.text: vyabhicāraratā yā ca strī dhanaṃ sā na cārhati ||
children.translated_text: and one addicted to adultery, is not entitled to property.

children.text: nārī khalv ananujñātā pitrā bhartrā sutena vā
children.translated_text: Indeed, a woman acting without permission from her father, husband, or son

children.text: viphalaṃ tad bhavet tasyā yat karoty aurdhvadehikam ||
children.translated_text: has no fruit from whatever rite for the hereafter she performs.

children.text: adāyikaṃ rājagāmi yoṣidbhṛtyordhvadehikam
children.translated_text: Property without an heir goes to the king, as does the post-mortem property of a woman or servant;

children.text: apāsya śrotriyadravyaṃ śrotriyebhyas tad arpayet ||
children.translated_text: excepting the property of a <s>Śrotriya</s>, he should hand that over to <s>Śrotriyas</s>.

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭānāṃ tu saṃsṛṣṭāḥ pṛthaksthānāṃ pṛthaksthitāḥ
children.translated_text: For reunited co-heirs, the reunited relatives; for those living separately, the separately situated relatives

children.text: abhāve 'rthaharā jñeyā nirbījānyonyabhāginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be known as takers of the wealth in default of heirs; where there is no issue, they share one another's property.
